<h1 id="vapi-api">Vapi API v1.0</h1>

> Scroll down for code samples, example requests and responses. Select a language for code samples from the tabs above or the mobile navigation menu.

Voice AI for developers.

Base URLs:

* <a href="https://api.vapi.ai">https://api.vapi.ai</a>

# Authentication

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: bearer Retrieve your API Key from [Dashboard](dashboard.vapi.ai).

<h1 id="vapi-api-assistants">Assistants</h1>

## List Assistants

<a id="opIdAssistantController_findAll"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vapi.ai/assistant \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /assistant`

<h3 id="list-assistants-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|number|false|This is the maximum number of items to return. Defaults to 100.|
|createdAtGt|query|string(date-time)|false|This will return items where the createdAt is greater than the specified value.|
|createdAtLt|query|string(date-time)|false|This will return items where the createdAt is less than the specified value.|
|createdAtGe|query|string(date-time)|false|This will return items where the createdAt is greater than or equal to the specified value.|
|createdAtLe|query|string(date-time)|false|This will return items where the createdAt is less than or equal to the specified value.|
|updatedAtGt|query|string(date-time)|false|This will return items where the updatedAt is greater than the specified value.|
|updatedAtLt|query|string(date-time)|false|This will return items where the updatedAt is less than the specified value.|
|updatedAtGe|query|string(date-time)|false|This will return items where the updatedAt is greater than or equal to the specified value.|
|updatedAtLe|query|string(date-time)|false|This will return items where the updatedAt is less than or equal to the specified value.|

<h3 id="list-assistants-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[[Assistant](#schemaassistant)]|false|none|none|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearer

> 409 Response

```json
{
  "error": "assistant_pinned",
  "message": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="delete-assistant-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[Assistant](#schemaassistant)|
|409|Conflict|One of its versions is pinned (see AssistantPinnedConflictResponseDTO), or Vapi for CX manages the assistant (see AssistantManagedConflictResponseDTO).|Inline|

<h3 id="delete-assistant-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **409**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|[AssistantPinnedConflictResponseDTO](#schemaassistantpinnedconflictresponsedto)|false|none|none|
|*oneOf*|[AssistantManagedConflictResponseDTO](#schemaassistantmanagedconflictresponsedto)|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearer
</aside>

Defaults to 0.4.<br><br>This setting exists because the transcriber will sometimes punctuate the transcription ending with a number, even though the customer hasn't uttered the full number. This happens commonly for long numbers when the customer reads the number in chunks.<br><br>@default 0.5|
|» stopSpeakingPlan|body|object|false|This is the plan for when assistant should stop talking on customer interruption.<br><br>You should configure this if you're running into these issues:<br>- The assistant is too slow to recognize customer's interruption.<br>- The assistant is too fast to recognize customer's interruption.<br>- The assistant is getting interrupted by phrases that are just acknowledgments.<br>- The assistant is getting interrupted by background noises.<br>- The assistant is not properly stopping -- it starts talking right after getting interrupted.|
|» » numWords|body|number|false|This is the number of words that the customer has to say before the assistant will stop talking.<br><br>Words like "stop", "actually", "no", etc. will always interrupt immediately regardless of this value.<br><br>Words like "okay", "yeah", "right" will never interrupt.<br><br>When set to 0, `voiceSeconds` is used in addition to the transcriptions to determine the customer has started speaking.<br><br>Defaults to 0.<br><br>@default 0|
|» » voiceSeconds|body|number|false|This is the seconds customer has to speak before the assistant stops talking. This uses the VAD (Voice Activity Detection) spike to determine if the customer has started speaking.<br><br>Considerations:<br>- A lower value might be more responsive but could potentially pick up non-speech sounds.<br>- A higher value reduces false positives but might slightly delay the detection of speech onset.<br><br>This is only used if `numWords` is set to 0.<br><br>Defaults to 0.2<br><br>@default 0.2|
|» » backoffSeconds|body|number|false|This is the seconds to wait before the assistant will start talking again after being interrupted.<br><br>Defaults to 1.<br><br>@default 1|
|» » acknowledgementPhrases|body|[string]|false|These are the phrases that will never interrupt the assistant, even if numWords threshold is met.<br>These are typically acknowledgement or backchanneling phrases.|
|» » interruptionPhrases|body|[string]|false|These are the phrases that will always interrupt the assistant immediately, regardless of numWords.<br>These are typically phrases indicating disagreement or desire to stop.|
|» monitorPlan|body|object|false|This is the plan for real-time monitoring of the assistant's calls.<br><br>Usage:<br>- To enable live listening of the assistant's calls, set `monitorPlan.listenEnabled` to `true`.<br>- To enable live control of the assistant's calls, set `monitorPlan.controlEnabled` to `true`.<br>- To attach monitors to the assistant, set `monitorPlan.monitorIds` to the set of monitor ids.|
|» » listenEnabled|body|boolean|false|This determines whether the assistant's calls allow live listening. Defaults to true.<br><br>Fetch `call.monitor.listenUrl` to get the live listening URL.<br><br>@default true|
|» » listenAuthenticationEnabled|body|boolean|false|This enables authentication on the `call.monitor.listenUrl`.<br><br>If `listenAuthenticationEnabled` is `true`, the `call.monitor.listenUrl` will require an `Authorization: Bearer <vapi-public-api-key>` header.<br><br>@default false|
|» » controlEnabled|body|boolean|false|This determines whether the assistant's calls allow live control. Defaults to true.<br><br>Fetch `call.monitor.controlUrl` to get the live control URL.<br><br>To use, send any control message via a POST request to `call.monitor.controlUrl`. Here are the types of controls supported: https://docs.vapi.ai/api-reference/messages/client-inbound-message<br><br>@default true|
|» » controlAuthenticationEnabled|body|boolean|false|This enables authentication on the `call.monitor.controlUrl`.<br><br>If `controlAuthenticationEnabled` is `true`, the `call.monitor.controlUrl` will require an `Authorization: Bearer <vapi-public-api-key>` header.<br><br>@default false|
|» » monitorIds|body|[string]|false|This the set of monitor ids that are attached to the assistant.<br>The source of truth for the monitor ids is the assistant_monitor join table.<br>This field can be used for transient assistants and to update assistants with new monitor ids.<br><br>@default []|
|» credentialIds|body|[string]|false|These are the credentials that will be used for the assistant calls. By default, all the credentials are available for use in the call but you can provide a subset using this.|
|» server|body|object|false|This is where Vapi will send webhooks. You can find all webhooks available along with their shape in ServerMessage schema.<br><br>The order of precedence is:<br><br>1. assistant.server.url<br>2. phoneNumber.serverUrl<br>3. org.serverUrl|
|» » timeoutSeconds|body|number|false|This is the timeout in seconds for the request. Defaults to 20 seconds.<br><br>@default 20|
|» » credentialId|body|string|false|The credential ID for server authentication|
|» » staticIpAddressesEnabled|body|boolean|false|If enabled, requests will originate from a static set of IPs owned and managed by Vapi.<br><br>@default false|
|» » encryptedPaths|body|[string]|false|This is the paths to encrypt in the request body if credentialId and encryptionPlan are defined.|
|» » url|body|string|false|This is where the request will be sent.|
|» » headers|body|object|false|These are the headers to include in the request.<br><br>Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.<br><br>Note: Specifying an Authorization header here will override the authorization provided by the `credentialId` (if provided). This is an anti-pattern and should be avoided outside of edge case scenarios.|
|» » backoffPlan|body|object|false|This is the backoff plan if the request fails. Defaults to undefined (the request will not be retried).<br><br>@default undefined (the request will not be retried)|
|» » » type|body|object|true|This is the type of backoff plan to use. Defaults to fixed.<br><br>@default fixed|
|» » » maxRetries|body|number|true|This is the maximum number of retries to attempt if the request fails. Defaults to 0 (no retries).<br><br>@default 0|
|» » » baseDelaySeconds|body|number|true|This is the base delay in seconds. For linear backoff, this is the delay between each retry. For exponential backoff, this is the initial delay.|

<h1 id="vapi-api-squads">Squads</h1>

## List Squads

<a id="opIdSquadController_findAll"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vapi.ai/squad \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /squad`

<h3 id="list-squads-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|idAny|query|[string]|false|Return only squads matching the provided ids|
|limit|query|number|false|This is the maximum number of items to return. Defaults to 100.|
|createdAtGt|query|string(date-time)|false|This will return items where the createdAt is greater than the specified value.|
|createdAtLt|query|string(date-time)|false|This will return items where the createdAt is less than the specified value.|
|createdAtGe|query|string(date-time)|false|This will return items where the createdAt is greater than or equal to the specified value.|
|createdAtLe|query|string(date-time)|false|This will return items where the createdAt is less than or equal to the specified value.|
|updatedAtGt|query|string(date-time)|false|This will return items where the updatedAt is greater than the specified value.|
|updatedAtLt|query|string(date-time)|false|This will return items where the updatedAt is less than the specified value.|
|updatedAtGe|query|string(date-time)|false|This will return items where the updatedAt is greater than or equal to the specified value.|
|updatedAtLe|query|string(date-time)|false|This will return items where the updatedAt is less than or equal to the specified value.|

## Create Squad

<a id="opIdSquadController_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vapi.ai/squad \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "members": [
      {}
    ],
    "membersOverrides": {}
  }'
```

`POST /squad`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "members": [
    {}
  ],
  "membersOverrides": {}
}
```

<h3 id="create-squad-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateSquadDTO](#schemacreatesquaddto)|true|none|
|» name|body|string|false|This is the name of the squad.|
|» members|body|[[SquadMemberDTO](#schemasquadmemberdto)]|true|This is the list of assistants that make up the squad.<br><br>The call will start with the first assistant in the list.|
|» membersOverrides|body|object|false|This can be used to override all the assistants' settings and provide values for their template variables.<br><br>Both `membersOverrides` and `members[n].assistantOverrides` can be used together. First, `members[n].assistantOverrides` is applied. Then, `membersOverrides` is applied as a global override.|

|» » variableValues|body|object|false|These are values that will be used to replace the template variables in the assistant messages and other text-based fields.<br>This uses LiquidJS syntax. https://liquidjs.com/tutorials/intro-to-liquid.html<br><br>So for example, `{{ name }}` will be replaced with the value of `name` in `variableValues`.<br>`{{"now" \| date: "%b %d, %Y, %I:%M %p", "America/New_York"}}` will be replaced with the current date and time in New York.<br> Some VAPI reserved defaults:<br> - *customer* - the customer object|
|» » name|body|string|false|This is the name of the assistant.<br><br>This is required when you want to transfer between assistants in a call.|
|» » voicemailMessage|body|string|false|This is the message that the assistant will say if the call is forwarded to voicemail.<br><br>If unspecified, it will hang up.|
|» » endCallMessage|body|string|false|This is the message that the assistant will say if it ends the call.<br><br>If unspecified, it will hang up without saying anything.|
|» » endCallPhrases|body|[string]|false|This list contains phrases that, if spoken by the assistant, will trigger the call to be hung up. Case insensitive.|
|» » compliancePlan|body|[CompliancePlan](#schemacomplianceplan)|false|none|
|» » metadata|body|object|false|This is for metadata you want to store on the assistant.|
|» » backgroundSpeechDenoisingPlan|body|object|false|This enables filtering of noise and background speech while the user is talking.<br><br>Features:<br>- Smart denoising using Krisp<br>- Fourier denoising<br><br>Smart denoising can be combined with or used independently of Fourier denoising.<br><br>Order of precedence:<br>- Smart denoising<br>- Fourier denoising|
|» » » smartDenoisingPlan|body|object|false|Whether smart denoising using Krisp is enabled.|
|» » » » enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether smart denoising using Krisp is enabled.|
|» » » fourierDenoisingPlan|body|object|false|Whether Fourier denoising is enabled. Note that this is experimental and may not work as expected.<br><br>This can be combined with smart denoising, and will be run afterwards.|
|» » » » enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether Fourier denoising is enabled. Note that this is experimental and may not work as expected.|
|» » » » mediaDetectionEnabled|body|boolean|false|Whether automatic media detection is enabled. When enabled, the filter will automatically<br>detect consistent background TV/music/radio and switch to more aggressive filtering settings.<br>Only applies when enabled is true.|
|» » » » staticThreshold|body|number|false|Static threshold in dB used as fallback when no baseline is established.|
|» » » » baselineOffsetDb|body|number|false|How far below the rolling baseline to filter audio, in dB.<br>Lower values (e.g., -10) are more aggressive, higher values (e.g., -20) are more conservative.|
|» » » » windowSizeMs|body|number|false|Rolling window size in milliseconds for calculating the audio baseline.<br>Larger windows adapt more slowly but are more stable.|
|» » » » baselinePercentile|body|number|false|Percentile to use for baseline calculation (1-99).<br>Higher percentiles (e.g., 85) focus on louder speech, lower percentiles (e.g., 50) include quieter speech.|

The output is stored in `call.analysis.successEvaluation`.<br><br>Options include:<br>- 'NumericScale': A scale of 1 to 10.<br>- 'DescriptiveScale': A scale of Excellent, Good, Fair, Poor.<br>- 'Checklist': A checklist of criteria and their status.<br>- 'Matrix': A grid that evaluates multiple criteria across different performance levels.<br>- 'PercentageScale': A scale of 0% to 100%.<br>- 'LikertScale': A scale of Strongly Agree, Agree, Neutral, Disagree, Strongly Disagree.<br>- 'AutomaticRubric': Automatically break down evaluation into several criteria, each with its own score.<br>- 'PassFail': A simple 'true' if call passed, 'false' if not.<br><br>Default is 'PassFail'.|

Here is the ended reason of the call:\n\n{{endedReason}}\n\n"<br>  }<br>]```<br><br>You can customize by providing any messages you want.<br><br>Here are the template variables available:<br>- {{transcript}}: the transcript of the call from `call.artifact.transcript`- {{systemPrompt}}: the system prompt of the call from `assistant.model.messages[type=system].content`- {{messages}}: the messages of the call from `assistant.model.messages`- {{rubric}}: the rubric of the success evaluation from `successEvaluationPlan.rubric`- {{endedReason}}: the ended reason of the call from `call.endedReason`|

<h1 id="vapi-api-calls">Calls</h1>

## List Calls

<a id="opIdCallController_findAll"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vapi.ai/call \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /call`

<h3 id="list-calls-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|query|string|false|This is the unique identifier for the call.|
|assistantId|query|string|false|This will return calls with the specified assistantId.|
|phoneNumberId|query|string|false|This is the phone number that will be used for the call. To use a transient number, use `phoneNumber` instead.<br><br>Only relevant for `outboundPhoneCall` and `inboundPhoneCall` type.|
|limit|query|number|false|This is the maximum number of items to return. Defaults to 100.|
|createdAtGt|query|string(date-time)|false|This will return items where the createdAt is greater than the specified value.|
|createdAtLt|query|string(date-time)|false|This will return items where the createdAt is less than the specified value.|
|createdAtGe|query|string(date-time)|false|This will return items where the createdAt is greater than or equal to the specified value.|
|createdAtLe|query|string(date-time)|false|This will return items where the createdAt is less than or equal to the specified value.|
|updatedAtGt|query|string(date-time)|false|This will return items where the updatedAt is greater than the specified value.|
|updatedAtLt|query|string(date-time)|false|This will return items where the updatedAt is less than the specified value.|
|updatedAtGe|query|string(date-time)|false|This will return items where the updatedAt is greater than or equal to the specified value.|
|updatedAtLe|query|string(date-time)|false|This will return items where the updatedAt is less than or equal to the specified value.|

|» » » » onNoPunctuationSeconds|body|number|false|The minimum number of seconds to wait after transcription ending without punctuation before sending a request to the model. |» » » » onNumberSeconds|body|number|false|The minimum number of seconds to wait after transcription ending with a number before sending a request to the model. |» » stopSpeakingPlan|body|object|false|This is the plan for when assistant should stop talking on customer interruption.<br><br>You should configure this if you're running into these issues:<br>- The assistant is too slow to recognize customer's interruption.<br>- The assistant is too fast to recognize customer's interruption.<br>- The assistant is getting interrupted by phrases that are just acknowledgments.<br>- The assistant is getting interrupted by background noises.<br>- The assistant is not properly stopping -- it starts talking right after getting interrupted.|
|» » » numWords|body|number|false|This is the number of words that the customer has to say before the assistant will stop talking.<br><br>Words like "stop", "actually", "no", etc. will always interrupt immediately regardless of this value.<br><br>Words like "okay", "yeah", "right" will never interrupt.<br><br>When set to 0, `voiceSeconds` is used in addition to the transcriptions to determine the customer has started speaking.<br><br>Defaults to 0.<br><br>@default 0|
|» » » voiceSeconds|body|number|false|This is the seconds customer has to speak before the assistant stops talking. This uses the VAD (Voice Activity Detection) spike to determine if the customer has started speaking.<br><br>Considerations:<br>- A lower value might be more responsive but could potentially pick up non-speech sounds.<br>- A higher value reduces false positives but might slightly delay the detection of speech onset.<br><br>This is only used if `numWords` is set to 0.<br><br>Defaults to 0.2<br><br>@default 0.2|
|» » » backoffSeconds|body|number|false|This is the seconds to wait before the assistant will start talking again after being interrupted.<br><br>Defaults to 1.<br><br>@default 1|
|» » » acknowledgementPhrases|body|[string]|false|These are the phrases that will never interrupt the assistant, even if numWords threshold is met.<br>These are typically acknowledgement or backchanneling phrases.|

|» » variableValues|body|object|false|These are values that will be used to replace the template variables in the assistant messages and other text-based fields.<br>This uses LiquidJS syntax. https://liquidjs.com/tutorials/intro-to-liquid.html<br><br>So for example, `{{ name }}` will be replaced with the value of `name` in `variableValues`.<br>`{{"now" \| date: "%b %d, %Y, %I:%M %p", "America/New_York"}}` will be replaced with the current date and time in New York.<br> Some VAPI reserved defaults:<br> - *customer* - the customer object|
|» » name|body|string|false|This is the name of the assistant.<br><br>This is required when you want to transfer between assistants in a call.|
|» » voicemailMessage|body|string|false|This is the message that the assistant will say if the call is forwarded to voicemail.<br><br>If unspecified, it will hang up.|
|» » endCallMessage|body|string|false|This is the message that the assistant will say if it ends the call.<br><br>If unspecified, it will hang up without saying anything.|
|» » endCallPhrases|body|[string]|false|This list contains phrases that, if spoken by the assistant, will trigger the call to be hung up. Case insensitive.|
|» » compliancePlan|body|[CompliancePlan](#schemacomplianceplan)|false|none|
|» » metadata|body|object|false|This is for metadata you want to store on the assistant.|
|» » backgroundSpeechDenoisingPlan|body|object|false|This enables filtering of noise and background speech while the user is talking.<br><br>Features:<br>- Smart denoising using Krisp<br>- Fourier denoising<br><br>Smart denoising can be combined with or used independently of Fourier denoising.<br><br>Order of precedence:<br>- Smart denoising<br>- Fourier denoising|
|» » » smartDenoisingPlan|body|object|false|Whether smart denoising using Krisp is enabled.|
|» » » » enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether smart denoising using Krisp is enabled.|
|» » » fourierDenoisingPlan|body|object|false|Whether Fourier denoising is enabled. Note that this is experimental and may not work as expected.<br><br>This can be combined with smart denoising, and will be run afterwards.|
|» » » » enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether Fourier denoising is enabled. Note that this is experimental and may not work as expected.|
|» » » » mediaDetectionEnabled|body|boolean|false|Whether automatic media detection is enabled. When enabled, the filter will automatically<br>detect consistent background TV/music/radio and switch to more aggressive filtering settings.<br>Only applies when enabled is true.|
|» » » » staticThreshold|body|number|false|Static threshold in dB used as fallback when no baseline is established.|
|» » » » baselineOffsetDb|body|number|false|How far below the rolling baseline to filter audio, in dB.<br>Lower values (e.g., -10) are more aggressive, higher values (e.g., -20) are more conservative.|
|» » » » windowSizeMs|body|number|false|Rolling window size in milliseconds for calculating the audio baseline.<br>Larger windows adapt more slowly but are more stable.|
|» » » » baselinePercentile|body|number|false|Percentile to use for baseline calculation (1-99).<br>Higher percentiles (e.g., 85) focus on louder speech, lower percentiles (e.g., 50) include quieter speech.|

|» » variableValues|body|object|false|These are values that will be used to replace the template variables in the assistant messages and other text-based fields.<br>This uses LiquidJS syntax. https://liquidjs.com/tutorials/intro-to-liquid.html<br><br>So for example, `{{ name }}` will be replaced with the value of `name` in `variableValues`.<br>`{{"now" \| date: "%b %d, %Y, %I:%M %p", "America/New_York"}}` will be replaced with the current date and time in New York.<br> Some VAPI reserved defaults:<br> - *customer* - the customer object|
|» » name|body|string|false|This is the name of the assistant.<br><br>This is required when you want to transfer between assistants in a call.|
|» » voicemailMessage|body|string|false|This is the message that the assistant will say if the call is forwarded to voicemail.<br><br>If unspecified, it will hang up.|
|» » endCallMessage|body|string|false|This is the message that the assistant will say if it ends the call.<br><br>If unspecified, it will hang up without saying anything.|
|» » endCallPhrases|body|[string]|false|This list contains phrases that, if spoken by the assistant, will trigger the call to be hung up. Case insensitive.|
|» » compliancePlan|body|[CompliancePlan](#schemacomplianceplan)|false|none|
|» » metadata|body|object|false|This is for metadata you want to store on the assistant.|
|» » backgroundSpeechDenoisingPlan|body|object|false|This enables filtering of noise and background speech while the user is talking.<br><br>Features:<br>- Smart denoising using Krisp<br>- Fourier denoising<br><br>Smart denoising can be combined with or used independently of Fourier denoising.<br><br>Order of precedence:<br>- Smart denoising<br>- Fourier denoising|
|» » » smartDenoisingPlan|body|object|false|Whether smart denoising using Krisp is enabled.|
|» » » » enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether smart denoising using Krisp is enabled.|
|» » » fourierDenoisingPlan|body|object|false|Whether Fourier denoising is enabled. Note that this is experimental and may not work as expected.<br><br>This can be combined with smart denoising, and will be run afterwards.|
|» » » » enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether Fourier denoising is enabled. Note that this is experimental and may not work as expected.|
|» » » » mediaDetectionEnabled|body|boolean|false|Whether automatic media detection is enabled. When enabled, the filter will automatically<br>detect consistent background TV/music/radio and switch to more aggressive filtering settings.<br>Only applies when enabled is true.|
|» » » » staticThreshold|body|number|false|Static threshold in dB used as fallback when no baseline is established.|
|» » » » baselineOffsetDb|body|number|false|How far below the rolling baseline to filter audio, in dB.<br>Lower values (e.g., -10) are more aggressive, higher values (e.g., -20) are more conservative.|
|» » » » windowSizeMs|body|number|false|Rolling window size in milliseconds for calculating the audio baseline.<br>Larger windows adapt more slowly but are more stable.|
|» » » » baselinePercentile|body|number|false|Percentile to use for baseline calculation (1-99).<br>Higher percentiles (e.g., 85) focus on louder speech, lower percentiles (e.g., 50) include quieter speech.|
|» » analysisPlan|body|object|false|**Deprecated.** This is the plan for analysis of assistant's calls. Stored in `call.analysis`.|
|» » » minMessagesThreshold|body|number|false|**Deprecated.** The minimum number of messages required to run the analysis plan.<br>If the number of messages is less than this, analysis will be skipped.<br><br>@default 2|
|» » » summaryPlan|body|object|false|**Deprecated.** This is the plan for generating the summary of the call. This outputs to `call.analysis.summary`.|
|» » » » messages|body|[object]|false|These are the messages used to generate the summary.<br><br>@default: ```<br>[<br>  {<br>    "role": "system",<br>    "content": "You are an expert note-taker. You will be given a transcript of a call. Summarize the call in 2-3 sentences. DO NOT return anything except the summary."<br>  },<br>  {<br>    "role": "user",<br>    "content": "Here is the transcript:\n\n{{transcript}}\n\n. Here is the ended reason of the call:\n\n{{endedReason}}\n\n"<br>  }<br>]```<br><br>You can customize by providing any messages you want.<br><br>Here are the template variables available:<br>- {{transcript}}: The transcript of the call from `call.artifact.transcript` <br>- {{systemPrompt}}: The system prompt of the call from `assistant.model.messages[type=system].content` <br>- {{messages}}: The messages of the call from `assistant.model.messages` <br>- {{endedReason}}: The ended reason of the call from `call.endedReason`|
|» » » » enabled|body|boolean|false|This determines whether a summary is generated and stored in `call.analysis.summary`. Defaults to true.<br><br>Usage:<br>- If you want to disable the summary, set this to false.<br><br>@default true|
|» » » » timeoutSeconds|body|number|false|This is how long the request is tried before giving up. When request times out, `call.analysis.summary` will be empty.<br><br>Usage:<br>- To guarantee the summary is generated, set this value high. Note, this will delay the end of call report in cases where model is slow to respond.<br><br>@default 5 seconds|
|» » » structuredDataPlan|body|object|false|**Deprecated.** This is the plan for generating the structured data from the call. This outputs to `call.analysis.structuredData`.|
|» » » » messages|body|[object]|false|These are the messages used to generate the structured data.<br><br>@default: ```<br>[<br>  {<br>    "role": "system",<br>    "content": "You are an expert data extractor. You will be given a transcript of a call. Extract structured data per the JSON Schema. Here is the ended reason of the call:\n\n{{endedReason}}\n\n"<br>  }<br>]```<br><br>You can customize by providing any messages you want.<br><br>Here are the template variables available:<br>- {{transcript}}: the transcript of the call from `call.artifact.transcript`- {{systemPrompt}}: the system prompt of the call from `assistant.model.messages[type=system].content`- {{messages}}: the messages of the call from `assistant.model.messages`- {{schema}}: the schema of the structured data from `structuredDataPlan.schema`- {{endedReason}}: the ended reason of the call from `call.endedReason`|
|» » » » enabled|body|boolean|false|This determines whether structured data is generated and stored in `call.analysis.structuredData`. Defaults to false.<br><br>Usage:<br>- If you want to extract structured data, set this to true and provide a `schema`.<br><br>@default false|
|» » » » schema|body|object|false|This is the schema of the structured data. The output is stored in `call.analysis.structuredData`.<br><br>Complete guide on JSON Schema can be found [here](https://ajv.js.org/json-schema.html#json-data-type).|
|» » » » timeoutSeconds|body|number|false|This is how long the request is tried before giving up. Note, this will delay the end of call report in cases where model is slow to respond.<br><br>@default 5 seconds|

|» » » successEvaluationPlan|body|object|false|**Deprecated.** This is the plan for generating the success evaluation of the call. This outputs to `call.analysis.successEvaluation`.|
|» » » » rubric|body|string|false|This enforces the rubric of the evaluation. The output is stored in `call.analysis.successEvaluation`.<br><br>Options include:<br>- 'NumericScale': A scale of 1 to 10.<br>- 'DescriptiveScale': A scale of Excellent, Good, Fair, Poor.<br>- 'Checklist': A checklist of criteria and their status.<br>- 'Matrix': A grid that evaluates multiple criteria across different performance levels.<br>- 'PercentageScale': A scale of 0% to 100%.<br>- 'LikertScale': A scale of Strongly Agree, Agree, Neutral, Disagree, Strongly Disagree.<br>- 'AutomaticRubric': Automatically break down evaluation into several criteria, each with its own score.<br>- 'PassFail': A simple 'true' if call passed, 'false' if not.<br><br>Default is 'PassFail'.|
|» » » » messages|body|[object]|false|These are the messages used to generate the success evaluation.<br><br>@default: ```<br>[<br>  {<br>    "role": "system",<br>    "content": "You are an expert call evaluator. You will be given a transcript of a call and the system prompt of the AI participant. Determine if the call was successful based on the objectives inferred from the system prompt. DO NOT return anything except the result.\n\nRubric:\\n{{rubric}}\n\nOnly respond with the result."<br>  },<br>  {<br>    "role": "user",<br>    "content": "Here is the transcript:\n\n{{transcript}}\n\n"<br>  },<br>  {<br>    "role": "user",<br>    "content": "Here was the system prompt of the call:\n\n{{systemPrompt}}\n\n. Here is the ended reason of the call:\n\n{{endedReason}}\n\n"<br>  }<br>]```<br><br>You can customize by providing any messages you want.<br><br>Here are the template variables available:<br>- {{transcript}}: the transcript of the call from `call.artifact.transcript`- {{systemPrompt}}: the system prompt of the call from `assistant.model.messages[type=system].content`- {{messages}}: the messages of the call from `assistant.model.messages`- {{rubric}}: the rubric of the success evaluation from `successEvaluationPlan.rubric`- {{endedReason}}: the ended reason of the call from `call.endedReason`|
|» » » » enabled|body|boolean|false|This determines whether a success evaluation is generated and stored in `call.analysis.successEvaluation`. Defaults to true.<br><br>Usage:<br>- If you want to disable the success evaluation, set this to false.<br><br>@default true|
|» » » » timeoutSeconds|body|number|false|This is how long the request is tried before giving up. When request times out, `call.analysis.successEvaluation` will be empty.<br><br>Usage:<br>- To guarantee the success evaluation is generated, set this value high. Note, this will delay the end of call report in cases where model is slow to respond.<br><br>@default 5 seconds|

|» » artifactPlan|body|object|false|This is the plan for artifacts generated during assistant's calls. Stored in `call.artifact`.|
|» » » recordingEnabled|body|boolean|false|This determines whether assistant's calls are recorded. Defaults to true.<br><br>Usage:<br>- If you don't want to record the calls, set this to false.<br>- If you want to record the calls when `assistant.hipaaEnabled` (deprecated) or `assistant.compliancePlan.hipaaEnabled` explicity set this to true and make sure to provide S3 or GCP credentials on the Provider Credentials page in the Dashboard.<br><br>You can find the recording at `call.artifact.recordingUrl` and `call.artifact.stereoRecordingUrl` after the call is ended.<br><br>@default true|

|» » » recordingUseCustomStorageEnabled|body|boolean|false|This determines whether to use custom storage (S3 or GCP) for call recordings when storage credentials are configured.<br><br>When set to false, recordings will be stored on Vapi's storage instead of your custom storage, even if you have custom storage credentials configured.<br><br>Usage:<br>- Set to false if you have custom storage configured but want to store recordings on Vapi's storage for this assistant.<br>- Set to true (or leave unset) to use your custom storage for recordings when available.<br><br>If your organization has ZDR (zero data retention) or PCI enabled, recordings are never written to Vapi storage. |» » » » messages|body|[object]|false|These are the messages used to generate the success evaluation.<br><br>@default: ```<br>[<br>  {<br>    "role": "system",<br>    "content": "You are an expert call evaluator. DO NOT return anything except the result.\n\nRubric:\\n{{rubric}}\n\nOnly respond with the result."<br>  },<br>  {<br>    "role": "user",<br>    "content": "Here is the transcript:\n\n{{transcript}}\n\n"<br>  },<br>  {<br>    "role": "user",<br>    "content": "Here was the system prompt of the call:\n\n{{systemPrompt}}\n\n. Here is the ended reason of the call:\n\n{{endedReason}}\n\n"<br>  }<br>]```<br><br>You can customize by providing any messages you want.<br><br>Here are the template variables available:<br>- {{transcript}}: the transcript of the call from `call.artifact.transcript`- {{systemPrompt}}: the system prompt of the call from `assistant.model.messages[type=system].content`- {{messages}}: the messages of the call from `assistant.model.messages`- {{rubric}}: the rubric of the success evaluation from `successEvaluationPlan.rubric`- {{endedReason}}: the ended reason of the call from `call.endedReason`|

|» » » stopSpeakingPlan|body|object|false|This is the plan for when assistant should stop talking on customer interruption.<br><br>You should configure this if you're running into these issues:<br>- The assistant is too slow to recognize customer's interruption.<br>- The assistant is too fast to recognize customer's interruption.<br>- The assistant is getting interrupted by phrases that are just acknowledgments.<br>- The assistant is getting interrupted by background noises.<br>- The assistant is not properly stopping -- it starts talking right after getting interrupted.|
|» » » » numWords|body|number|false|This is the number of words that the customer has to say before the assistant will stop talking.<br><br>Words like "stop", "actually", "no", etc. will always interrupt immediately regardless of this value.<br><br>Words like "okay", "yeah", "right" will never interrupt.<br><br>When set to 0, `voiceSeconds` is used in addition to the transcriptions to determine the customer has started speaking.<br><br>Defaults to 0.<br><br>@default 0|
|» » » » voiceSeconds|body|number|false|This is the seconds customer has to speak before the assistant stops talking. This uses the VAD (Voice Activity Detection) spike to determine if the customer has started speaking.<br><br>Considerations:<br>- A lower value might be more responsive but could potentially pick up non-speech sounds.<br>- A higher value reduces false positives but might slightly delay the detection of speech onset.<br><br>This is only used if `numWords` is set to 0.<br><br>Defaults to 0.2<br><br>@default 0.2|
|» » » » backoffSeconds|body|number|false|This is the seconds to wait before the assistant will start talking again after being interrupted.<br><br>Defaults to 1.<br><br>@default 1|
|» » » » acknowledgementPhrases|body|[string]|false|These are the phrases that will never interrupt the assistant, even if numWords threshold is met.<br>These are typically acknowledgement or backchanneling phrases.|

|» » » variableValues|body|object|false|These are values that will be used to replace the template variables in the assistant messages and other text-based fields.<br>This uses LiquidJS syntax. https://liquidjs.com/tutorials/intro-to-liquid.html<br><br>So for example, `{{ name }}` will be replaced with the value of `name` in `variableValues`.<br>`{{"now" \| date: "%b %d, %Y, %I:%M %p", "America/New_York"}}` will be replaced with the current date and time in New York.<br> Some VAPI reserved defaults:<br> - *customer* - the customer object|
|» » » name|body|string|false|This is the name of the assistant.<br><br>This is required when you want to transfer between assistants in a call.|

|» » » endCallPhrases|body|[string]|false|This list contains phrases that, if spoken by the assistant, will trigger the call to be hung up. Case insensitive.|

|» » » backgroundSpeechDenoisingPlan|body|object|false|This enables filtering of noise and background speech while the user is talking.<br><br>Features:<br>- Smart denoising using Krisp<br>- Fourier denoising<br><br>Smart denoising can be combined with or used independently of Fourier denoising.<br><br>Order of precedence:<br>- Smart denoising<br>- Fourier denoising|
|» » » » smartDenoisingPlan|body|object|false|Whether smart denoising using Krisp is enabled.|
|» » » » » enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether smart denoising using Krisp is enabled.|
|» » » » fourierDenoisingPlan|body|object|false|Whether Fourier denoising is enabled. Note that this is experimental and may not work as expected.<br><br>This can be combined with smart denoising, and will be run afterwards.|
|» » » » » enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether Fourier denoising is enabled. Note that this is experimental and may not work as expected.|
|» » » » » mediaDetectionEnabled|body|boolean|false|Whether automatic media detection is enabled. When enabled, the filter will automatically<br>detect consistent background TV/music/radio and switch to more aggressive filtering settings.<br>Only applies when enabled is true.|
|» » » » » staticThreshold|body|number|false|Static threshold in dB used as fallback when no baseline is established.|
|» » » » » baselineOffsetDb|body|number|false|How far below the rolling baseline to filter audio, in dB.<br>Lower values (e.g., -10) are more aggressive, higher values (e.g., -20) are more conservative.|
|» » » » » windowSizeMs|body|number|false|Rolling window size in milliseconds for calculating the audio baseline.<br>Larger windows adapt more slowly but are more stable.|
|» » » » » baselinePercentile|body|number|false|Percentile to use for baseline calculation (1-99).<br>Higher percentiles (e.g., 85) focus on louder speech, lower percentiles (e.g., 50) include quieter speech.|

The output is stored in `call.analysis.successEvaluation`.<br><br>Options include:<br>- 'NumericScale': A scale of 1 to 10.<br>- 'DescriptiveScale': A scale of Excellent, Good, Fair, Poor.<br>- 'Checklist': A checklist of criteria and their status.<br>- 'Matrix': A grid that evaluates multiple criteria across different performance levels.<br>- 'PercentageScale': A scale of 0% to 100%.<br>- 'LikertScale': A scale of Strongly Agree, Agree, Neutral, Disagree, Strongly Disagree.<br>- 'AutomaticRubric': Automatically break down evaluation into several criteria, each with its own score.<br>- 'PassFail': A simple 'true' if call passed, 'false' if not.<br><br>Default is 'PassFail'.|

Here is the ended reason of the call:\n\n{{endedReason}}\n\n"<br>  }<br>]```<br><br>You can customize by providing any messages you want.<br><br>Here are the template variables available:<br>- {{transcript}}: the transcript of the call from `call.artifact.transcript`- {{systemPrompt}}: the system prompt of the call from `assistant.model.messages[type=system].content`- {{messages}}: the messages of the call from `assistant.model.messages`- {{rubric}}: the rubric of the success evaluation from `successEvaluationPlan.rubric`- {{endedReason}}: the ended reason of the call from `call.endedReason`|

|» » » » recordingUseCustomStorageEnabled|body|boolean|false|This determines whether to use custom storage (S3 or GCP) for call recordings when storage credentials are configured.<br><br>When set to false, recordings will be stored on Vapi's storage instead of your custom storage, even if you have custom storage credentials configured.<br><br>Usage:<br>- Set to false if you have custom storage configured but want to store recordings on Vapi's storage for this assistant.<br>- Set to true (or leave unset) to use your custom storage for recordings when available.<br><br>If your organization has ZDR (zero data retention) or PCI enabled, recordings are never written to Vapi storage. |» » » » » *oneOf*|body|[LivekitSmartEndpointingPlan](#schemalivekitsmartendpointingplan)|false|none|
|» » » » » *oneOf*|body|[CustomEndpointingModelSmartEndpointingPlan](#schemacustomendpointingmodelsmartendpointingplan)|false|none|
|» » » » customEndpointingRules|body|[[AssistantCustomEndpointingRule](#schemaassistantcustomendpointingrule) \| [CustomerCustomEndpointingRule](#schemacustomercustomendpointingrule) \| [BothCustomEndpointingRule](#schemabothcustomendpointingrule)]|false|These are the custom endpointing rules to set an endpointing timeout based on a regex on the customer's speech or the assistant's last message.<br><br>Usage:<br>- If you have yes/no questions like "are you interested in a loan?", you can set a shorter timeout.<br>- If you have questions where the customer may pause to look up information like "what's my account number?", you can set a longer timeout.<br>- If you want to wait longer while customer is enumerating a list of numbers, you can set a longer timeout.<br><br>These rules have the highest precedence and will override both `smartEndpointingPlan` and `transcriptionEndpointingPlan` when a rule is matched.<br><br>The rules are evaluated in order and the first one that matches will be used.<br><br>Order of precedence for endpointing:<br>1. customEndpointingRules (if any match)<br>2. smartEndpointingPlan (if set)<br>3. transcriptionEndpointingPlan<br><br>@default []|
|» » » » » *oneOf*|body|[AssistantCustomEndpointingRule](#schemaassistantcustomendpointingrule)|false|none|
|» » » » » *oneOf*|body|[CustomerCustomEndpointingRule](#schemacustomercustomendpointingrule)|false|none|
|» » » » » *oneOf*|body|[BothCustomEndpointingRule](#schemabothcustomendpointingrule)|false|none|
|» » » » transcriptionEndpointingPlan|body|object|false|This determines how a customer speech is considered done (endpointing) using the transcription of customer's speech.<br><br>Once an endpoint is triggered, the request is sent to `assistant.model`.<br><br>Note: This plan is only used if `smartEndpointingPlan` is not set and transcriber does not have built-in endpointing capabilities. If both are provided, `smartEndpointingPlan` takes precedence.<br>This plan will also be overridden by any matching `customEndpointingRules`.|
|» » » » » onPunctuationSeconds|body|number|false|The minimum number of seconds to wait after transcription ending with punctuation before sending a request to the model. Defaults to 0.1.<br><br>This setting exists because the transcriber punctuates the transcription when it's more confident that customer has completed a thought.<br><br>@default 0.1|
|» » » » » onNoPunctuationSeconds|body|number|false|The minimum number of seconds to wait after transcription ending without punctuation before sending a request to the model. Defaults to 1.5.<br><br>This setting exists to catch the cases where the transcriber was not confident enough to punctuate the transcription, but the customer is done and has been silent for a long time.<br><br>@default 1.5|
|» » » » » onNumberSeconds|body|number|false|The minimum number of seconds to wait after transcription ending with a number before sending a request to the model. Defaults to 0.4.<br><br>This setting exists because the transcriber will sometimes punctuate the transcription ending with a number, even though the customer hasn't uttered the full number. This happens commonly for long numbers when the customer reads the number in chunks.<br><br>@default 0.5|
|» » » stopSpeakingPlan|body|object|false|This is the plan for when assistant should stop talking on customer interruption.<br><br>You should configure this if you're running into these issues:<br>- The assistant is too slow to recognize customer's interruption.<br>- The assistant is too fast to recognize customer's interruption.<br>- The assistant is getting interrupted by phrases that are just acknowledgments.<br>- The assistant is getting interrupted by background noises.<br>- The assistant is not properly stopping -- it starts talking right after getting interrupted.|
|» » » » numWords|body|number|false|This is the number of words that the customer has to say before the assistant will stop talking.<br><br>Words like "stop", "actually", "no", etc. will always interrupt immediately regardless of this value.<br><br>Words like "okay", "yeah", "right" will never interrupt.<br><br>When set to 0, `voiceSeconds` is used in addition to the transcriptions to determine the customer has started speaking.<br><br>Defaults to 0.<br><br>@default 0|
|» » » » voiceSeconds|body|number|false|This is the seconds customer has to speak before the assistant stops talking. This uses the VAD (Voice Activity Detection) spike to determine if the customer has started speaking.<br><br>Considerations:<br>- A lower value might be more responsive but could potentially pick up non-speech sounds.<br>- A higher value reduces false positives but might slightly delay the detection of speech onset.<br><br>This is only used if `numWords` is set to 0.<br><br>Defaults to 0.2<br><br>@default 0.2|
|» » » » backoffSeconds|body|number|false|This is the seconds to wait before the assistant will start talking again after being interrupted.<br><br>Defaults to 1.<br><br>@default 1|
|» » » » acknowledgementPhrases|body|[string]|false|These are the phrases that will never interrupt the assistant, even if numWords threshold is met.<br>These are typically acknowledgement or backchanneling phrases.|
|» » » » interruptionPhrases|body|[string]|false|These are the phrases that will always interrupt the assistant immediately, regardless of numWords.<br>These are typically phrases indicating disagreement or desire to stop.|
|» » » monitorPlan|body|object|false|This is the plan for real-time monitoring of the assistant's calls.<br><br>Usage:<br>- To enable live listening of the assistant's calls, set `monitorPlan.listenEnabled` to `true`.<br>- To enable live control of the assistant's calls, set `monitorPlan.controlEnabled` to `true`.<br>- To attach monitors to the assistant, set `monitorPlan.monitorIds` to the set of monitor ids.|
|» » » » listenEnabled|body|boolean|false|This determines whether the assistant's calls allow live listening. Defaults to true.<br><br>Fetch `call.monitor.listenUrl` to get the live listening URL.<br><br>@default true|
|» » » » listenAuthenticationEnabled|body|boolean|false|This enables authentication on the `call.monitor.listenUrl`.<br><br>If `listenAuthenticationEnabled` is `true`, the `call.monitor.listenUrl` will require an `Authorization: Bearer <vapi-public-api-key>` header.<br><br>@default false|
|» » » » controlEnabled|body|boolean|false|This determines whether the assistant's calls allow live control. Defaults to true.<br><br>Fetch `call.monitor.controlUrl` to get the live control URL.<br><br>To use, send any control message via a POST request to `call.monitor.controlUrl`. Here are the types of controls supported: https://docs.vapi.ai/api-reference/messages/client-inbound-message<br><br>@default true|
|» » » » controlAuthenticationEnabled|body|boolean|false|This enables authentication on the `call.monitor.controlUrl`.<br><br>If `controlAuthenticationEnabled` is `true`, the `call.monitor.controlUrl` will require an `Authorization: Bearer <vapi-public-api-key>` header.<br><br>@default false|
|» » » » monitorIds|body|[string]|false|This the set of monitor ids that are attached to the assistant.<br>The source of truth for the monitor ids is the assistant_monitor join table.<br>This field can be used for transient assistants and to update assistants with new monitor ids.<br><br>@default []|
|» » » credentialIds|body|[string]|false|These are the credentials that will be used for the assistant calls. By default, all the credentials are available for use in the call but you can provide a subset using this.|
|» » » server|body|object|false|This is where Vapi will send webhooks. You can find all webhooks available along with their shape in ServerMessage schema.<br><br>The order of precedence is:<br><br>1. assistant.server.url<br>2. phoneNumber.serverUrl<br>3. org.serverUrl|
|» » » » timeoutSeconds|body|number|false|This is the timeout in seconds for the request. Defaults to 20 seconds.<br><br>@default 20|
|» » » » credentialId|body|string|false|The credential ID for server authentication|
|» » » » staticIpAddressesEnabled|body|boolean|false|If enabled, requests will originate from a static set of IPs owned and managed by Vapi.<br><br>@default false|
|» » » » encryptedPaths|body|[string]|false|This is the paths to encrypt in the request body if credentialId and encryptionPlan are defined.|
|» » » » url|body|string|false|This is where the request will be sent.|
|» » » » headers|body|object|false|These are the headers to include in the request.<br><br>Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.<br><br>Note: Specifying an Authorization header here will override the authorization provided by the `credentialId` (if provided). This is an anti-pattern and should be avoided outside of edge case scenarios.|
|» » » » backoffPlan|body|object|false|This is the backoff plan if the request fails. Defaults to undefined (the request will not be retried).<br><br>@default undefined (the request will not be retried)|
|» » » » » type|body|object|true|This is the type of backoff plan to use. Defaults to fixed.<br><br>@default fixed|
|» » » » » maxRetries|body|number|true|This is the maximum number of retries to attempt if the request fails. Defaults to 0 (no retries).<br><br>@default 0|
|» » » » » baseDelaySeconds|body|number|true|This is the base delay in seconds. For linear backoff, this is the delay between each retry. For exponential backoff, this is the initial delay.|
|» » » » » excludedStatusCodes|body|[object]|false|This is the excluded status codes. If the response status code is in this list, the request will not be retried.<br>By default, the request will be retried for any non-2xx status code.|
|» » » keypadInputPlan|body|[KeypadInputPlan](#schemakeypadinputplan)|false|none|
|» » number|body|string|false|This is the number of the customer.|
|» » sipUri|body|string|false|This is the SIP URI of the customer.|
|» » name|body|string|false|This is the name of the customer. This is just for your own reference.<br><br>For SIP inbound calls, this is extracted from the `From` SIP header with format `"Display Name" <sip:username@domain>`.|

<h3 id="create-call-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Client/policy failure (limits, validation, missing resources)|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|System failure (database, queue, or internal infra)|None|

<h3 id="create-call-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **201**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|[Call](#schemacall)|false|none|none|
|*oneOf*|[CallBatchResponse](#schemacallbatchresponse)|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearer
</aside>

## Get Call

<a id="opIdCallController_findOne"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vapi.ai/call/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /call/{id}`

<h3 id="get-call-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|The unique identifier for the resource.|

## Delete Call

<a id="opIdCallController_deleteCallData"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.vapi.ai/call/{id}' \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "ids": [
      "string"
    ]
  }'
```

`DELETE /call/{id}`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ids": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="delete-call-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[DeleteCallDTO](#schemadeletecalldto)|true|none|
|» ids|body|[string]|false|These are the Call IDs to be bulk deleted.<br>If provided, the call ID if any in the request query will be ignored<br>When requesting a bulk delete, updates when a call is deleted will be sent as a webhook to the server URL configured in the Org settings.<br>It may take up to a few hours to complete the bulk delete, and will be asynchronous.|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[Call](#schemacall)|
|503|Service Unavailable|Failed to erase call recordings; the call was not deleted. Retry the request.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearer
</aside>

## Update Call

<a id="opIdCallController_update"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vapi.ai/call/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string"
  }'
```

`PATCH /call/{id}`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="update-call-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|The unique identifier for the resource.|
|body|body|[UpdateCallDTO](#schemaupdatecalldto)|true|none|
|» name|body|string|false|This is the name of the call. This is just for your own reference.|

## Download Call Mono Recording

<a id="opIdCallArtifactController_monoRecordingDownload"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vapi.ai/call/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/mono-recording \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /call/{id}/mono-recording`

<h3 id="download-call-mono-recording-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|Call ID|

<h3 id="download-call-mono-recording-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||None|
|302|Found|Redirect to a short-lived presigned URL for the recording.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized — missing or invalid API token.|None|
|404|Not Found|Artifact not found.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearer
</aside>

<h1 id="vapi-api-chats">Chats</h1>

## List Chats

<a id="opIdChatController_listChats"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.vapi.ai/chat \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /chat`

<h3 id="list-chats-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|query|string|false|This is the unique identifier for the chat to filter by.|
|assistantId|query|string|false|This is the unique identifier for the assistant that will be used for the chat.|
|assistantIdAny|query|string|false|Filter by multiple assistant IDs. Provide as comma-separated values.|
|squadId|query|string|false|This is the unique identifier for the squad that will be used for the chat.|
|sessionId|query|string|false|This is the unique identifier for the session that will be used for the chat.|
|previousChatId|query|string|false|This is the unique identifier for the previous chat to filter by.|
|idAny|query|string|false|Filter by multiple chat IDs. Provide as comma-separated values.|
|page|query|number|false|This is the page number to return. Defaults to 1.|
|sortOrder|query|string|false|This is the sort order for pagination. Defaults to 'DESC'.|
|sortBy|query|string|false|This is the column to sort by. Defaults to 'createdAt'.|
|limit|query|number|false|This is the maximum number of items to return. Defaults to 100.|
|createdAtGt|query|string(date-time)|false|This will return items where the createdAt is greater than the specified value.|
|createdAtLt|query|string(date-time)|false|This will return items where the createdAt is less than the specified value.|
|createdAtGe|query|string(date-time)|false|This will return items where the createdAt is greater than or equal to the specified value.|
|createdAtLe|query|string(date-time)|false|This will return items where the createdAt is less than or equal to the specified value.|
|updatedAtGt|query|string(date-time)|false|This will return items where the updatedAt is greater than the specified value.|
|updatedAtLt|query|string(date-time)|false|This will return items where the updatedAt is less than the specified value.|
|updatedAtGe|query|string(date-time)|false|This will return items where the updatedAt is greater than or equal to the specified value.|
|updatedAtLe|query|string(date-time)|false|This will return items where the updatedAt is less than or equal to the specified value.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sortOrder|ASC|
|sortOrder|DESC|
|sortBy|createdAt|
|sortBy|duration|
|sortBy|cost|


`POST /chat`

Creates a new chat with optional SMS delivery via transport field. Requires at least one of: assistantId/assistant, sessionId, or previousChatId. Note: sessionId and previousChatId are mutually exclusive. Transport field enables SMS delivery with two modes: (1) New conversation - provide transport.phoneNumberId and transport.customer to create a new session, (2) Existing conversation - provide sessionId to use existing session data. Cannot specify both sessionId and transport fields together. The transport.useLLMGeneratedMessageForOutbound flag controls whether input is processed by LLM (true, default) or forwarded directly as SMS (false).

|» » backgroundSpeechDenoisingPlan|body|object|false|This enables filtering of noise and background speech while the user is talking.<br><br>Features:<br>- Smart denoising using Krisp<br>- Fourier denoising<br><br>Smart denoising can be combined with or used independently of Fourier denoising.<br><br>Order of precedence:<br>- Smart denoising<br>- Fourier denoising|
|» » » smartDenoisingPlan|body|object|false|Whether smart denoising using Krisp is enabled.|
|» » » » enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether smart denoising using Krisp is enabled.|
|» » » fourierDenoisingPlan|body|object|false|Whether Fourier denoising is enabled. Note that this is experimental and may not work as expected.<br><br>This can be combined with smart denoising, and will be run afterwards.|
|» » » » enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether Fourier denoising is enabled. Note that this is experimental and may not work as expected.|
|» » » » mediaDetectionEnabled|body|boolean|false|Whether automatic media detection is enabled. When enabled, the filter will automatically<br>detect consistent background TV/music/radio and switch to more aggressive filtering settings.<br>Only applies when enabled is true.|
|» » » » staticThreshold|body|number|false|Static threshold in dB used as fallback when no baseline is established.|
|» » » » baselineOffsetDb|body|number|false|How far below the rolling baseline to filter audio, in dB.<br>Lower values (e.g., -10) are more aggressive, higher values (e.g., -20) are more conservative.|
|» » » » windowSizeMs|body|number|false|Rolling window size in milliseconds for calculating the audio baseline.<br>Larger windows adapt more slowly but are more stable.|
|» » » » baselinePercentile|body|number|false|Percentile to use for baseline calculation (1-99).<br>Higher percentiles (e.g., 85) focus on louder speech, lower percentiles (e.g., 50) include quieter speech.|
|» » analysisPlan|body|object|false|**Deprecated.** This is the plan for analysis of assistant's calls. Stored in `call.analysis`.|
|» » » minMessagesThreshold|body|number|false|**Deprecated.** The minimum number of messages required to run the analysis plan.<br>If the number of messages is less than this, analysis will be skipped.<br><br>@default 2|
|» » » summaryPlan|body|object|false|**Deprecated.** This is the plan for generating the summary of the call. This outputs to `call.analysis.summary`.|
|» » » » messages|body|[object]|false|These are the messages used to generate the summary.<br><br>@default: ```<br>[<br>  {<br>    "role": "system",<br>    "content": "You are an expert note-taker. DO NOT return anything except the summary."<br>  },<br>  {<br>    "role": "user",<br>    "content": "Here is the transcript:\n\n{{transcript}}\n\n. Here is the ended reason of the call:\n\n{{endedReason}}\n\n"<br>  }<br>]```<br><br>You can customize by providing any messages you want.<br><br>Here are the template variables available:<br>- {{transcript}}: The transcript of the call from `call.artifact.transcript` <br>- {{systemPrompt}}: The system prompt of the call from `assistant.model.messages[type=system].content` <br>- {{messages}}: The messages of the call from `assistant.model.messages` <br>- {{endedReason}}: The ended reason of the call from `call.endedReason`|
|» » » » enabled|body|boolean|false|This determines whether a summary is generated and stored in `call.analysis.summary`. Defaults to true.<br><br>Usage:<br>- If you want to disable the summary, set this to false.<br><br>@default true|
|» » » » timeoutSeconds|body|number|false|This is how long the request is tried before giving up. Note, this will delay the end of call report in cases where model is slow to respond.<br><br>@default 5 seconds|

Here is the ended reason of the call:\n\n{{endedReason}}\n\n"<br>  }<br>]```<br><br>You can customize by providing any messages you want.<br><br>Here are the template variables available:<br>- {{transcript}}: the transcript of the call from `call.artifact.transcript`- {{systemPrompt}}: the system prompt of the call from `assistant.model.messages[type=system].content`- {{messages}}: the messages of the call from `assistant.model.messages`- {{schema}}: the schema of the structured data from `structuredDataPlan.schema`- {{endedReason}}: the ended reason of the call from `call.endedReason`|

|» » » » timeoutSeconds|body|number|false|This is how long the request is tried before giving up. |» » » » rubric|body|string|false|This enforces the rubric of the evaluation. The output is stored in `call.analysis.successEvaluation`.<br><br>Options include:<br>- 'NumericScale': A scale of 1 to 10.<br>- 'DescriptiveScale': A scale of Excellent, Good, Fair, Poor.<br>- 'Checklist': A checklist of criteria and their status.<br>- 'Matrix': A grid that evaluates multiple criteria across different performance levels.<br>- 'PercentageScale': A scale of 0% to 100%.<br>- 'LikertScale': A scale of Strongly Agree, Agree, Neutral, Disagree, Strongly Disagree.<br>- 'AutomaticRubric': Automatically break down evaluation into several criteria, each with its own score.<br>- 'PassFail': A simple 'true' if call passed, 'false' if not.<br><br>Default is 'PassFail'.|
|» » » » messages|body|[object]|false|These are the messages used to generate the success evaluation.<br><br>@default: ```<br>[<br>  {<br>    "role": "system",<br>    "content": "You are an expert call evaluator. DO NOT return anything except the result.\n\nRubric:\\n{{rubric}}\n\nOnly respond with the result."<br>  },<br>  {<br>    "role": "user",<br>    "content": "Here is the transcript:\n\n{{transcript}}\n\n"<br>  },<br>  {<br>    "role": "user",<br>    "content": "Here was the system prompt of the call:\n\n{{systemPrompt}}\n\n. Here is the ended reason of the call:\n\n{{endedReason}}\n\n"<br>  }<br>]```<br><br>You can customize by providing any messages you want.<br><br>Here are the template variables available:<br>- {{transcript}}: the transcript of the call from `call.artifact.transcript`- {{systemPrompt}}: the system prompt of the call from `assistant.model.messages[type=system].content`- {{messages}}: the messages of the call from `assistant.model.messages`- {{rubric}}: the rubric of the success evaluation from `successEvaluationPlan.rubric`- {{endedReason}}: the ended reason of the call from `call.endedReason`|
|» » » » enabled|body|boolean|false|This determines whether a success evaluation is generated and stored in `call.analysis.successEvaluation`. Defaults to true.<br><br>Usage:<br>- If you want to disable the success evaluation, set this to false.<br><br>@default true|
|» » » » timeoutSeconds|body|number|false|This is how long the request is tried before giving up. |» » » recordingEnabled|body|boolean|false|This determines whether assistant's calls are recorded. Defaults to true.<br><br>Usage:<br>- If you don't want to record the calls, set this to false.<br>- If you want to record the calls when `assistant.hipaaEnabled` (deprecated) or `assistant.compliancePlan.hipaaEnabled` explicity set this to true and make sure to provide S3 or GCP credentials on the Provider Credentials page in the Dashboard.<br><br>You can find the recording at `call.artifact.recordingUrl` and `call.artifact.stereoRecordingUrl` after the call is ended.<br><br>@default true|
|» » » recordingFormat|body|string|false|This determines the format of the recording. Defaults to `wav;l16`.<br><br>@default 'wav;l16'|
|» » » recordingUseCustomStorageEnabled|body|boolean|false|This determines whether to use custom storage (S3 or GCP) for call recordings when storage credentials are configured.<br><br>When set to false, recordings will be stored on Vapi's storage instead of your custom storage, even if you have custom storage credentials configured.<br><br>Usage:<br>- Set to false if you have custom storage configured but want to store recordings on Vapi's storage for this assistant.<br>- Set to true (or leave unset) to use your custom storage for recordings when available.<br><br>If your organization has ZDR (zero data retention) or PCI enabled, recordings are never written to Vapi storage. In that case, false means "do not use my custom storage", so nothing is stored at all.<br><br>@default true|
|» » » videoRecordingEnabled|body|boolean|false|This determines whether the video is recorded during the call. Defaults to false. Only relevant for `webCall` type.<br><br>You can find the video recording at `call.artifact.videoRecordingUrl` after the call is ended.<br><br>@default false|
|» » » fullMessageHistoryEnabled|body|boolean|false|This determines whether the artifact contains the full message history, even after handoff context engineering. Defaults to false.|
|» » » pcapEnabled|body|boolean|false|This determines whether the SIP packet capture is enabled. Defaults to true. Only relevant for `phone` type calls where phone number's provider is `vapi` or `byo-phone-number`.<br><br>You can find the packet capture at `call.artifact.pcapUrl` after the call is ended.<br><br>@default true|
|» » » pcapS3PathPrefix|body|string|false|This is the path where the SIP packet capture will be uploaded. This is only used if you have provided S3 or GCP credentials on the Provider Credentials page in the Dashboard.<br><br>If credential.s3PathPrefix or credential.bucketPlan.path is set, this will append to it.<br><br>Usage:<br>- If you want to upload the packet capture to a specific path, set this to the path. Example: `/my-assistant-captures`.<br>- If you want to upload the packet capture to the root of the bucket, set this to `/`.<br><br>@default '/'|
|» » » pcapUseCustomStorageEnabled|body|boolean|false|This determines whether to use custom storage (S3 or GCP) for SIP packet captures when storage credentials are configured.<br><br>When set to false, packet captures will be stored on Vapi's storage instead of your custom storage, even if you have custom storage credentials configured.<br><br>Usage:<br>- Set to false if you have custom storage configured but want to store packet captures on Vapi's storage for this assistant.<br>- Set to true (or leave unset) to use your custom storage for packet captures when available.<br><br>If your organization has ZDR (zero data retention) or PCI enabled, packet captures are never written to Vapi storage. In that case, false means "do not use my custom storage", so nothing is stored at all.<br><br>@default true|
|» » » loggingEnabled|body|boolean|false|This determines whether the call logs are enabled. Defaults to true.<br><br>@default true|
|» » » loggingUseCustomStorageEnabled|body|boolean|false|This determines whether to use custom storage (S3 or GCP) for call logs when storage credentials are configured.<br><br>When set to false, logs will be stored on Vapi's storage instead of your custom storage, even if you have custom storage credentials configured.<br><br>Usage:<br>- Set to false if you have custom storage configured but want to store logs on Vapi's storage for this assistant.<br>- Set to true (or leave unset) to use your custom storage for logs when available.<br><br>If your organization has ZDR (zero data retention) or PCI enabled, logs are never written to Vapi storage. In that case, false means "do not use my custom storage", so nothing is stored at all.<br><br>@default true|

|» » variableValues|body|object|false|These are values that will be used to replace the template variables in the assistant messages and other text-based fields.<br>This uses LiquidJS syntax. https://liquidjs.com/tutorials/intro-to-liquid.html<br><br>So for example, `{{ name }}` will be replaced with the value of `name` in `variableValues`.<br>`{{"now" \| date: "%b %d, %Y, %I:%M %p", "America/New_York"}}` will be replaced with the current date and time in New York.<br> Some VAPI reserved defaults:<br> - *customer* - the customer object|
|» » name|body|string|false|This is the name of the assistant.<br><br>This is required when you want to transfer between assistants in a call.|
|» » voicemailMessage|body|string|false|This is the message that the assistant will say if the call is forwarded to voicemail.<br><br>If unspecified, it will hang up.|
|» » endCallMessage|body|string|false|This is the message that the assistant will say if it ends the call.<br><br>If unspecified, it will hang up without saying anything.|
|» » endCallPhrases|body|[string]|false|This list contains phrases that, if spoken by the assistant, will trigger the call to be hung up. Case insensitive.|
|» » compliancePlan|body|[CompliancePlan](#schemacomplianceplan)|false|none|
|» » metadata|body|object|false|This is for metadata you want to store on the assistant.|
|» » backgroundSpeechDenoisingPlan|body|object|false|This enables filtering of noise and background speech while the user is talking.<br><br>Features:<br>- Smart denoising using Krisp<br>- Fourier denoising<br><br>Smart denoising can be combined with or used independently of Fourier denoising.<br><br>Order of precedence:<br>- Smart denoising<br>- Fourier denoising|
|» » » smartDenoisingPlan|body|object|false|Whether smart denoising using Krisp is enabled.|
|» » » » enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether smart denoising using Krisp is enabled.|
|» » » fourierDenoisingPlan|body|object|false|Whether Fourier denoising is enabled. Note that this is experimental and may not work as expected.<br><br>This can be combined with smart denoising, and will be run afterwards.|
|» » » » enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether Fourier denoising is enabled. Note that this is experimental and may not work as expected.|
|» » » » mediaDetectionEnabled|body|boolean|false|Whether automatic media detection is enabled. When enabled, the filter will automatically<br>detect consistent background TV/music/radio and switch to more aggressive filtering settings.<br>Only applies when enabled is true.|
|» » » » staticThreshold|body|number|false|Static threshold in dB used as fallback when no baseline is established.|
|» » » » baselineOffsetDb|body|number|false|How far below the rolling baseline to filter audio, in dB.<br>Lower values (e.g., -10) are more aggressive, higher values (e.g., -20) are more conservative.|
|» » » » windowSizeMs|body|number|false|Rolling window size in milliseconds for calculating the audio baseline.<br>Larger windows adapt more slowly but are more stable.|
|» » » » baselinePercentile|body|number|false|Percentile to use for baseline calculation (1-99).<br>Higher percentiles (e.g., 85) focus on louder speech, lower percentiles (e.g., 50) include quieter speech.|
|» » analysisPlan|body|object|false|**Deprecated.** This is the plan for analysis of assistant's calls. Stored in `call.analysis`.|
|» » » minMessagesThreshold|body|number|false|**Deprecated.** The minimum number of messages required to run the analysis plan.<br>If the number of messages is less than this, analysis will be skipped.<br><br>@default 2|
|» » » summaryPlan|body|object|false|**Deprecated.** This is the plan for generating the summary of the call. This outputs to `call.analysis.summary`.|
|» » » » messages|body|[object]|false|These are the messages used to generate the summary.<br><br>@default: ```<br>[<br>  {<br>    "role": "system",<br>    "content": "You are an expert note-taker. You will be given a transcript of a call. Summarize the call in 2-3 sentences. DO NOT return anything except the summary."<br>  },<br>  {<br>    "role": "user",<br>    "content": "Here is the transcript:\n\n{{transcript}}\n\n. Here is the ended reason of the call:\n\n{{endedReason}}\n\n"<br>  }<br>]```<br><br>You can customize by providing any messages you want.<br><br>Here are the template variables available:<br>- {{transcript}}: The transcript of the call from `call.artifact.transcript` <br>- {{systemPrompt}}: The system prompt of the call from `assistant.model.messages[type=system].content` <br>- {{messages}}: The messages of the call from `assistant.model.messages` <br>- {{endedReason}}: The ended reason of the call from `call.endedReason`|
|» » » » enabled|body|boolean|false|This determines whether a summary is generated and stored in `call.analysis.summary`. Defaults to true.<br><br>Usage:<br>- If you want to disable the summary, set this to false.<br><br>@default true|
|» » » » timeoutSeconds|body|number|false|This is how long the request is tried before giving up. When request times out, `call.analysis.summary` will be empty.<br><br>Usage:<br>- To guarantee the summary is generated, set this value high. Note, this will delay the end of call report in cases where model is slow to respond.<br><br>@default 5 seconds|
|» » » structuredDataPlan|body|object|false|**Deprecated.** This is the plan for generating the structured data from the call. This outputs to `call.analysis.structuredData`.|
|» » » » messages|body|[object]|false|These are the messages used to generate the structured data.<br><br>@default: ```<br>[<br>  {<br>    "role": "system",<br>    "content": "You are an expert data extractor. Here is the ended reason of the call:\n\n{{endedReason}}\n\n"<br>  }<br>]```<br><br>You can customize by providing any messages you want.<br><br>Here are the template variables available:<br>- {{transcript}}: the transcript of the call from `call.artifact.transcript`- {{systemPrompt}}: the system prompt of the call from `assistant.model.messages[type=system].content`- {{messages}}: the messages of the call from `assistant.model.messages`- {{schema}}: the schema of the structured data from `structuredDataPlan.schema`- {{endedReason}}: the ended reason of the call from `call.endedReason`|
|» » » » enabled|body|boolean|false|This determines whether structured data is generated and stored in `call.analysis.structuredData`. Defaults to false.<br><br>Usage:<br>- If you want to extract structured data, set this to true and provide a `schema`.<br><br>@default false|
|» » » » schema|body|object|false|This is the schema of the structured data. The output is stored in `call.analysis.structuredData`.<br><br>Complete guide on JSON Schema can be found [here](https://ajv.js.org/json-schema.html#json-data-type).|
|» » » » timeoutSeconds|body|number|false|This is how long the request is tried before giving up.
