Your core responsibility is to manage the transfer process efficiently.\n\n## Core Responsibility\n- Facilitate the transfer process by using transferSuccessful or transferCancel tools appropriately\n\n## When to Respond\n- Answer questions about the transfer process or provide summaries when specifically asked by the operator\n- Respond to direct questions about the current transfer situation\n\n## What to Avoid\n- Do not discuss topics unrelated to the transfer\n- Do not engage in general conversation\n- Keep all interactions focused on facilitating the transfer\n\n## Transfer Tools\n- Use transferSuccessful when the transfer should proceed\n- Use transferCancel when the transfer cannot be completed\n\nStay focused on your core responsibility of facilitating transfers.'<br>  }<br>]```<br><br>**Default Behavior:** If you don't provide any messages or don't include a system message as the first message, the default system message above will be automatically added.<br><br>**Override Default:** To replace the default system message, provide your own system message as the first message in the array.<br><br>**Add Context:** You can provide additional messages (user, assistant, etc.) to add context while keeping the default system message, or combine them with your custom system message.|

Use this when you detect a human has answered and is ready to take the call."<br>- `transferCancel`: "Call this function to cancel the transfer when no human answers or transfer should not proceed. <h2 id="tocS_AssistantCustomEndpointingRule">AssistantCustomEndpointingRule</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaassistantcustomendpointingrule"></a>
<a id="schema_AssistantCustomEndpointingRule"></a>
<a id="tocSassistantcustomendpointingrule"></a>
<a id="tocsassistantcustomendpointingrule"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "assistant",
  "regex": "string",
  "regexOptions": [
    {
      "type": "ignore-case",
      "enabled": true
    }
  ],
  "timeoutSeconds": 0
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|This endpointing rule is based on the last assistant message before customer started speaking.<br><br>Flow:<br>- Assistant speaks<br>- Customer starts speaking<br>- Customer transcription comes in<br>- This rule is evaluated on the last assistant message<br>- If a match is found based on `regex`, the endpointing timeout is set to `timeoutSeconds`<br><br>Usage:<br>- If you have yes/no questions in your use case like "are you interested in a loan?", you can set a shorter timeout.<br>- If you have questions where the customer may pause to look up information like "what's my account number?", you can set a longer timeout.|
|regex|string|true|none|This is the regex pattern to match.<br><br>Note:<br>- This works by using the `RegExp.test` method in Node.JS. Eg. `/hello/.test("hello there")` will return `true`.<br><br>Hot tip:<br>- In JavaScript, escape `\` when sending the regex pattern. Eg. `"hello\sthere"` will be sent over the wire as `"hellosthere"`. Send `"hello\\sthere"` instead.<br>- `RegExp.test` does substring matching, so `/cat/.test("I love cats")` will return `true`. To do full string matching, send "^cat$".|
|regexOptions|[[RegexOption](#schemaregexoption)]|false|none|These are the options for the regex match. Defaults to all disabled.<br><br>@default []|
|timeoutSeconds|number|true|none|This is the endpointing timeout in seconds, if the rule is matched.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|assistant|

Eg. `"hello\sthere"` will be sent over the wire as `"hellosthere"`. Send `"hello\\sthere"` instead.<br>- `RegExp.test` does substring matching, so `/cat/.test("I love cats")` will return `true`. To do full string matching, send "^cat$".|

To do full string matching, send "^cat$".|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|provider|string|true|none|This is the provider for the smart endpointing plan.|
|waitFunction|string|false|none|This expression describes how long the bot will wait to start speaking based on the likelihood that the user has reached an endpoint.<br><br>This is a millisecond valued function. It maps probabilities (real numbers on [0,1]) to milliseconds that the bot should wait before speaking ([0, \infty]). Any negative values that are returned are set to zero (the bot can't start talking in the past).<br><br>A probability of zero represents very high confidence that the caller has stopped speaking, and would like the bot to speak to them. A probability of one represents very high confidence that the caller is still speaking.<br><br>Under the hood, this is parsed into a mathjs expression. Whatever you use to write your expression needs to be valid with respect to mathjs<br><br>@default "20 + 500 * sqrt(x) + 2500 * x^3"|

<h2 id="tocS_TranscriptionEndpointingPlan">TranscriptionEndpointingPlan</h2>

```json
{
  "onPunctuationSeconds": 0.1,
  "onNoPunctuationSeconds": 1.5,
  "onNumberSeconds": 0.5
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|onPunctuationSeconds|number|false|none|The minimum number of seconds to wait after transcription ending with punctuation before sending a request to the model. Defaults to 0.1.<br><br>This setting exists because the transcriber punctuates the transcription when it's more confident that customer has completed a thought.<br><br>@default 0.1|
|onNoPunctuationSeconds|number|false|none|The minimum number of seconds to wait after transcription ending without punctuation before sending a request to the model. Defaults to 1.5.<br><br>This setting exists to catch the cases where the transcriber was not confident enough to punctuate the transcription, but the customer is done and has been silent for a long time.<br><br>@default 1.5|
|onNumberSeconds|number|false|none|The minimum number of seconds to wait after transcription ending with a number before sending a request to the model. Defaults to 0.4.<br><br>This setting exists because the transcriber will sometimes punctuate the transcription ending with a number, even though the customer hasn't uttered the full number. This happens commonly for long numbers when the customer reads the number in chunks.<br><br>@default 0.5|

<h2 id="tocS_StartSpeakingPlan">StartSpeakingPlan</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemastartspeakingplan"></a>

```json
{
  "waitSeconds": 0.4,
  "smartEndpointingEnabled": false,
  "smartEndpointingPlan": {
    "provider": "vapi"
  },
  "customEndpointingRules": [
    {
      "type": "assistant",
      "regex": "string",
      "regexOptions": [
        {
          "type": "ignore-case",
          "enabled": true
        }
      ],
      "timeoutSeconds": 0
    }
  ],
  "transcriptionEndpointingPlan": {
    "onPunctuationSeconds": 0.1,
    "onNoPunctuationSeconds": 1.5,
    "onNumberSeconds": 0.5
  }
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|waitSeconds|number|false|none|This is how long assistant waits before speaking. Defaults to 0.4.<br><br>This is the minimum it will wait but if there is latency is the pipeline, this minimum will be exceeded. This is intended as a stopgap in case the pipeline is moving too fast.<br><br>Example:<br>- If model generates tokens and voice generates bytes within 100ms, the pipeline still waits 300ms before outputting speech.<br><br>Usage:<br>- If the customer is taking long pauses, set this to a higher value.<br>- If the assistant is accidentally jumping in too much, set this to a higher value.<br><br>@default 0.4|
|smartEndpointingEnabled|boolean \| string|false|none|**Deprecated.**|
|smartEndpointingPlan|[VapiSmartEndpointingPlan](#schemavapismartendpointingplan) \| [LivekitSmartEndpointingPlan](#schemalivekitsmartendpointingplan) \| [CustomEndpointingModelSmartEndpointingPlan](#schemacustomendpointingmodelsmartendpointingplan)|false|none|This is the plan for smart endpointing. Pick between Vapi smart endpointing, LiveKit, or custom endpointing model (or nothing). We strongly recommend using livekit endpointing when working in English. LiveKit endpointing is not supported in other languages, yet.<br><br>If this is set, it will override and take precedence over `transcriptionEndpointingPlan`.<br>This plan will still be overridden by any matching `customEndpointingRules`.<br><br>If this is not set, the system will automatically use the transcriber's built-in endpointing capabilities if available.|
|customEndpointingRules|[[AssistantCustomEndpointingRule](#schemaassistantcustomendpointingrule) \| [CustomerCustomEndpointingRule](#schemacustomercustomendpointingrule) \| [BothCustomEndpointingRule](#schemabothcustomendpointingrule)]|false|none|These are the custom endpointing rules to set an endpointing timeout based on a regex on the customer's speech or the assistant's last message.<br><br>Usage:<br>- If you have yes/no questions like "are you interested in a loan?", you can set a shorter timeout.<br>- If you have questions where the customer may pause to look up information like "what's my account number?", you can set a longer timeout.<br>- If you want to wait longer while customer is enumerating a list of numbers, you can set a longer timeout.<br><br>These rules have the highest precedence and will override both `smartEndpointingPlan` and `transcriptionEndpointingPlan` when a rule is matched.<br><br>The rules are evaluated in order and the first one that matches will be used.<br><br>Order of precedence for endpointing:<br>1. customEndpointingRules (if any match)<br>2. smartEndpointingPlan (if set)<br>3. transcriptionEndpointingPlan<br><br>@default []|
|transcriptionEndpointingPlan|object|false|none|This determines how a customer speech is considered done (endpointing) using the transcription of customer's speech.<br><br>Once an endpoint is triggered, the request is sent to `assistant.model`.<br><br>Note: This plan is only used if `smartEndpointingPlan` is not set and transcriber does not have built-in endpointing capabilities. If both are provided, `smartEndpointingPlan` takes precedence.<br>This plan will also be overridden by any matching `customEndpointingRules`.|

<h2 id="tocS_FourierDenoisingPlan">FourierDenoisingPlan</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemafourierdenoisingplan"></a>
<a id="schema_FourierDenoisingPlan"></a>
<a id="tocSfourierdenoisingplan"></a>
<a id="tocsfourierdenoisingplan"></a>

```json
{
  "enabled": false,
  "mediaDetectionEnabled": true,
  "staticThreshold": -35,
  "baselineOffsetDb": -15,
  "windowSizeMs": 3000,
  "baselinePercentile": 85
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enabled|boolean|false|none|Whether Fourier denoising is enabled. Note that this is experimental and may not work as expected.|
|mediaDetectionEnabled|boolean|false|none|Whether automatic media detection is enabled. When enabled, the filter will automatically<br>detect consistent background TV/music/radio and switch to more aggressive filtering settings.<br>Only applies when enabled is true.|
|staticThreshold|number|false|none|Static threshold in dB used as fallback when no baseline is established.|
|baselineOffsetDb|number|false|none|How far below the rolling baseline to filter audio, in dB.<br>Lower values (e.g., -10) are more aggressive, higher values (e.g., -20) are more conservative.|
|windowSizeMs|number|false|none|Rolling window size in milliseconds for calculating the audio baseline.<br>Larger windows adapt more slowly but are more stable.|
|baselinePercentile|number|false|none|Percentile to use for baseline calculation (1-99).<br>Higher percentiles (e.g., 85) focus on louder speech, lower percentiles (e.g., 50) include quieter speech.|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|smartDenoisingPlan|object|false|none|Whether smart denoising using Krisp is enabled.|
|fourierDenoisingPlan|object|false|none|Whether Fourier denoising is enabled. Note that this is experimental and may not work as expected.<br><br>This can be combined with smart denoising, and will be run afterwards.|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|false|none|Optional name for the transfer assistant|
|model|object|true|none|Model configuration for the transfer assistant|
|voice|[AzureVoice](#schemaazurevoice) \| [CartesiaVoice](#schemacartesiavoice) \| [CustomVoice](#schemacustomvoice) \| [DeepgramVoice](#schemadeepgramvoice) \| [ElevenLabsVoice](#schemaelevenlabsvoice) \| [HumeVoice](#schemahumevoice) \| [LMNTVoice](#schemalmntvoice) \| [NeuphonicVoice](#schemaneuphonicvoice) \| [OpenAIVoice](#schemaopenaivoice) \| [PlayHTVoice](#schemaplayhtvoice) \| [WellSaidVoice](#schemawellsaidvoice) \| [RimeAIVoice](#schemarimeaivoice) \| [SmallestAIVoice](#schemasmallestaivoice) \| [VapiVoice](#schemavapivoice) \| [SesameVoice](#schemasesamevoice) \| [InworldVoice](#schemainworldvoice) \| [MinimaxVoice](#schemaminimaxvoice) \| [XaiVoice](#schemaxaivoice) \| [MicrosoftVoice](#schemamicrosoftvoice)|false|none|These are the options for the transfer assistant's voice.|
|transcriber|[AssemblyAITranscriber](#schemaassemblyaitranscriber) \| [AzureSpeechTranscriber](#schemaazurespeechtranscriber) \| [CustomTranscriber](#schemacustomtranscriber) \| [DeepgramTranscriber](#schemadeepgramtranscriber) \| [ElevenLabsTranscriber](#schemaelevenlabstranscriber) \| [GladiaTranscriber](#schemagladiatranscriber) \| [GoogleTranscriber](#schemagoogletranscriber) \| [SpeechmaticsTranscriber](#schemaspeechmaticstranscriber) \| [TalkscriberTranscriber](#schematalkscribertranscriber) \| [OpenAITranscriber](#schemaopenaitranscriber) \| [CartesiaTranscriber](#schemacartesiatranscriber) \| [SonioxTranscriber](#schemasonioxtranscriber) \| [XaiTranscriber](#schemaxaitranscriber) \| [VapiTranscriber](#schemavapitranscriber)|false|none|These are the options for the transfer assistant's transcriber.|
|firstMessage|string|false|none|This is the first message that the transfer assistant will say.<br>This can also be a URL to a custom audio file.<br><br>If unspecified, assistant will wait for user to speak and use the model to respond once they speak.|
|backgroundSound|string \| string(uri)|false|none|This is the background sound in the transfer assistant call. Default for phone calls is 'office' and default for web calls is 'off'.<br>You can also provide a custom sound by providing a URL to an audio file.|
|startSpeakingPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan for when the transfer assistant should start talking.<br><br>You should configure this if the transfer assistant needs different endpointing behavior than the base assistant.<br><br>If this is not set, the transfer assistant will inherit the start speaking plan from the base assistant.|
|firstMessageMode|string|false|none|This is the mode for the first message. Default is 'assistant-speaks-first'.<br><br>Use:<br>- 'assistant-speaks-first' to have the assistant speak first.<br>- 'assistant-waits-for-user' to have the assistant wait for the user to speak first.<br>- 'assistant-speaks-first-with-model-generated-message' to have the assistant speak first with a message generated by the model based on the conversation state.<br><br>@default 'assistant-speaks-first'|
|maxDurationSeconds|number|false|none|This is the maximum duration in seconds for the transfer assistant conversation.<br>After this time, the transfer will be cancelled automatically.<br>@default 120|
|assistantHooksInheritEnabled|boolean|false|none|This decides whether the transfer assistant runs the main assistant's hooks on the operator leg of a `warm-transfer-experimental` transfer. The operator is the "customer" there. When unset or `true`, the transfer assistant runs all of the main assistant's hooks, plus `hooks`. When `false`, it runs only `hooks`, plus the main assistant's `call.ending` hooks. An `endCall` in an inherited `customer.speech.timeout` hook ends the whole call when the operator is silent, so set this to `false` to stop that.|
|hooks|[[CallHookAssistantSpeechInterrupted](#schemacallhookassistantspeechinterrupted) \| [CallHookCustomerSpeechInterrupted](#schemacallhookcustomerspeechinterrupted) \| [CallHookCustomerSpeechTimeout](#schemacallhookcustomerspeechtimeout) \| [CallHookModelResponseTimeout](#schemacallhookmodelresponsetimeout) \| [CallHookTranscriberEndpointedSpeechLowConfidence](#schemacallhooktranscriberendpointedspeechlowconfidence)]|false|none|These are the hooks the transfer assistant runs on the operator leg of a `warm-transfer-experimental` transfer. The operator is the "customer" there, so `customer.speech.timeout` fires on operator silence. Whether the main assistant's other hooks also run on the operator leg depends on `assistantHooksInheritEnabled`. These hooks run after them. `call.ending` and `call.timeElapsed` are not allowed here. The main assistant's `call.ending` hooks are kept automatically. Time-elapsed hooks are not armed on the operator leg. An `endCall` tool in these hooks ends the whole call, not only the operator leg. A `tool` action must carry an inline `tool`, because `toolId` is not resolved for the transfer assistant.|
|backgroundSpeechDenoisingPlan|object|false|none|This enables filtering of noise and background speech while the user is talking.<br><br>Features:<br>- Smart denoising using Krisp<br>- Fourier denoising<br><br>Smart denoising can be combined with or used independently of Fourier denoising.<br><br>Order of precedence:<br>- Smart denoising<br>- Fourier denoising|
|silenceTimeoutSeconds|number|false|none|This is the number of seconds of silence to wait before ending the call. Defaults to 30.<br><br>@default 30|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|firstMessageMode|assistant-speaks-first|
|firstMessageMode|assistant-speaks-first-with-model-generated-message|
|firstMessageMode|assistant-waits-for-user|

```json
  }

```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|messages|[[ToolMessageStart](#schematoolmessagestart) \| [ToolMessageComplete](#schematoolmessagecomplete) \| [ToolMessageFailed](#schematoolmessagefailed) \| [ToolMessageDelayed](#schematoolmessagedelayed)]|false|none|Messages spoken while the tool is running. Multiple request-start messages are variants. For request-response-delayed, same timing means variants and different timings mean staged updates.|
|type|string|true|none|The type of tool. "transferCancel" for Transfer Cancel tool. This tool can only be used during warm-transfer-experimental by the transfer assistant to cancel an ongoing transfer and return the call back to the original assistant when the transfer cannot be completed.|
|rejectionPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan to reject a tool call based on the conversation state.<br><br>// Example 1: Reject endCall if user didn't say goodbye<br>```json<br>{<br>  conditions: [{<br>    type: 'regex',<br>    regex: '(?i)\\b(bye\|goodbye\|farewell\|see you later\|take care)\\b',<br>    target: { position: -1, role: 'user' },<br>    negate: true  // Reject if pattern does NOT match<br>  }]<br>}<br>```<br><br>// Example 2: Reject transfer if user is actually asking a question<br>```json<br>{<br>  conditions: [{<br>    type: 'regex',<br>    regex: '\\?',<br>    target: { position: -1, role: 'user' }<br>  }]<br>}<br>```<br><br>// Example 3: Reject transfer if user didn't mention transfer recently<br>```json<br>{<br>  conditions: [{<br>    type: 'liquid',<br>    liquid: `{% assign recentMessages = messages \| last: 5 %}<br>{% assign userMessages = recentMessages \| where: 'role', 'user' %}<br>{% assign mentioned = false %}<br>{% for msg in userMessages %}<br>  {% if msg.content contains 'transfer' or msg.content contains 'connect' or msg.content contains 'speak to' %}<br>    {% assign mentioned = true %}<br>    {% break %}<br>  {% endif %}<br>{% endfor %}<br>{% if mentioned %}<br>  false<br>{% else %}<br>  true<br>{% endif %}`<br>  }]<br>}<br>```<br><br>// Example 4: Reject endCall if the bot is looping and trying to exit<br>```json<br>{<br>  conditions: [{<br>    type: 'liquid',<br>    liquid: `{% assign recentMessages = messages \| last: 6 %}<br>{% assign userMessages = recentMessages \| where: 'role', 'user' \| reverse %}<br>{% if userMessages.size < 3 %}<br>  false<br>{% else %}<br>  {% assign msg1 = userMessages[0].content \| downcase %}<br>  {% assign msg2 = userMessages[1].content \| downcase %}<br>  {% assign msg3 = userMessages[2].content \| downcase %}<br>  {% comment %} Check for repetitive messages {% endcomment %}<br>  {% if msg1 == msg2 or msg1 == msg3 or msg2 == msg3 %}<br>    true<br>  {% comment %} Check for common loop phrases {% endcomment %}<br>  {% elsif msg1 contains 'cool thanks' or msg2 contains 'cool thanks' or msg3 contains 'cool thanks' %}<br>    true<br>  {% elsif msg1 contains 'okay thanks' or msg2 contains 'okay thanks' or msg3 contains 'okay thanks' %}<br>    true<br>  {% elsif msg1 contains 'got it' or msg2 contains 'got it' or msg3 contains 'got it' %}<br>    true<br>  {% else %}<br>    false<br>  {% endif %}<br>{% endif %}`<br>  }]<br>}<br>```|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|transferCancel|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|mode|string|true|none|This configures how transfer is executed and the experience of the destination party receiving the call.<br><br>Usage:<br>- `blind-transfer`: The assistant forwards the call to the destination without any message or summary.<br>- `blind-transfer-add-summary-to-sip-header`: The assistant forwards the call to the destination and adds a SIP header X-Transfer-Summary to the call to include the summary.<br>- `warm-transfer-say-message`: The assistant dials the destination, delivers the `message` to the destination party, connects the customer, and leaves the call.<br>- `warm-transfer-say-summary`: The assistant dials the destination, provides a summary of the call to the destination party, connects the customer, and leaves the call.<br>- `warm-transfer-wait-for-operator-to-speak-first-and-then-say-message`: The assistant dials the destination, waits for the operator to speak, delivers the `message` to the destination party, and then connects the customer.<br>- `warm-transfer-wait-for-operator-to-speak-first-and-then-say-summary`: The assistant dials the destination, waits for the operator to speak, provides a summary of the call to the destination party, and then connects the customer.<br>- `warm-transfer-twiml`: The assistant dials the destination, executes the twiml instructions on the destination call leg, connects the customer, and leaves the call.<br>- `warm-transfer-experimental`: The assistant puts the customer on hold, dials the destination, and if the destination answers (and is human), delivers a message or summary before connecting the customer. If the destination is unreachable or not human (e.g., with voicemail detection), the assistant delivers the `fallbackMessage` to the customer and optionally ends the call.<br><br>@default 'blind-transfer'|
|message|string \| [CustomMessage](#schemacustommessage)|false|none|This is the message the assistant will deliver to the destination party before connecting the customer.<br><br>Usage:<br>- Used only when `mode` is `blind-transfer-add-summary-to-sip-header`, `warm-transfer-say-message`, `warm-transfer-wait-for-operator-to-speak-first-and-then-say-message`, or `warm-transfer-experimental`.|
|timeout|number|false|none|This is the timeout in seconds for the warm-transfer-wait-for-operator-to-speak-first-and-then-say-message/summary<br><br>@default 60|
|sipVerb|object|false|none|This specifies the SIP verb to use while transferring the call.<br>- 'refer': Uses SIP REFER to transfer the call (default)<br>- 'bye': Ends current call with SIP BYE<br>- 'dial': Uses SIP DIAL to transfer the call|
|dialTimeout|number|false|none|This sets the timeout for the dial operation in seconds. This is the duration the call will ring before timing out.<br><br>Only applicable when `sipVerb='dial'`. Not applicable for SIP REFER or BYE.<br><br>@default 60|
|holdAudioUrl|string|false|none|This is the URL to an audio file played while the customer is on hold during transfer.<br><br>Usage:<br>- Used only when `mode` is `warm-transfer-experimental`.<br>- Used when transferring calls to play hold audio for the customer.<br>- Must be a publicly accessible URL to an audio file.<br>- Supported formats: MP3 and WAV.<br>- If not provided, the default hold audio will be used.|
|transferCompleteAudioUrl|string|false|none|This is the URL to an audio file played after the warm transfer message or summary is delivered to the destination party.<br>It can be used to play a custom sound like 'beep' to notify that the transfer is complete.<br><br>Usage:<br>- Used only when `mode` is `warm-transfer-experimental`.<br>- Used when transferring calls to play hold audio for the destination party.<br>- Must be a publicly accessible URL to an audio file.<br>- Supported formats: MP3 and WAV.|
|contextEngineeringPlan|[ContextEngineeringPlanLastNMessages](#schemacontextengineeringplanlastnmessages) \| [ContextEngineeringPlanNone](#schemacontextengineeringplannone) \| [ContextEngineeringPlanAll](#schemacontextengineeringplanall)|false|none|This is the plan for manipulating the message context before initiating the warm transfer.<br>Usage:<br>- Used only when `mode` is `warm-transfer-experimental`.<br>- These messages will automatically be added to the transferAssistant's system message.<br>- If 'none', we will not add any transcript to the transferAssistant's system message.<br>- If you want to provide your own messages, use transferAssistant.model.messages instead.<br><br>@default { type: 'all' }|
|twiml|string|false|none|This is the TwiML instructions to execute on the destination call leg before connecting the customer.<br><br>Usage:<br>- Used only when `mode` is `warm-transfer-twiml`.<br>- Supports only `Play`, `Say`, `Gather`, `Hangup` and `Pause` verbs.<br>- Maximum length is 4096 characters.<br><br>Example:<br>```<br><Say voice="alice" language="en-US">Hello, transferring a customer to you.</Say><br><Pause length="2"/><br><Say>They called about billing questions.</Say><br>```|
|summaryPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan for generating a summary of the call to present to the destination party.<br><br>Usage:<br>- Used only when `mode` is `blind-transfer-add-summary-to-sip-header` or `warm-transfer-say-summary` or `warm-transfer-wait-for-operator-to-speak-first-and-then-say-summary` or `warm-transfer-experimental`.|
|sipHeadersInReferToEnabled|boolean|false|none|This flag includes the sipHeaders from above in the refer to sip uri as url encoded query params.<br><br>@default false|
|fallbackPlan|object|false|none|This configures the fallback plan when the transfer fails (destination unreachable, busy, or not human).<br><br>Usage:<br>- Used when `mode` is `warm-transfer-experimental`. If not provided, a default message will be used.<br>- Used for SIP cold transfers (`blind-transfer` modes) when transfer outcome detection and fallback<br>  are enabled for the organization: on a failed transfer, the assistant speaks `message`, then ends<br>  the call or continues with the customer per `endCallEnabled`.|

<h2 id="tocS_TransferDestinationNumber">TransferDestinationNumber</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematransferdestinationnumber"></a>
<a id="schema_TransferDestinationNumber"></a>
<a id="tocStransferdestinationnumber"></a>
<a id="tocstransferdestinationnumber"></a>

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "type": "number",
  "numberE164CheckEnabled": true,
  "number": "string",
  "extension": "string",
  "callerId": "string",
  "transferPlan": {
    "mode": "blind-transfer",
    "message": "string",
    "timeout": 60,
    "sipVerb": "refer",
    "dialTimeout": 60,
    "holdAudioUrl": "string",
    "transferCompleteAudioUrl": "string",
    "contextEngineeringPlan": {
      "type": "lastNMessages",
      "maxMessages": 0
    },
    "twiml": "string",
    "summaryPlan": {
      "messages": [
        {}
      ],
      "enabled": true,
      "timeoutSeconds": 1
    },
    "sipHeadersInReferToEnabled": true,
    "fallbackPlan": {
      "message": "string",
      "endCallEnabled": true
    }
  },
  "name": "string",
  "description": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|message|string \| [CustomMessage](#schemacustommessage)|false|none|This is spoken to the customer before connecting them to the destination.<br><br>Usage:<br>- If this is not provided and transfer tool messages is not provided, default is "Transferring the call now".<br>- If set to "", nothing is spoken. This is useful when you want to silently transfer. This is especially useful when transferring between assistants in a squad. In this scenario, you likely also want to set `assistant.firstMessageMode=assistant-speaks-first-with-model-generated-message` for the destination assistant.<br><br>This accepts a string or a ToolMessageStart class. Latter is useful if you want to specify multiple messages for different languages through the `contents` field.|
|type|string|true|none|none|
|numberE164CheckEnabled|boolean|false|none|This is the flag to toggle the E164 check for the `number` field. This is an advanced property which should be used if you know your use case requires it.<br><br>Use cases:<br>- `false`: To allow non-E164 numbers like `+001234567890`, `1234`, or `abc`. This is useful for dialing out to non-E164 numbers on your SIP trunks.<br>- `true` (default): To allow only E164 numbers like `+14155551234`. This is standard for PSTN calls.<br><br>If `false`, the `number` is still required to only contain alphanumeric characters (regex: `/^\+?[a-zA-Z0-9]+$/`).<br><br>@default true (E164 check is enabled)|
|number|string|true|none|This is the phone number to transfer the call to.|
|extension|string|false|none|This is the extension to dial after transferring the call to the `number`.|
|callerId|string|false|none|This is the caller ID to use when transferring the call to the `number`.<br><br>Usage:<br>- If not provided, the caller ID will be the number the call is coming **from**.<br>  Example: a customer with number +14151111111 calls in to and the assistant transfers out to +16470000000. +16470000000 will see +14151111111 as the caller.<br>  For inbound calls, the caller ID is the customer's number. For outbound calls, the caller ID is the phone number of the assistant.<br>- To change this behavior, provide a `callerId`.<br>- Set to '{{customer.number}}' to always use the customer's number as the caller ID.<br>- Set to '{{phoneNumber.number}}' to always use the phone number of the assistant as the caller ID.<br>- Set to any E164 number to always use that number as the caller ID. This needs to be a number that is owned or verified by your Transport provider like Twilio.<br><br>Note: on Twilio, a caller who withheld their number has no caller ID the destination carrier will accept, so the assistant's phone number is presented instead and the transfer goes through. This applies when `callerId` is not provided and when it is set to '{{customer.number}}'.<br><br>For Twilio, you can read up more here: https://www.twilio.com/docs/voice/twiml/dial#callerid|
|transferPlan|object|false|none|This configures how transfer is executed and the experience of the destination party receiving the call. Defaults to `blind-transfer`.<br><br>@default `transferPlan.mode='blind-transfer'`|
|name|string|false|none|This is the name of the transfer destination. This is just for your own reference.<br><br>Usage:<br>- Optional. Stored with the destination wherever it is supplied. For `number`<br>  and `sip` destinations it is also persisted on the transfer record in the<br>  call artifact after a transfer and displayed in the dashboard call log (on<br>  the transfer divider in the transcript view) alongside the destination.<br>  When omitted, everything behaves exactly as before.<br>- Display-only. Unlike `description`, it is never included in prompts or tool<br>  descriptions and has no effect on model behavior or destination choice.|
|description|string|false|none|This is the description of the destination, used by the AI to choose when and how to transfer the call.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|number|

|message|string \| [CustomMessage](#schemacustommessage)|false|none|This is spoken to the customer before connecting them to the destination.<br><br>Usage:<br>- If this is not provided and transfer tool messages is not provided, default is "Transferring the call now".<br>- If set to "", nothing is spoken. This is useful when you want to silently transfer. This is especially useful when transferring between assistants in a squad. In this scenario, you likely also want to set `assistant.firstMessageMode=assistant-speaks-first-with-model-generated-message` for the destination assistant.<br><br>This accepts a string or a ToolMessageStart class. Latter is useful if you want to specify multiple messages for different languages through the `contents` field.|

For `number`<br>  and `sip` destinations it is also persisted on the transfer record in the<br>  call artifact after a transfer and displayed in the dashboard call log (on<br>  the transfer divider in the transcript view) alongside the destination.<br>  When omitted, everything behaves exactly as before.<br>- Display-only. Unlike `description`, it is never included in prompts or tool<br>  descriptions and has no effect on model behavior or destination choice.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|messages|[[ToolMessageStart](#schematoolmessagestart) \| [ToolMessageComplete](#schematoolmessagecomplete) \| [ToolMessageFailed](#schematoolmessagefailed) \| [ToolMessageDelayed](#schematoolmessagedelayed)]|false|none|Messages spoken while the tool is running. Multiple request-start messages are variants. For request-response-delayed, same timing means variants and different timings mean staged updates.|
|type|string|true|none|none|
|destinations|[[TransferDestinationAssistant](#schematransferdestinationassistant) \| [TransferDestinationNumber](#schematransferdestinationnumber) \| [TransferDestinationSip](#schematransferdestinationsip)]|false|none|These are the destinations that the call can be transferred to. If no destinations are provided, server.url will be used to get the transfer destination once the tool is called.|
|rejectionPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan to reject a tool call based on the conversation state.<br><br>// Example 1: Reject endCall if user didn't say goodbye<br>```json<br>{<br>  conditions: [{<br>    type: 'regex',<br>    regex: '(?i)\\b(bye\|goodbye\|farewell\|see you later\|take care)\\b',<br>    target: { position: -1, role: 'user' },<br>    negate: true  // Reject if pattern does NOT match<br>  }]<br>}<br>```<br><br>// Example 2: Reject transfer if user is actually asking a question<br>```json<br>{<br>  conditions: [{<br>    type: 'regex',<br>    regex: '\\?',<br>    target: { position: -1, role: 'user' }<br>  }]<br>}<br>```<br><br>// Example 3: Reject transfer if user didn't mention transfer recently<br>```json<br>{<br>  conditions: [{<br>    type: 'liquid',<br>    liquid: `{% assign recentMessages = messages \| last: 5 %}<br>{% assign userMessages = recentMessages \| where: 'role', 'user' %}<br>{% assign mentioned = false %}<br>{% for msg in userMessages %}<br>  {% if msg.content contains 'transfer' or msg.content contains 'connect' or msg.content contains 'speak to' %}<br>    {% assign mentioned = true %}<br>    {% break %}<br>  {% endif %}<br>{% endfor %}<br>{% if mentioned %}<br>  false<br>{% else %}<br>  true<br>{% endif %}`<br>  }]<br>}<br>```<br><br>// Example 4: Reject endCall if the bot is looping and trying to exit<br>```json<br>{<br>  conditions: [{<br>    type: 'liquid',<br>    liquid: `{% assign recentMessages = messages \| last: 6 %}<br>{% assign userMessages = recentMessages \| where: 'role', 'user' \| reverse %}<br>{% if userMessages.size < 3 %}<br>  false<br>{% else %}<br>  {% assign msg1 = userMessages[0].content \| downcase %}<br>  {% assign msg2 = userMessages[1].content \| downcase %}<br>  {% assign msg3 = userMessages[2].content \| downcase %}<br>  {% comment %} Check for repetitive messages {% endcomment %}<br>  {% if msg1 == msg2 or msg1 == msg3 or msg2 == msg3 %}<br>    true<br>  {% comment %} Check for common loop phrases {% endcomment %}<br>  {% elsif msg1 contains 'cool thanks' or msg2 contains 'cool thanks' or msg3 contains 'cool thanks' %}<br>    true<br>  {% elsif msg1 contains 'okay thanks' or msg2 contains 'okay thanks' or msg3 contains 'okay thanks' %}<br>    true<br>  {% elsif msg1 contains 'got it' or msg2 contains 'got it' or msg3 contains 'got it' %}<br>    true<br>  {% else %}<br>    false<br>  {% endif %}<br>{% endif %}`<br>  }]<br>}<br>```|

```json
          "cachingEnabled": true,
          "provider": "azure",
          "voiceId": "andrew",
          "speed": 0.5,
          "chunkPlan": {
            "enabled": true,
            "minCharacters": 30,
            "punctuationBoundaries": [
              "。",
              "，",
              ".",
              "!",
              "?",
              ";",
              "،",
              "۔",
              "।",
              "॥",
              "|",
              "||",
              ",",
              ":"
            ],
            "formatPlan": {
              "enabled": true,
              "numberToDigitsCutoff": 2025,
              "replacements": [
                {
                  "type": "exact",
                  "replaceAllEnabled": false,
                  "key": "string",
                  "value": "string"
                }
              ],
              "formattersEnabled": "markdown"
            }
          }
        }

  },

  "type": "stay-on-line",
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|message|string|true|none|This is the message asking for consent to record the call.<br>If the type is `stay-on-line`, the message should ask the user to hang up if they do not consent.<br>If the type is `verbal`, the message should ask the user to verbally consent or decline.|
|voice|[AzureVoice](#schemaazurevoice) \| [CartesiaVoice](#schemacartesiavoice) \| [CustomVoice](#schemacustomvoice) \| [DeepgramVoice](#schemadeepgramvoice) \| [ElevenLabsVoice](#schemaelevenlabsvoice) \| [HumeVoice](#schemahumevoice) \| [LMNTVoice](#schemalmntvoice) \| [NeuphonicVoice](#schemaneuphonicvoice) \| [OpenAIVoice](#schemaopenaivoice) \| [PlayHTVoice](#schemaplayhtvoice) \| [WellSaidVoice](#schemawellsaidvoice) \| [RimeAIVoice](#schemarimeaivoice) \| [SmallestAIVoice](#schemasmallestaivoice) \| [VapiVoice](#schemavapivoice) \| [SesameVoice](#schemasesamevoice) \| [InworldVoice](#schemainworldvoice) \| [MinimaxVoice](#schemaminimaxvoice) \| [XaiVoice](#schemaxaivoice) \| [MicrosoftVoice](#schemamicrosoftvoice)|false|none|This is the voice to use for the consent message. If not specified, inherits from the assistant's voice.<br>Use a different voice for the consent message for a better user experience.|
|firstMessageMode|string|false|none|This controls whether the consent assistant speaks first or waits for the caller to speak first.<br><br>Use:<br>- `assistant-speaks-first` (default) to have the consent assistant play the consent message as soon as the call is answered.<br>- `assistant-waits-for-user` to have the consent assistant wait for the caller to speak before playing the consent message.<br><br>We strongly recommend `assistant-waits-for-user` for outbound calls. Some telephony providers signal "answered" while the line is still ringing, which can cause the consent message to play into a ringing line and be missed by the caller. Waiting for the caller to speak first guarantees they hear the full consent message.<br><br>Note: when combined with `type: 'stay-on-line'`, silence only counts toward consent after the caller has spoken at least once.<br><br>@default 'assistant-speaks-first'|
|type|string|true|none|This is the type of recording consent plan. This type assumes consent is granted if the user stays on the line.|
|waitSeconds|number|false|none|Number of seconds to wait before transferring to the assistant if user stays on the call|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|firstMessageMode|assistant-speaks-first|
|firstMessageMode|assistant-waits-for-user|
|type|stay-on-line|

```json
  ],
```

```json
    "type": "string",
    "items": {},
    "properties": {
      "property1": {},
      "property2": {}
    },
    "description": "string",
    "pattern": "string",
    "format": "date-time",
    "required": [
      "string"
    ],
    "enum": [
      "string"
    ],
    "title": "string"
  },
  "timeoutSeconds": 1
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|messages|[object]|false|none|These are the messages used to generate the structured data.<br><br>@default: ```<br>[<br>  {<br>    "role": "system",<br>    "content": "You are an expert data extractor. You will be given a transcript of a call. Extract structured data per the JSON Schema. DO NOT return anything except the structured data.\n\nJson Schema:\\n{{schema}}\n\nOnly respond with the JSON."<br>  },<br>  {<br>    "role": "user",<br>    "content": "Here is the transcript:\n\n{{transcript}}\n\n. Here is the ended reason of the call:\n\n{{endedReason}}\n\n"<br>  }<br>]```<br><br>You can customize by providing any messages you want.<br><br>Here are the template variables available:<br>- {{transcript}}: the transcript of the call from `call.artifact.transcript`- {{systemPrompt}}: the system prompt of the call from `assistant.model.messages[type=system].content`- {{messages}}: the messages of the call from `assistant.model.messages`- {{schema}}: the schema of the structured data from `structuredDataPlan.schema`- {{endedReason}}: the ended reason of the call from `call.endedReason`|
|enabled|boolean|false|none|This determines whether structured data is generated and stored in `call.analysis.structuredData`. Defaults to false.<br><br>Usage:<br>- If you want to extract structured data, set this to true and provide a `schema`.<br><br>@default false|
|schema|object|false|none|This is the schema of the structured data. The output is stored in `call.analysis.structuredData`.<br><br>Complete guide on JSON Schema can be found [here](https://ajv.js.org/json-schema.html#json-data-type).|
|timeoutSeconds|number|false|none|This is how long the request is tried before giving up. When request times out, `call.analysis.structuredData` will be empty.<br><br>Usage:<br>- To guarantee the structured data is generated, set this value high. Note, this will delay the end of call report in cases where model is slow to respond.<br><br>@default 5 seconds|

<h2 id="tocS_SuccessEvaluationPlan">SuccessEvaluationPlan</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemasuccessevaluationplan"></a>

<a id="tocSsuccessevaluationplan"></a>
<a id="tocssuccessevaluationplan"></a>

```json
{
  "rubric": "NumericScale",
  "messages": [
    {}
  ],
  "enabled": true,
  "timeoutSeconds": 1
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|rubric|string|false|none|This enforces the rubric of the evaluation. The output is stored in `call.analysis.successEvaluation`.<br><br>Options include:<br>- 'NumericScale': A scale of 1 to 10.<br>- 'DescriptiveScale': A scale of Excellent, Good, Fair, Poor.<br>- 'Checklist': A checklist of criteria and their status.<br>- 'Matrix': A grid that evaluates multiple criteria across different performance levels.<br>- 'PercentageScale': A scale of 0% to 100%.<br>- 'LikertScale': A scale of Strongly Agree, Agree, Neutral, Disagree, Strongly Disagree.<br>- 'AutomaticRubric': Automatically break down evaluation into several criteria, each with its own score.<br>- 'PassFail': A simple 'true' if call passed, 'false' if not.<br><br>Default is 'PassFail'.|
|messages|[object]|false|none|These are the messages used to generate the success evaluation.<br><br>@default: ```<br>[<br>  {<br>    "role": "system",<br>    "content": "You are an expert call evaluator. You will be given a transcript of a call and the system prompt of the AI participant. Determine if the call was successful based on the objectives inferred from the system prompt. DO NOT return anything except the result.\n\nRubric:\\n{{rubric}}\n\nOnly respond with the result."<br>  },<br>  {<br>    "role": "user",<br>    "content": "Here is the transcript:\n\n{{transcript}}\n\n"<br>  },<br>  {<br>    "role": "user",<br>    "content": "Here was the system prompt of the call:\n\n{{systemPrompt}}\n\n. Here is the ended reason of the call:\n\n{{endedReason}}\n\n"<br>  }<br>]```<br><br>You can customize by providing any messages you want.<br><br>Here are the template variables available:<br>- {{transcript}}: the transcript of the call from `call.artifact.transcript`- {{systemPrompt}}: the system prompt of the call from `assistant.model.messages[type=system].content`- {{messages}}: the messages of the call from `assistant.model.messages`- {{rubric}}: the rubric of the success evaluation from `successEvaluationPlan.rubric`- {{endedReason}}: the ended reason of the call from `call.endedReason`|
|enabled|boolean|false|none|This determines whether a success evaluation is generated and stored in `call.analysis.successEvaluation`. Defaults to true.<br><br>Usage:<br>- If you want to disable the success evaluation, set this to false.<br><br>@default true|
|timeoutSeconds|number|false|none|This is how long the request is tried before giving up. When request times out, `call.analysis.successEvaluation` will be empty.<br><br>Usage:<br>- To guarantee the success evaluation is generated, set this value high. Note, this will delay the end of call report in cases where model is slow to respond.<br><br>@default 5 seconds|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|rubric|NumericScale|
|rubric|DescriptiveScale|
|rubric|Checklist|
|rubric|Matrix|
|rubric|PercentageScale|
|rubric|LikertScale|
|rubric|AutomaticRubric|
|rubric|PassFail|

<h2 id="tocS_CreateStructuredOutputDTO">CreateStructuredOutputDTO</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacreatestructuredoutputdto"></a>
<a id="schema_CreateStructuredOutputDTO"></a>
<a id="tocScreatestructuredoutputdto"></a>
<a id="tocscreatestructuredoutputdto"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "ai",
  "regex": "string",
  "model": {
    "messages": [
      {
        "content": "string",
        "role": "assistant"
      }
    ],
    "provider": "openai",
    "model": "gpt-6-luna",
    "reasoningEffort": "minimal",
    "temperature": 0,
    "maxTokens": 50
  },
  "compliancePlan": {
    "forceStoreOnHipaaEnabled": false
  },
  "conditions": [
    {
      "type": "minMessages",
      "count": 4
    },
    {
      "type": "minCallDuration",
      "seconds": 10
    }
  ],
  "name": "string",
  "schema": {
    "type": "string",
    "items": {},
    "properties": {
      "property1": {},
      "property2": {}
    },
    "description": "string",
    "pattern": "string",
    "format": "date-time",
    "required": [
      "string"
    ],
    "enum": [
      "string"
    ],
    "title": "string"
  },
  "description": "string",
  "assistantIds": [
    "string"
  ],
  "workflowIds": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|false|none|This is the type of structured output.<br><br>- 'ai': Uses an LLM to extract structured data from the conversation (default).<br>- 'regex': Uses a regex pattern to extract data from the transcript without an LLM.<br><br>Defaults to 'ai' if not specified.|
|regex|string|false|none|This is the regex pattern to match against the transcript.<br><br>Simulation evaluations use a canonical transcript built from recorded messages:<br>User: and AI: dialogue, AI: tool_calls: JSON name/arguments records, and<br>AI: tool_call_results: JSON results. System messages are excluded. These<br>fixed labels apply even when custom artifact transcript labels are configured.<br>Tool payloads participate in first-match and all-match extraction in event order.<br>An empty message array falls back to the supplied transcript verbatim.<br>Production-call extraction and call preview use their existing transcripts,<br>so previewing the same output on a simulation's call can return a different result.<br><br>Only used when type is 'regex'. Supports both raw patterns (e.g. '\d+') and<br>regex literal format (e.g. '/\d+/gi'). Uses RE2 syntax for safety.<br><br>The result depends on the schema type:<br>- boolean: true if the pattern matches, false otherwise<br>- string: the first match or first capture group<br>- number/integer: the first match parsed as a number<br>- array: all matches|
|model|[WorkflowOpenAIModel](#schemaworkflowopenaimodel) \| [WorkflowAnthropicModel](#schemaworkflowanthropicmodel) \| [WorkflowAnthropicBedrockModel](#schemaworkflowanthropicbedrockmodel) \| [WorkflowGoogleModel](#schemaworkflowgooglemodel) \| [WorkflowCustomModel](#schemaworkflowcustommodel)|false|none|This is the model that will be used to extract the structured output.<br><br>To provide your own custom system and user prompts for structured output extraction, populate the messages array with your system and user messages. You can specify liquid templating in your system and user messages.<br>For text extraction, you must reference 'transcript', 'messages', or 'messagesWithConfidence' with the `{{}}` syntax to access the conversation history.<br>In structured outputs, `{{messages}}` includes conversation text and tool calls/results but omits caller transcription-confidence fields. Text extraction can use `{{messagesWithConfidence}}` when the output needs the original message history with transcription confidence. These variables also apply in structured-output schema descriptions. Audio-targeted (`messages-with-audio`) extraction ignores custom messages. Stored call artifacts and API messages retain their confidence data.<br>Between the system or user messages, you must reference a variation of the structured output with the `{{}}` syntax to access the structured output definition.<br>i.e.:<br>`{{structuredOutput}}`<br>`{{structuredOutput.name}}`<br>`{{structuredOutput.description}}`<br>`{{structuredOutput.schema}}`<br><br>If model is not specified, GPT-4.1 will be used by default for extraction, utilizing default system and user prompts.<br>If messages or required fields are not specified, the default system and user prompts will be used.|
|compliancePlan|object|false|none|Compliance configuration for this output. Only enable overrides if no sensitive data will be stored.|
|conditions|[[MinMessagesCondition](#schemaminmessagescondition) \| [MinCallDurationCondition](#schemamincalldurationcondition) \| [EndedReasonCondition](#schemaendedreasoncondition)]|false|none|These are the conditions that gate the execution of this structured output. Every condition must pass for the structured output to run (AND semantics). When omitted or empty, no user-defined conditions gate this output. Send null to clear a previously saved gate.|
|name|string|true|none|This is the name of the structured output.|
|schema|object|true|none|This is the JSON Schema definition for the structured output.<br><br>This is required when creating a structured output. Defines the structure and validation rules for the data that will be extracted. Supports all JSON Schema features including:<br>- Objects and nested properties<br>- Arrays and array validation<br>- String, number, boolean, and null types<br>- Enums and const values<br>- Validation constraints (min/max, patterns, etc.)<br>- Composition with allOf, anyOf, oneOf|
|description|string|false|none|This is the description of what the structured output extracts.<br><br>Use this to provide context about what data will be extracted and how it will be used.|
|assistantIds|[string]|false|none|These are the assistant IDs that this structured output is linked to.<br><br>When linked to assistants, this structured output will be available for extraction during those assistant's calls.|
|workflowIds|[string]|false|none|These are the workflow IDs that this structured output is linked to.<br><br>When linked to workflows, this structured output will be available for extraction during those workflow's execution.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|ai|
|type|regex|

|value|number|true|none|This is the value that will be used to compare the result of the structured output with the comparator.<br>If the result of the comparison is true, the points will be added to the overall score.|
|points|number|true|none|These are the points that will be added to the overall score if the condition is met.<br>The points must be between 0 and 100.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|recordingEnabled|boolean|false|none|This determines whether assistant's calls are recorded. Defaults to true.<br><br>Usage:<br>- If you don't want to record the calls, set this to false.<br>- If you want to record the calls when `assistant.hipaaEnabled` (deprecated) or `assistant.compliancePlan.hipaaEnabled` explicity set this to true and make sure to provide S3 or GCP credentials on the Provider Credentials page in the Dashboard.<br><br>You can find the recording at `call.artifact.recordingUrl` and `call.artifact.stereoRecordingUrl` after the call is ended.<br><br>@default true|
|recordingFormat|string|false|none|This determines the format of the recording. Defaults to `wav;l16`.<br><br>@default 'wav;l16'|
|recordingUseCustomStorageEnabled|boolean|false|none|This determines whether to use custom storage (S3 or GCP) for call recordings when storage credentials are configured.<br><br>When set to false, recordings will be stored on Vapi's storage instead of your custom storage, even if you have custom storage credentials configured.<br><br>Usage:<br>- Set to false if you have custom storage configured but want to store recordings on Vapi's storage for this assistant.<br>- Set to true (or leave unset) to use your custom storage for recordings when available.<br><br>If your organization has ZDR (zero data retention) or PCI enabled, recordings are never written to Vapi storage. In that case, false means "do not use my custom storage", so nothing is stored at all.<br><br>@default true|
|videoRecordingEnabled|boolean|false|none|This determines whether the video is recorded during the call. Defaults to false. Only relevant for `webCall` type.<br><br>You can find the video recording at `call.artifact.videoRecordingUrl` after the call is ended.<br><br>@default false|
|fullMessageHistoryEnabled|boolean|false|none|This determines whether the artifact contains the full message history, even after handoff context engineering. Defaults to false.|
|pcapEnabled|boolean|false|none|This determines whether the SIP packet capture is enabled. Defaults to true. Only relevant for `phone` type calls where phone number's provider is `vapi` or `byo-phone-number`.<br><br>You can find the packet capture at `call.artifact.pcapUrl` after the call is ended.<br><br>@default true|
|pcapS3PathPrefix|string|false|none|This is the path where the SIP packet capture will be uploaded. This is only used if you have provided S3 or GCP credentials on the Provider Credentials page in the Dashboard.<br><br>If credential.s3PathPrefix or credential.bucketPlan.path is set, this will append to it.<br><br>Usage:<br>- If you want to upload the packet capture to a specific path, set this to the path. Example: `/my-assistant-captures`.<br>- If you want to upload the packet capture to the root of the bucket, set this to `/`.<br><br>@default '/'|
|pcapUseCustomStorageEnabled|boolean|false|none|This determines whether to use custom storage (S3 or GCP) for SIP packet captures when storage credentials are configured.<br><br>When set to false, packet captures will be stored on Vapi's storage instead of your custom storage, even if you have custom storage credentials configured.<br><br>Usage:<br>- Set to false if you have custom storage configured but want to store packet captures on Vapi's storage for this assistant.<br>- Set to true (or leave unset) to use your custom storage for packet captures when available.<br><br>If your organization has ZDR (zero data retention) or PCI enabled, packet captures are never written to Vapi storage. In that case, false means "do not use my custom storage", so nothing is stored at all.<br><br>@default true|
|loggingEnabled|boolean|false|none|This determines whether the call logs are enabled. Defaults to true.<br><br>@default true|
|loggingUseCustomStorageEnabled|boolean|false|none|This determines whether to use custom storage (S3 or GCP) for call logs when storage credentials are configured.<br><br>When set to false, logs will be stored on Vapi's storage instead of your custom storage, even if you have custom storage credentials configured.<br><br>Usage:<br>- Set to false if you have custom storage configured but want to store logs on Vapi's storage for this assistant.<br>- Set to true (or leave unset) to use your custom storage for logs when available.<br><br>If your organization has ZDR (zero data retention) or PCI enabled, logs are never written to Vapi storage. In that case, false means "do not use my custom storage", so nothing is stored at all.<br><br>@default true|
|transcriptPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan for `call.artifact.transcript`. To disable, set `transcriptPlan.enabled` to false.|
|recordingPath|string|false|none|This is the path where the recording will be uploaded. This is only used if you have provided S3 or GCP credentials on the Provider Credentials page in the Dashboard.<br><br>If credential.s3PathPrefix or credential.bucketPlan.path is set, this will append to it.<br><br>Usage:<br>- If you want to upload the recording to a specific path, set this to the path. Example: `/my-assistant-recordings`.<br>- If you want to upload the recording to the root of the bucket, set this to `/`.<br><br>@default '/'|
|structuredOutputIds|[string]|false|none|This is an array of structured output IDs to be calculated during the call.<br>The outputs will be extracted and stored in `call.artifact.structuredOutputs` after the call is ended.|
|structuredOutputs|[[CreateStructuredOutputDTO](#schemacreatestructuredoutputdto)]|false|none|This is an array of transient structured outputs to be calculated during the call.<br>The outputs will be extracted and stored in `call.artifact.structuredOutputs` after the call is ended.<br>Use this to provide inline structured output configurations instead of referencing existing ones via structuredOutputIds.|
|scorecardIds|[string]|false|none|This is an array of scorecard IDs that will be evaluated based on the structured outputs extracted during the call.<br>The scorecards will be evaluated and the results will be stored in `call.artifact.scorecards` after the call has ended.|
|scorecards|[[CreateScorecardDTO](#schemacreatescorecarddto)]|false|none|This is the array of scorecards that will be evaluated based on the structured outputs extracted during the call.<br>The scorecards will be evaluated and the results will be stored in `call.artifact.scorecards` after the call has ended.|
|loggingPath|string|false|none|This is the path where the call logs will be uploaded. This is only used if you have provided S3 or GCP credentials on the Provider Credentials page in the Dashboard.<br><br>If credential.s3PathPrefix or credential.bucketPlan.path is set, this will append to it.<br><br>Usage:<br>- If you want to upload the call logs to a specific path, set this to the path. Example: `/my-assistant-logs`.<br>- If you want to upload the call logs to the root of the bucket, set this to `/`.<br><br>@default '/'|

```json
{

    "im listening",
    "im with you",
    "right",

    "understood",
    "yeah",

    "uh-huh",
    "mm-hmm",
    "gotcha",
    "mhmm",
    "ah",
    "yeah okay",
    "yeah sure"
  ],
  "interruptionPhrases": [
    "stop",
    "shut",
    "up",
    "enough",
    "quiet",
    "silence",
    "but",
    "dont",
    "not",
    "no",
    "hold",
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|numWords|number|false|none|This is the number of words that the customer has to say before the assistant will stop talking.<br><br>Words like "stop", "actually", "no", etc. will always interrupt immediately regardless of this value.<br><br>Words like "okay", "yeah", "right" will never interrupt.<br><br>When set to 0, `voiceSeconds` is used in addition to the transcriptions to determine the customer has started speaking.<br><br>Defaults to 0.<br><br>@default 0|
|voiceSeconds|number|false|none|This is the seconds customer has to speak before the assistant stops talking. This uses the VAD (Voice Activity Detection) spike to determine if the customer has started speaking.<br><br>Considerations:<br>- A lower value might be more responsive but could potentially pick up non-speech sounds.<br>- A higher value reduces false positives but might slightly delay the detection of speech onset.<br><br>This is only used if `numWords` is set to 0.<br><br>Defaults to 0.2<br><br>@default 0.2|
|backoffSeconds|number|false|none|This is the seconds to wait before the assistant will start talking again after being interrupted.<br><br>Defaults to 1.<br><br>@default 1|
|acknowledgementPhrases|[string]|false|none|These are the phrases that will never interrupt the assistant, even if numWords threshold is met.<br>These are typically acknowledgement or backchanneling phrases.|
|interruptionPhrases|[string]|false|none|These are the phrases that will always interrupt the assistant immediately, regardless of numWords.<br>These are typically phrases indicating disagreement or desire to stop.|

for the assistant calls. By default, all the credentials are available for use in the call but you can supplement an additional credentials using this. Dynamic credentials override existing credentials.|
|hooks|[[CallHookCallEnding](#schemacallhookcallending) \| [CallHookAssistantSpeechInterrupted](#schemacallhookassistantspeechinterrupted) \| [CallHookCustomerSpeechInterrupted](#schemacallhookcustomerspeechinterrupted) \| [CallHookCustomerSpeechTimeout](#schemacallhookcustomerspeechtimeout) \| [SessionCreatedHook](#schemasessioncreatedhook)]|false|none|This is a set of actions that will be performed on certain events.|
|name|string|false|none|This is the name of the assistant.<br><br>This is required when you want to transfer between assistants in a call.|
|voicemailMessage|string|false|none|This is the message that the assistant will say if the call is forwarded to voicemail.<br><br>If unspecified, it will hang up.|
|endCallMessage|string|false|none|This is the message that the assistant will say if it ends the call.<br><br>If unspecified, it will hang up without saying anything.|
|endCallPhrases|[string]|false|none|This list contains phrases that, if spoken by the assistant, will trigger the call to be hung up. Case insensitive.|
|compliancePlan|[CompliancePlan](#schemacomplianceplan)|false|none|none|
|metadata|object|false|none|This is for metadata you want to store on the assistant.|
|backgroundSpeechDenoisingPlan|object|false|none|This enables filtering of noise and background speech while the user is talking.<br><br>Features:<br>- Smart denoising using Krisp<br>- Fourier denoising<br><br>Smart denoising can be combined with or used independently of Fourier denoising.<br><br>Order of precedence:<br>- Smart denoising<br>- Fourier denoising|
|analysisPlan|object|false|none|**Deprecated.** This is the plan for analysis of assistant's calls. Stored in `call.analysis`.|
|artifactPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan for artifacts generated during assistant's calls. Stored in `call.artifact`.|
|startSpeakingPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan for when the assistant should start talking.<br><br>You should configure this if you're running into these issues:<br>- The assistant is too slow to start talking after the customer is done speaking.<br>- The assistant is too fast to start talking after the customer is done speaking.<br>- The assistant is so fast that it's actually interrupting the customer.|
|stopSpeakingPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan for when assistant should stop talking on customer interruption.<br><br>You should configure this if you're running into these issues:<br>- The assistant is too slow to recognize customer's interruption.<br>- The assistant is too fast to recognize customer's interruption.<br>- The assistant is getting interrupted by phrases that are just acknowledgments.<br>- The assistant is getting interrupted by background noises.<br>- The assistant is not properly stopping -- it starts talking right after getting interrupted.|
|monitorPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan for real-time monitoring of the assistant's calls.<br><br>Usage:<br>- To enable live listening of the assistant's calls, set `monitorPlan.listenEnabled` to `true`.<br>- To enable live control of the assistant's calls, set `monitorPlan.controlEnabled` to `true`.<br>- To attach monitors to the assistant, set `monitorPlan.monitorIds` to the set of monitor ids.|
|credentialIds|[string]|false|none|These are the credentials that will be used for the assistant calls. By default, all the credentials are available for use in the call but you can provide a subset using this.|
|server|object|false|none|This is where Vapi will send webhooks. You can find all webhooks available along with their shape in ServerMessage schema.<br><br>The order of precedence is:<br><br>1. assistant.server.url<br>2. phoneNumber.serverUrl<br>3. org.serverUrl|
|keypadInputPlan|[KeypadInputPlan](#schemakeypadinputplan)|false|none|none|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|none|
|contextEngineeringPlan|[ContextEngineeringPlanLastNMessages](#schemacontextengineeringplanlastnmessages) \| [ContextEngineeringPlanNone](#schemacontextengineeringplannone) \| [ContextEngineeringPlanAll](#schemacontextengineeringplanall) \| [ContextEngineeringPlanUserAndAssistantMessages](#schemacontextengineeringplanuserandassistantmessages) \| [ContextEngineeringPlanPreviousAssistantMessages](#schemacontextengineeringplanpreviousassistantmessages)|false|none|This is the plan for manipulating the message context before handing off the call to the next assistant.|
|assistantName|string|false|none|This is the assistant to transfer the call to. You must provide either assistantName or assistantId.|
|assistantId|string|false|none|This is the assistant id to transfer the call to. You must provide either assistantName or assistantId.|
|assistant|object|false|none|This is a transient assistant to transfer the call to. You may provide a transient assistant in the response  `handoff-destination-request` in a dynamic handoff.|
|variableExtractionPlan|object|false|none|This is the variable extraction plan for the handoff tool.|
|assistantOverrides|object|false|none|These are the assistant overrides to apply to the destination assistant.|
|description|string|false|none|This is the description of the destination, used by the AI to choose when and how to transfer the call.|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|assistant|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|assistantVersion|string \| null|false|none|This is the assistant version (e.g. `v3`) to pin for this squad member. When set, the call uses<br>the snapshot from `assistant_version` (by `(assistantId, version)`) instead of the latest. Valid<br>only with `assistantId`; rejected with inline `assistant`. Omit to follow the latest version.|
|assistantDestinations|[[TransferDestinationAssistant](#schematransferdestinationassistant) \| [HandoffDestinationAssistant](#schemahandoffdestinationassistant)]|false|none|none|
|assistantId|string \| null|false|none|This is the assistant that will be used for the call. To use a transient assistant, use `assistant` instead.|
|assistant|object|false|none|This is the assistant that will be used for the call. To use an existing assistant, use `assistantId` instead.|
|assistantOverrides|object|false|none|This can be used to override the assistant's settings and provide values for it's template variables.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|false|none|This is the name of the squad.|
|members|[[SquadMemberDTO](#schemasquadmemberdto)]|true|none|This is the list of assistants that make up the squad.<br><br>The call will start with the first assistant in the list.|
|membersOverrides|object|false|none|This can be used to override all the assistants' settings and provide values for their template variables.<br><br>Both `membersOverrides` and `members[n].assistantOverrides` can be used together. First, `members[n].assistantOverrides` is applied. Then, `membersOverrides` is applied as a global override.|

|squadId|string|false|none|This is the squad id to transfer the call to.|
|squad|object|false|none|This is a transient squad to transfer the call to.|
|entryAssistantName|string|false|none|This is the name of the entry assistant to start with when handing off to the squad.<br>If not provided, the first member of the squad will be used.|
|variableExtractionPlan|object|false|none|This is the variable extraction plan for the handoff tool.|
|squadOverrides|object|false|none|These are the overrides to apply to the squad configuration.<br>Maps to squad-level membersOverrides.|
|description|string|false|none|This is the description of the destination, used by the AI to choose when and how to transfer the call.|
