### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|messages|[[ToolMessageStart](#schematoolmessagestart) \| [ToolMessageComplete](#schematoolmessagecomplete) \| [ToolMessageFailed](#schematoolmessagefailed) \| [ToolMessageDelayed](#schematoolmessagedelayed)]|false|none|Messages spoken while the tool is running. Multiple request-start messages are variants. For request-response-delayed, same timing means variants and different timings mean staged updates.|
|type|string|true|none|This is the type of the tool.<br>When you're using handoff tool, we recommend adding this to your system prompt<br>---<br># System context<br><br>You are part of a multi-agent system designed to make agent coordination and execution easy. Agents uses two primary abstraction: **Agents** and **Handoffs**. An agent encompasses instructions and tools and can hand off a conversation to another agent when appropriate. Handoffs are achieved by calling a handoff function, generally named `handoff_to_<agent_name>`. Handoffs between agents are handled seamlessly in the background; do not mention or draw attention to these handoffs in your conversation with the user.<br><br># Agent context<br><br>{put your agent system prompt here}<br>---|
|defaultResult|string|false|none|This is the default local tool result message used when no runtime handoff result override is returned.|
|destinations|[[HandoffDestinationAssistant](#schemahandoffdestinationassistant) \| [HandoffDestinationDynamic](#schemahandoffdestinationdynamic) \| [HandoffDestinationSquad](#schemahandoffdestinationsquad)]|false|none|These are the destinations that the call can be handed off to.<br><br>Usage:<br>1. Single destination<br><br>Use `assistantId` to handoff the call to a saved assistant, or `assistantName` to handoff the call to an assistant in the same squad.<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "tools": [<br>    {<br>      "type": "handoff",<br>      "destinations": [<br>        {<br>          "type": "assistant",<br>          "assistantId": "assistant-123", // or "assistantName": "Assistant123"<br>          "description": "customer wants to be handed off to assistant-123",<br>          "contextEngineeringPlan": {<br>            "type": "all"<br>          }<br>        }<br>      ],<br>    }<br>  ]<br>}<br>```<br><br>2. Multiple destinations<br><br>2.1. Multiple Tools, Each With One Destination (OpenAI recommended)<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "tools": [<br>    {<br>      "type": "handoff",<br>      "destinations": [<br>        {<br>          "type": "assistant",<br>          "assistantId": "assistant-123",<br>          "description": "customer wants to be handed off to assistant-123",<br>          "contextEngineeringPlan": {<br>            "type": "all"<br>          }<br>        },<br>      ],<br>    },<br>    {<br>      "type": "handoff",<br>      "destinations": [<br>        {<br>          "type": "assistant",<br>          "assistantId": "assistant-456",<br>          "description": "customer wants to be handed off to assistant-456",<br>          "contextEngineeringPlan": {<br>            "type": "all"<br>          }<br>        }<br>      ],<br>    }<br>  ]<br>}<br>```<br><br>2.2. One Tool, Multiple Destinations (Anthropic recommended)<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "tools": [<br>    {<br>      "type": "handoff",<br>      "destinations": [<br>        {<br>          "type": "assistant",<br>          "assistantId": "assistant-123",<br>          "description": "customer wants to be handed off to assistant-123",<br>          "contextEngineeringPlan": {<br>            "type": "all"<br>          }<br>        },<br>        {<br>          "type": "assistant",<br>          "assistantId": "assistant-456",<br>          "description": "customer wants to be handed off to assistant-456",<br>          "contextEngineeringPlan": {<br>            "type": "all"<br>          }<br>        }<br>      ],<br>    }<br>  ]<br>}<br>```<br><br>3. Dynamic destination<br><br>3.1 To determine the destination dynamically, supply a `dynamic` handoff destination type and a `server` object.<br>    VAPI will send a handoff-destination-request webhook to the `server.url`.<br>    The response from the server will be used as the destination (if valid).<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "tools": [<br>    {<br>      "type": "handoff",<br>      "destinations": [<br>        {<br>          "type": "dynamic",<br>          "server": {<br>            "url": "https://example.com"<br>          }<br>        }<br>      ],<br>    }<br>  ]<br>}<br>```<br><br>3.2. To pass custom parameters to the server, you can use the `function` object.<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "tools": [<br>    {<br>      "type": "handoff",<br>      "destinations": [<br>        {<br>          "type": "dynamic",<br>          "server": {<br>            "url": "https://example.com"<br>          },<br>        }<br>      ],<br>      "function": {<br>        "name": "handoff",<br>        "description": "Call this function when the customer is ready to be handed off to the next assistant",<br>        "parameters": {<br>          "type": "object",<br>          "properties": {<br>            "destination": {<br>              "type": "string",<br>              "description": "Use dynamic when customer is ready to be handed off to the next assistant",<br>              "enum": ["dynamic"]<br>            },<br>            "customerAreaCode": {<br>              "type": "number",<br>              "description": "Area code of the customer"<br>            },<br>            "customerIntent": {<br>              "type": "string",<br>              "enum": ["new-customer", "existing-customer"],<br>              "description": "Use new-customer when customer is a new customer, existing-customer when customer is an existing customer"<br>            },<br>            "customerSentiment": {<br>              "type": "string",<br>              "enum": ["positive", "negative", "neutral"],<br>              "description": "Use positive when customer is happy, negative when customer is unhappy, neutral when customer is neutral"<br>            }<br>          }<br>        }<br>      }<br>    }<br>  ]<br>}<br>```<br><br>The properties `customerAreaCode`, `customerIntent`, and `customerSentiment` will be passed to the server in the webhook request body.|
|function|object|false|none|This is the optional function definition that will be passed to the LLM.<br>If this is not defined, we will construct this based on the other properties.<br><br>For example, given the following tools definition:<br>```json<br>{<br>  "tools": [<br>    {<br>      "type": "handoff",<br>      "destinations": [<br>        {<br>          "type": "assistant",<br>          "assistantId": "assistant-123",<br>          "description": "customer wants to be handed off to assistant-123",<br>          "contextEngineeringPlan": {<br>            "type": "all"<br>          }<br>        },<br>        {<br>          "type": "assistant",<br>          "assistantId": "assistant-456",<br>          "description": "customer wants to be handed off to assistant-456",<br>          "contextEngineeringPlan": {<br>            "type": "all"<br>          }<br>        }<br>      ],<br>    }<br>  ]<br>}<br>```<br><br>We will construct the following function definition:<br>```json<br>{<br>  "function": {<br>    "name": "handoff_to_assistant-123",<br>    "description": "<br>         Use this function to handoff the call to the next assistant.<br>         Only use it when instructions explicitly ask you to use the handoff_to_assistant function.<br>         DO NOT call this function unless you are instructed to do so.<br>         Here are the destinations you can handoff the call to:<br>         1. assistant-123. When: customer wants to be handed off to assistant-123<br>         2. assistant-456. When: customer wants to be handed off to assistant-456<br>    ",<br>    "parameters": {<br>      "type": "object",<br>      "properties": {<br>        "destination": {<br>          "type": "string",<br>          "description": "Options: assistant-123 (customer wants to be handed off to assistant-123), assistant-456 (customer wants to be handed off to assistant-456)",<br>          "enum": ["assistant-123", "assistant-456"]<br>        },<br>      },<br>      "required": ["destination"]<br>    }<br>  }<br>}<br>```<br><br>To override this function, please provide an OpenAI function definition and refer to it in the system prompt.<br>You may override parts of the function definition (i.e. you may only want to change the function name for your prompt).<br>If you choose to override the function parameters, it must include `destination` as a required parameter, and it must evaluate to either an assistantId, assistantName, or a the string literal `dynamic`.<br><br>To pass custom parameters to the server in a dynamic handoff, you can use the function parameters, with `dynamic` as the destination.<br>```json<br>{<br>  "function": {<br>    "name": "dynamic_handoff",<br>    "description": "<br>         Call this function when the customer is ready to be handed off to the next assistant<br>    ",<br>    "parameters": {<br>      "type": "object",<br>      "properties": {<br>        "destination": {<br>          "type": "string",<br>          "enum": ["dynamic"]<br>        },<br>        "customerAreaCode": {<br>          "type": "number",<br>          "description": "Area code of the customer"<br>        },<br>        "customerIntent": {<br>          "type": "string",<br>          "enum": ["new-customer", "existing-customer"],<br>          "description": "Use new-customer when customer is a new customer, existing-customer when customer is an existing customer"<br>        },<br>        "customerSentiment": {<br>          "type": "string",<br>          "enum": ["positive", "negative", "neutral"],<br>          "description": "Use positive when customer is happy, negative when customer is unhappy, neutral when customer is neutral"<br>        }<br>      },<br>      "required": ["destination", "customerAreaCode", "customerIntent", "customerSentiment"]<br>    }<br>  }<br>}<br>```|

[{<br>    type: 'regex',<br>    regex: '(?i)\\b(bye\|goodbye\|farewell\|see you later\|take care)\\b',<br>    target: { position: -1, role: 'user' },<br>    negate: true  // Reject if pattern does NOT match<br>  }]<br>}<br>```<br><br>// Example 2: Reject transfer if user is actually asking a question<br>```json<br>{<br>  conditions: [{<br>    type: 'regex',<br>    regex: '\\?',<br>    target: { position: -1, role: 'user' }<br>  }]<br>}<br>```<br><br>// Example 3: Reject transfer if user didn't mention transfer recently<br>```json<br>{<br>  conditions: [{<br>    type: 'liquid',<br>    liquid: `{% assign recentMessages = messages \| last: 5 %}<br>{% assign userMessages = recentMessages \| where: 'role', 'user' %}<br>{% assign mentioned = false %}<br>{% for msg in userMessages %}<br>  {% if msg.content contains 'transfer' or msg.content contains 'connect' or msg.content contains 'speak to' %}<br>    {% assign mentioned = true %}<br>    {% break %}<br>  {% endif %}<br>{% endfor %}<br>{% if mentioned %}<br>  false<br>{% else %}<br>  true<br>{% endif %}`<br>  }]<br>}<br>```<br><br>// Example 4: Reject endCall if the bot is looping and trying to exit<br>```json<br>{<br>  conditions: [{<br>    type: 'liquid',<br>    liquid: `{% assign recentMessages = messages \| last: 6 %}<br>{% assign userMessages = recentMessages \| where: 'role', 'user' \| reverse %}<br>{% if userMessages.size < 3 %}<br>  false<br>{% else %}<br>  {% assign msg1 = userMessages[0].content \| downcase %}<br>  {% assign msg2 = userMessages[1].content \| downcase %}<br>  {% assign msg3 = userMessages[2].content |knowledgeBase|[CreateCustomKnowledgeBaseDTO](#schemacreatecustomknowledgebasedto)|false|none|These are the options for the knowledge base.|
|provider|string|true|none|This is the provider that will be used for the model. Any service, including your own server, that is compatible with the OpenAI API can be used.|
|metadataSendMode|string|false|none|This determines whether metadata is sent in requests to the custom provider.<br><br>- `off` will not send any metadata. payload will look like `{ messages }`<br>- `variable` will send `assistant.metadata` as a variable on the payload. payload will look like `{ messages, metadata }`<br>- `destructured` will send `assistant.metadata` fields directly on the payload. payload will look like `{ messages, ...metadata }`<br><br>Further, `variable` and `destructured` will send `call`, `phoneNumber`, and `customer` objects in the payload.<br><br>Default is `variable`.|
|headers|object|false|none|Custom headers to send with requests. These headers can override default OpenAI headers except for Authorization (which should be specified using a custom-llm credential).|
|url|string|true|none|These is the URL we'll use for the OpenAI client's `baseURL`. Ex. https://openrouter.ai/api/v1|
|wordLevelConfidenceEnabled|boolean|false|none|This determines whether the transcriber's word level confidence is sent in requests to the custom provider. Default is false.<br>This only works for Deepgram transcribers.|
|timeoutSeconds|number|false|none|This sets the timeout for the connection to the custom provider without needing to stream any tokens back. Default is 20 seconds.|
|model|string|true|none|This is the name of the model. Ex. cognitivecomputations/dolphin-mixtral-8x7b|
|temperature|number|false|none|This is the temperature that will be used for calls. Default is 0.5.|

On gpt-6-luna and claude-haiku-5-5 no cap is applied unless you set one (claude-haiku-5-5 sends its 128,000-token maximum), because reasoning uses output tokens and a small cap can leave the reply empty.|

|numFastTurns|number|false|none|This sets how many turns at the start of the conversation to use a smaller, faster model from the same provider before switching to the primary model. Example, gpt-3.5-turbo if provider is openai.<br><br>Default is 0.<br><br>@default 0|

```json
{
  "topP": 0,
  "topK": 0,
  "presencePenalty": 0,
  "frequencyPenalty": 0,
  "speechConfig": {
    "voiceConfig": {
      "prebuiltVoiceConfig": {
        "voiceName": "Puck"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|topP|number|false|none|This is the nucleus sampling parameter that controls the cumulative probability of tokens considered during text generation.<br>Only applicable with the Gemini Flash 2.0 Multimodal Live API.|
|topK|number|false|none|This is the top-k sampling parameter that limits the number of highest probability tokens considered during text generation.<br>Only applicable with the Gemini Flash 2.0 Multimodal Live API.|
|presencePenalty|number|false|none|This is the presence penalty parameter that influences the model's likelihood to repeat information by penalizing tokens based on their presence in the text.<br>Only applicable with the Gemini Flash 2.0 Multimodal Live API.|
|frequencyPenalty|number|false|none|This is the frequency penalty parameter that influences the model's likelihood to repeat tokens by penalizing them based on their frequency in the text.<br>Only applicable with the Gemini Flash 2.0 Multimodal Live API.|
|speechConfig|object|false|none|This is the speech configuration object that defines the voice settings to be used for the model's speech output.<br>Only applicable with the Gemini Flash 2.0 Multimodal Live API.|

|maxTokens|number|false|none|This is the max number of tokens that the assistant will be allowed to generate in each turn of the conversation. Default is 250. On gpt-6-luna and claude-haiku-5-5 no cap is applied unless you set one (claude-haiku-5-5 sends its 128,000-token maximum), because reasoning uses output tokens and a small cap can leave the reply empty.|

To use existing tools, use `toolIds`.<br><br>Both `tools` and `toolIds` can be used together.|
|toolIds|[string]|false|none|These are the tools that the assistant can use during the call. To use transient tools, use `tools`.<br><br>Both `tools` and `toolIds` can be used together.|
|toolRefs|[[ToolRef](#schematoolref)]|false|none|These are version-pinned references to tools. Each entry pins a specific<br>version of a tool by `(toolId, version)`. When the same `toolId` appears<br>in both `toolIds` and `toolRefs[]`, the `toolRefs` pin wins (the<br>`toolIds` entry is dropped at write time).|

|speaker|object|false|none|Configuration for the GPT-Live speaker.|
|reasoner|object|false|none|Configuration for the reasoner supporting the GPT-Live speaker.|
|provider|string|true|none|This is the provider that will be used for the model.|
|model|string|true|none|This is the OpenAI model that will be used.<br>For GPT-Live configuration and supported settings, see https://docs.vapi.ai/gpt-live/overview.<br><br>When using Vapi OpenAI or your own Azure Credentials, you have the option to specify the region for the selected model. This shouldn't be specified unless you have a specific reason to do so. Vapi will automatically find the fastest region that make sense.<br>This is helpful when you are required to comply with Data Residency rules. Learn more about Azure regions here https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/explore/global-infrastructure/data-residency/.<br><br>@default undefined|
|fallbackModels|[string]|false|none|These are the fallback models that will be used if the primary model fails. This shouldn't be specified unless you have a specific reason to do so. Vapi will automatically find the fastest fallbacks that make sense.|
|toolStrictCompatibilityMode|string|false|none|Azure OpenAI doesn't support `maxLength` right now https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/openai/how-to/structured-outputs?tabs=python-secure%2Cdotnet-entra-id&pivots=programming-language-csharp#unsupported-type-specific-keywords. Need to strip.<br><br>- `strip-parameters-with-unsupported-validation` will strip parameters with unsupported validation.<br>- `strip-unsupported-validation` will keep the parameters but strip unsupported validation.<br><br>@default `strip-unsupported-validation`|
|promptCacheRetention|string|false|none|This controls the prompt cache retention policy for models that support extended caching (GPT-4.1, GPT-5 series).<br><br>- `in_memory`: Default behavior, cache retained in GPU memory only<br>- `24h`: Extended caching, keeps cached prefixes active for up to 24 hours by offloading to GPU-local storage<br><br>Only applies to models: gpt-5.6-sol, gpt-5.6-terra, gpt-5.6-luna, gpt-5.5, chat-latest, gpt-5.4, gpt-5.4-mini, gpt-5.4-nano, gpt-5.2, gpt-5.1, gpt-5.1-codex, gpt-5.1-codex-mini, gpt-5.1-chat-latest, gpt-5, gpt-5-codex, gpt-4.1<br><br>@default undefined (uses API default which is 'in_memory')|
|promptCacheKey|string|false|none|This is the prompt cache key for models that support extended caching (GPT-4.1, GPT-5 series).<br><br>Providing a cache key allows you to share cached prefixes across requests.<br><br>@default undefined|
|serviceTier|string|false|none|This is the OpenAI service tier to request.<br><br>- `fast`: requests Fast mode, which gives faster responses at a higher per-token rate. How much faster depends on the model.<br>- `priority`: the old name for `fast`, accepted and billed the same.<br>- `default`: standard processing.<br>- `auto`: the default when unset. On Vapi's OpenAI keys this is standard processing; on your own OpenAI key, OpenAI applies your project's default tier.<br><br>OpenAI sets Fast mode rates per model, and they are not a fixed multiple of the standard rates. Vapi bills them only when OpenAI reports that it served the request in Fast mode. Otherwise the request is billed at standard rates, for example when Fast mode isn't available for the model on Vapi, OpenAI downgrades the request, or the request runs on Azure OpenAI.<br><br>Supported models and their Fast mode rates: https://docs.vapi.ai/providers/model/openai|
|reasoningEffort|string|false|none|Reasoning effort for reasoning-capable OpenAI models.<br>For `gpt-realtime-2`: forwarded to V2 stream's session.update as `reasoning.effort`.<br>For non-realtime OpenAI models, model-aware validation limits newly public<br>values while preserving the existing four-value storage contract.|
|temperature|number|false|none|This is the temperature that will be used for calls. Default is 0.5.|
|maxTokens|number|false|none|This is the max number of tokens that the assistant will be allowed to generate in each turn of the conversation. Default is 250. On gpt-6-luna and claude-haiku-5-5 no cap is applied unless you set one (claude-haiku-5-5 sends its 128,000-token maximum), because reasoning uses output tokens and a small cap can leave the reply empty.|
|emotionRecognitionEnabled|boolean|false|none|This determines whether we detect user's emotion while they speak and send it as an additional info to model.<br><br>Default `false` because the model is usually are good at understanding the user's emotion from text.<br><br>@default false|
|numFastTurns|number|false|none|This sets how many turns at the start of the conversation to use a smaller, faster model from the same provider before switching to the primary model. Example, gpt-3.5-turbo if provider is openai.<br><br>Default is 0.<br><br>@default 0|

On gpt-6-luna and claude-haiku-5-5 no cap is applied unless you set one (claude-haiku-5-5 sends its 128,000-token maximum), because reasoning uses output tokens and a small cap can leave the reply empty.|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|messages|[[OpenAIMessage](#schemaopenaimessage)]|false|none|These are the messages used to customize the prompt used for structured output extraction.<br><br>When provided, these messages replace the default prompts. For text extraction, message contents support LiquidJS templating with the following variables:<br>- `{{transcript}}`, `{{messages}}`, or `{{messagesWithConfidence}}` to reference the conversation (one is required)<br>- `{{structuredOutput.name}}`, `{{structuredOutput.description}}`, or `{{structuredOutput.schema}}` to reference the structured output definition (one is required)<br>- `{{systemPrompt}}`, `{{callEndedReason}}`, `{{duration}}`, `{{startedAt}}`, `{{endedAt}}`, and any `assistantOverrides.variableValues`<br><br>In structured outputs, `{{messages}}` includes conversation text and tool calls/results, but omits caller transcription-confidence fields. For text extraction, `{{messagesWithConfidence}}` includes the original message history with transcription confidence for outputs that explicitly need it.   ],

```json
  "maxTokens": 50
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|messages|[[OpenAIMessage](#schemaopenaimessage)]|false|none|These are the messages used to customize the prompt used for structured output extraction.<br><br>When provided, these messages replace the default prompts. For text extraction, message contents support LiquidJS templating with the following variables:<br>- `{{transcript}}`, `{{messages}}`, or `{{messagesWithConfidence}}` to reference the conversation (one is required)<br>- `{{structuredOutput.name}}`, `{{structuredOutput.description}}`, or `{{structuredOutput.schema}}` to reference the structured output definition (one is required)<br>- `{{systemPrompt}}`, `{{callEndedReason}}`, `{{duration}}`, `{{startedAt}}`, `{{endedAt}}`, and any `assistantOverrides.variableValues`<br><br>In structured outputs, `{{messages}}` includes conversation text and tool calls/results, but omits caller transcription-confidence fields. For text extraction, `{{messagesWithConfidence}}` includes the original message history with transcription confidence for outputs that explicitly need it. These variables also apply in structured-output schema descriptions. Audio-targeted (`messages-with-audio`) extraction ignores custom messages. Stored call artifacts and API messages retain their confidence data. `{{transcript}}` is the spoken text only, which uses significantly fewer tokens.<br><br>If not provided, default system and user prompts are used.|
|provider|string|true|none|This is the provider of the model (`custom-llm`).|
|metadataSendMode|string|false|none|This determines whether metadata is sent in requests to the custom provider.<br><br>- `off` will not send any metadata. payload will look like `{ messages }`<br>- `variable` will send `assistant.metadata` as a variable on the payload. payload will look like `{ messages, metadata }`<br>- `destructured` will send `assistant.metadata` fields directly on the payload. payload will look like `{ messages, ...metadata }`<br><br>Further, `variable` and `destructured` will send `call`, `phoneNumber`, and `customer` objects in the payload.<br><br>Default is `variable`.|
|url|string|true|none|These is the URL we'll use for the OpenAI client's `baseURL`. Ex. https://openrouter.ai/api/v1|
|headers|object|false|none|These are the headers we'll use for the OpenAI client's `headers`.|
|timeoutSeconds|number|false|none|This sets the timeout for the connection to the custom provider without needing to stream any tokens back. Default is 20 seconds.|
|model|string|true|none|This is the name of the model. Ex. cognitivecomputations/dolphin-mixtral-8x7b|
|temperature|number|false|none|This is the temperature of the model.|
|maxTokens|number|false|none|This is the max tokens of the model.|

<h2 id="tocS_TwilioVoicemailDetectionPlan">TwilioVoicemailDetectionPlan</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematwiliovoicemaildetectionplan"></a>
<a id="schema_TwilioVoicemailDetectionPlan"></a>
<a id="tocStwiliovoicemaildetectionplan"></a>
<a id="tocstwiliovoicemaildetectionplan"></a>

```json
{
  "provider": "twilio",
  "voicemailDetectionTypes": [
    "machine_end_beep",
    "machine_end_silence"
  ],
  "enabled": true,
  "machineDetectionTimeout": 3,
  "machineDetectionSpeechThreshold": 1000,
  "machineDetectionSpeechEndThreshold": 500,
  "machineDetectionSilenceTimeout": 2000
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|provider|string|true|none|This is the provider to use for voicemail detection.|
|voicemailDetectionTypes|[string]|false|none|These are the AMD messages from Twilio that are considered as voicemail. Default is ['machine_end_beep', 'machine_end_silence'].<br><br>@default {Array} ['machine_end_beep', 'machine_end_silence']|
|enabled|boolean|false|none|This sets whether the assistant should detect voicemail. Defaults to true.<br><br>@default true|
|machineDetectionTimeout|number|false|none|The number of seconds that Twilio should attempt to perform answering machine detection before timing out and returning AnsweredBy as unknown. Default is 30 seconds.<br><br>Increasing this value will provide the engine more time to make a determination. This can be useful when DetectMessageEnd is provided in the MachineDetection parameter and there is an expectation of long answering machine greetings that can exceed 30 seconds.<br><br>Decreasing this value will reduce the amount of time the engine has to make a determination. This can be particularly useful when the Enable option is provided in the MachineDetection parameter and you want to limit the time for initial detection.<br><br>Check the [Twilio docs](https://www.twilio.com/docs/voice/answering-machine-detection#optional-api-tuning-parameters) for more info.<br><br>@default 30|
|machineDetectionSpeechThreshold|number|false|none|The number of milliseconds that is used as the measuring stick for the length of the speech activity. Durations lower than this value will be interpreted as a human, longer as a machine. Default is 2400 milliseconds.<br><br>Increasing this value will reduce the chance of a False Machine (detected machine, actually human) for a long human greeting (e.g., a business greeting) but increase the time it takes to detect a machine.<br><br>Decreasing this value will reduce the chances of a False Human (detected human, actually machine) for short voicemail greetings. The value of this parameter may need to be reduced by more than 1000ms to detect very short voicemail greetings. A reduction of that significance can result in increased False Machine detections. Adjusting the MachineDetectionSpeechEndThreshold is likely the better approach for short voicemails. Decreasing MachineDetectionSpeechThreshold will also reduce the time it takes to detect a machine.<br><br>Check the [Twilio docs](https://www.twilio.com/docs/voice/answering-machine-detection#optional-api-tuning-parameters) for more info.<br><br>@default 2400|
|machineDetectionSpeechEndThreshold|number|false|none|The number of milliseconds of silence after speech activity at which point the speech activity is considered complete. Default is 1200 milliseconds.<br><br>Increasing this value will typically be used to better address the short voicemail greeting scenarios. For short voicemails, there is typically 1000-2000ms of audio followed by 1200-2400ms of silence and then additional audio before the beep. Increasing the MachineDetectionSpeechEndThreshold to ~2500ms will treat the 1200-2400ms of silence as a gap in the greeting but not the end of the greeting and will result in a machine detection. The downsides of such a change include:<br>- Increasing the delay for human detection by the amount you increase this parameter, e.g., a change of 1200ms to 2500ms increases human detection delay by 1300ms.<br>- Cases where a human has two utterances separated by a period of silence (e.g. a "Hello", then 2000ms of silence, and another "Hello") may be interpreted as a machine.<br><br>Decreasing this value will result in faster human detection. The consequence is that it can lead to increased False Human (detected human, actually machine) detections because a silence gap in a voicemail greeting (not necessarily just in short voicemail scenarios) can be incorrectly interpreted as the end of speech.<br><br>Check the [Twilio docs](https://www.twilio.com/docs/voice/answering-machine-detection#optional-api-tuning-parameters) for more info.<br><br>@default 1200|
|machineDetectionSilenceTimeout|number|false|none|The number of milliseconds of initial silence after which an unknown AnsweredBy result will be returned. Default is 5000 milliseconds.<br><br>Increasing this value will result in waiting for a longer period of initial silence before returning an 'unknown' AMD result.<br><br>Decreasing this value will result in waiting for a shorter period of initial silence before returning an 'unknown' AMD result.<br><br>Check the [Twilio docs](https://www.twilio.com/docs/voice/answering-machine-detection#optional-api-tuning-parameters) for more info.<br><br>@default 5000|

|voicemailDetectionTypes|fax|

|voicemailDetectionTypes|machine_end_beep|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|triggerResetMode|string|false|none|This is whether the counter for hook trigger resets the user speaks.<br><br>@default never|
|timeoutSeconds|number|true|none|This is the timeout in seconds before action is triggered.<br>The clock starts when the assistant finishes speaking and remains active until the user speaks.<br><br>@default 7.5<br>@minimum 2<br>@maximum 1000|
|triggerMaxCount|number|false|none|This is the maximum number of times the hook will trigger in a call.<br><br>@default 3|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|triggerResetMode|onUserSpeech|
|triggerResetMode|never|

```json
{
  "on": "string",
  "do": [
    {
      "type": "say",
      "exact": "Are you still there?",
      "prompt": "Ask the user if they're still in the call"
    }
  ],
  "options": {
    "triggerResetMode": "onUserSpeech",
    "timeoutSeconds": 1,
    "triggerMaxCount": 1
  },
  "name": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|on|string|true|none|Must be either "customer.speech.timeout" or match the pattern "customer.speech.timeout[property=value]"|
|do|[[SayHookAction](#schemasayhookaction) \| [ToolCallHookAction](#schematoolcallhookaction) \| [MessageAddHookAction](#schemamessageaddhookaction)]|true|none|This is the set of actions to perform when the hook triggers|
|options|object|false|none|This is the set of filters that must match for the hook to trigger|
|name|string|false|none|This is the name of the hook, it can be set by the user to identify the hook.<br>If no name is provided, the hook will be auto generated as UUID.<br><br>@default UUID|

|name|string|true|none|none|
|edges|[[Edge](#schemaedge)]|true|none|none|
|globalPrompt|string|false|none|none|
|server|object|false|none|This is where Vapi will send webhooks. You can find all webhooks available along with their shape in ServerMessage schema.<br><br>The order of precedence is:<br><br>1. tool.server<br>2. workflow.server / assistant.server<br>3. phoneNumber.server<br>4. org.server|
|compliancePlan|object|false|none|This is the compliance plan for the workflow. It allows you to configure HIPAA and other compliance settings.|
|analysisPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan for analysis of workflow's calls. Stored in `call.analysis`.|
|artifactPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan for artifacts generated during workflow's calls. Stored in `call.artifact`.|
|startSpeakingPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan for when the workflow nodes should start talking.<br><br>You should configure this if you're running into these issues:<br>- The assistant is too slow to start talking after the customer is done speaking.<br>- The assistant is too fast to start talking after the customer is done speaking.<br>- The assistant is so fast that it's actually interrupting the customer.|
|stopSpeakingPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan for when workflow nodes should stop talking on customer interruption.<br><br>You should configure this if you're running into these issues:<br>- The assistant is too slow to recognize customer's interruption.<br>- The assistant is too fast to recognize customer's interruption.<br>- The assistant is getting interrupted by phrases that are just acknowledgments.<br>- The assistant is getting interrupted by background noises.<br>- The assistant is not properly stopping -- it starts talking right after getting interrupted.|
|monitorPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan for real-time monitoring of the workflow's calls.<br><br>Usage:<br>- To enable live listening of the workflow's calls, set `monitorPlan.listenEnabled` to `true`.<br>- To enable live control of the workflow's calls, set `monitorPlan.controlEnabled` to `true`.|
|backgroundSpeechDenoisingPlan|object|false|none|This enables filtering of noise and background speech while the user is talking.<br><br>Features:<br>- Smart denoising using Krisp<br>- Fourier denoising<br><br>Both can be used together. Order of precedence:<br>- Smart denoising<br>- Fourier denoising|
|credentialIds|[string]|false|none|These are the credentials that will be used for the workflow calls. By default, all the credentials are available for use in the call but you can provide a subset using this.|
|keypadInputPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan for keypad input handling during workflow calls.|
|voicemailMessage|string|false|none|This is the message that the assistant will say if the call is forwarded to voicemail.<br><br>If unspecified, it will hang up.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|This is the exact replacement type. You can use this to replace a specific word or phrase with a different word or phrase.<br><br>Usage:<br>- Replace "hello" with "hi": { type: 'exact', key: 'hello', value: 'hi' }<br>- Replace "good morning" with "good day": { type: 'exact', key: 'good morning', value: 'good day' }<br>- Replace a specific name: { type: 'exact', key: 'John Doe', value: 'Jane Smith' }<br>- Replace an acronym: { type: 'exact', key: 'AI', value: 'Artificial Intelligence' }<br>- Replace a company name with its phonetic pronunciation: { type: 'exact', key: 'Vapi', value: 'Vappy' }|
|replaceAllEnabled|boolean|false|none|This option let's you control whether to replace all instances of the key or only the first one. By default, it only replaces the first instance.<br>Examples:<br>- For { type: 'exact', key: 'hello', value: 'hi', replaceAllEnabled: false }. Before: "hello world, hello universe" \| After: "hi world, hello universe"<br>- For { type: 'exact', key: 'hello', value: 'hi', replaceAllEnabled: true }. Before: "hello world, hello universe" \| After: "hi world, hi universe"<br>@default false|
|key|string|true|none|This is the key to replace.|
|value|string|true|none|This is the value that will replace the match.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|exact|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|This is the regex replacement type. You can use this to replace a word or phrase that matches a pattern.<br><br>Usage:<br>- Replace all numbers with "some number": { type: 'regex', regex: '\\d+', value: 'some number' }<br>- Replace email addresses with "[EMAIL]": { type: 'regex', regex: '\\b[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\\.[A-Z\|a-z]{2,}\\b', value: '[EMAIL]' }<br>- Replace phone numbers with a formatted version: { type: 'regex', regex: '(\\d{3})(\\d{3})(\\d{4})', value: '($1) $2-$3' }<br>- Replace all instances of "color" or "colour" with "hue": { type: 'regex', regex: 'colou?r', value: 'hue' }<br>- Capitalize the first letter of every sentence: { type: 'regex', regex: '(?<=\\. \|^)[a-z]', value: (match) => match.toUpperCase() }|
|regex|string|true|none|This is the regex pattern to replace.<br><br>Note:<br>- This works by using the `string.replace` method in Node.JS. Eg. `"hello there".replace(/hello/g, "hi")` will return `"hi there"`.<br><br>Hot tip:<br>- In JavaScript, escape `\` when sending the regex pattern. Eg. `"hello\sthere"` will be sent over the wire as `"hellosthere"`. Send `"hello\\sthere"` instead.|
|options|[[RegexOption](#schemaregexoption)]|false|none|These are the options for the regex replacement. Defaults to all disabled.<br><br>@default []|
|value|string|true|none|This is the value that will replace the match.|

```json
  "numberToDigitsCutoff": 2025,

    {

      "value": "string"
    }
  ],
  "formattersEnabled": "markdown"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enabled|boolean|false|none|This determines whether the chunk is formatted before being sent to the voice provider. This helps with enunciation. This includes phone numbers, emails and addresses. Default `true`.<br><br>Usage:<br>- To rely on the voice provider's formatting logic, set this to `false`.<br><br>If `voice.chunkPlan.enabled` is `false`, this is automatically `false` since there's no chunk to format.<br><br>@default true|
|numberToDigitsCutoff|number|false|none|This is the cutoff after which a number is converted to individual digits instead of being spoken as words.<br><br>Example:<br>- If cutoff 2025, "12345" is converted to "1 2 3 4 5" while "1200" is converted to "twelve hundred".<br><br>Usage:<br>- If your use case doesn't involve IDs like zip codes, set this to a high value.<br>- If your use case involves IDs that are shorter than 5 digits, set this to a lower value.<br><br>@default 2025|
|replacements|[[ExactReplacement](#schemaexactreplacement) \| [RegexReplacement](#schemaregexreplacement)]|false|none|These are the custom replacements you can make to the chunk before it is sent to the voice provider.<br><br>Usage:<br>- To replace a specific word or phrase with a different word or phrase, use the `ExactReplacement` type. Eg. `{ type: 'exact', key: 'hello', value: 'hi' }`<br>- To replace a word or phrase that matches a pattern, use the `RegexReplacement` type. Eg. `{ type: 'regex', regex: '\\b[a-zA-Z]{5}\\b', value: 'hi' }`<br><br>@default []|
|formattersEnabled|[string]|false|none|List of formatters to apply. If not provided, all default formatters will be applied.<br>If provided, only the specified formatters will be applied.<br>Note: Some essential formatters like angle bracket removal will always be applied.<br>@default undefined|

|speed|number|false|none|Defines the speed for voice settings. Ignored by `eleven_v4_turbo` and `eleven_v3_conversational`.|
|optimizeStreamingLatency|number|false|none|Defines the optimize streaming latency for voice settings. Defaults to 3. Ignored by `eleven_v4_turbo` and `eleven_v3_conversational`.|
|enableSsmlParsing|boolean|false|none|This enables the use of https://elevenlabs.io/docs/speech-synthesis/prompting#pronunciation. Defaults to false to save latency. Ignored by `eleven_v4_turbo` and `eleven_v3_conversational`.<br><br>@default false|

|language|string|false|none|This is the language (ISO 639-1) that is enforced for the model. Currently only Turbo v2.5, Flash v2.5 and the Text to Dialogue models support language enforcement; other models ignore it.|

|emotion|string|false|none|An emotion to be applied to the speech.|
|voiceGuidance|number|false|none|A number between 1 and 6. Use lower numbers to reduce how unique your chosen voice will be compared to other voices.|
|styleGuidance|number|false|none|A number between 1 and 30. Use lower numbers to to reduce how strong your chosen emotion will be. Higher numbers will create a very emotional performance.|
|textGuidance|number|false|none|A number between 1 and 2. This number influences how closely the generated speech adheres to the input text. Use lower values to create more fluid speech, but with a higher chance of deviating from the input text. Higher numbers will make the generated speech more accurate to the input text, ensuring that the words spoken align closely with the provided text.|
|model|string|false|none|Playht voice model/engine to use.|
|language|string|false|none|The language to use for the speech.|
|chunkPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan for chunking the model output before it is sent to the voice provider.|
|fallbackPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan for voice provider fallbacks in the event that the primary voice provider fails.|

|phonemizeBetweenBrackets|boolean|false|none|This is a flag that controls whether text inside brackets should be phonemized (converted to phonetic pronunciation) - Example: "{h'El.o} World" will pronounce "Hello" as expected.|
|reduceLatency|boolean|false|none|This is a flag that controls whether to optimize for reduced latency in streaming. https://docs.rime.ai/api-reference/endpoint/websockets#param-reduce-latency|
|inlineSpeedAlpha|string|false|none|This is a string that allows inline speed control using alpha notation. https://docs.rime.ai/api-reference/endpoint/websockets#param-inline-speed-alpha|
|language|string|false|none|Language for speech synthesis. Uses ISO 639 codes. Supported: en, es, de, fr, ar, hi, ja, he, pt, ta, si.|

The temperature parameter controls variance. Lower temperatures result in more predictable results, higher temperatures allow each run to vary more, so the voice may sound less like the baseline voice.|
|emotion|string|false|none|An emotion to be applied to the speech.|
|voiceGuidance|number|false|none|A number between 1 and 6. Use lower numbers to reduce how unique your chosen voice will be compared to other voices.|

|textGuidance|number|false|none|A number between 1 and 2. This number influences how closely the generated speech adheres to the input text. Use lower values to create more fluid speech, but with a higher chance of deviating from the input text. Higher numbers will make the generated speech more accurate to the input text, ensuring that the words spoken align closely with the provided text.|
|model|string|false|none|Playht voice model/engine to use.|
|language|string|false|none|The language to use for the speech.|
|chunkPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan for chunking the model output before it is sent to the voice provider.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cachingEnabled|boolean|false|none|This is the flag to toggle voice caching for the assistant.|
|provider|string|true|none|This is the voice provider that will be used.|
|voiceId|string|true|none|This is the provider-specific ID that will be used.|
|model|string|false|none|This is the model that will be used. Defaults to 'arcana' when not specified.|
|speed|number|false|none|This is the speed multiplier that will be used.|
|pauseBetweenBrackets|boolean|false|none|This is a flag that controls whether to add slight pauses using angle brackets. Example: "Hi. <200> I'd love to have a conversation with you." adds a 200ms pause between the first and second sentences.|
|phonemizeBetweenBrackets|boolean|false|none|This is a flag that controls whether text inside brackets should be phonemized (converted to phonetic pronunciation) - Example: "{h'El.o} World" will pronounce "Hello" as expected.|
|reduceLatency|boolean|false|none|This is a flag that controls whether to optimize for reduced latency in streaming. https://docs.rime.ai/api-reference/endpoint/websockets#param-reduce-latency|
|inlineSpeedAlpha|string|false|none|This is a string that allows inline speed control using alpha notation. https://docs.rime.ai/api-reference/endpoint/websockets#param-inline-speed-alpha|
|language|string|false|none|Language for speech synthesis. Uses ISO 639 codes. Supported: en, es, de, fr, ar, hi, ja, he, pt, ta, si.|
|chunkPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan for chunking the model output before it is sent to the voice provider.|

```json
  "provider": "twilio",

  "record": false,
  "recordingChannels": "mono"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|provider|string|true|none|none|
|timeout|number|false|none|The integer number of seconds that we should allow the phone to ring before assuming there is no answer.<br>The default is `60` seconds and the maximum is `600` seconds.<br>For some call flows, we will add a 5-second buffer to the timeout value you provide.<br>For this reason, a timeout value of 10 seconds could result in an actual timeout closer to 15 seconds.<br>You can set this to a short time, such as `15` seconds, to hang up before reaching an answering machine or voicemail.<br><br>@default 60|
|record|boolean|false|none|Whether to record the call.<br>Can be `true` to record the phone call, or `false` to not.<br>The default is `false`.<br><br>@default false|
|recordingChannels|string|false|none|The number of channels in the final recording.<br>Can be: `mono` or `dual`.<br>The default is `mono`.<br>`mono` records both legs of the call in a single channel of the recording file.<br>`dual` records each leg to a separate channel of the recording file.<br>The first channel of a dual-channel recording contains the parent call and the second channel contains the child call.<br><br>@default 'mono'|

<h2 id="tocS_SipTrunkGateway">SipTrunkGateway</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemasiptrunkgateway"></a>
<a id="schema_SipTrunkGateway"></a>
<a id="tocSsiptrunkgateway"></a>
<a id="tocssiptrunkgateway"></a>

```json
{
  "ip": "string",
  "port": 1,
  "netmask": 24,
  "inboundEnabled": true,
  "outboundEnabled": true,
  "outboundProtocol": "tls/srtp",
  "optionsPingEnabled": true
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ip|string|true|none|This is the address of the gateway. Inbound gateways require an IPv4 address like 1.1.1.1. Outbound-only gateways can also use a fully qualified domain name like my-sip-trunk.pstn.twilio.com.|
|port|number|false|none|This is the port number of the gateway. Default is 5060.<br><br>@default 5060|
|netmask|number|false|none|This is the netmask of the gateway. Defaults to 32.<br><br>@default 32|
|inboundEnabled|boolean|false|none|This is whether inbound calls are allowed from this gateway. Default is true.<br><br>@default true|
|outboundEnabled|boolean|false|none|This is whether outbound calls should be sent to this gateway. Default is true.<br><br>Note, if netmask is less than 32, it doesn't affect the outbound IPs that are tried. 1 attempt is made to `ip:port`.<br><br>@default true|
|outboundProtocol|string|false|none|This is the protocol to use for SIP signaling outbound calls. Default is udp.<br><br>@default udp|
|optionsPingEnabled|boolean|false|none|This is whether to send options ping to the gateway. This can be used to check if the gateway is reachable. Default is false.<br><br>This is useful for high availability setups where you want to check if the gateway is reachable before routing calls to it. Note, if no gateway for a trunk is reachable, outbound calls will be rejected.<br><br>@default false|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|

|outboundProtocol|tls/srtp|
|outboundProtocol|tcp|
|outboundProtocol|tls|
|outboundProtocol|udp|

<h2 id="tocS_BucketPlan">BucketPlan</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->

```json
  "name": "string",
  "region": "string",
  "path": "string",
  "hmacAccessKey": "string",
  "hmacSecret": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|true|none|This is the name of the bucket.|
|region|string|false|none|This is the region of the bucket.<br><br>Usage:<br>- If `credential.type` is `aws`, then this is required.<br>- If `credential.type` is `gcp`, then this is optional since GCP allows buckets to be accessed without a region but region is required for data residency requirements. Read here: https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/request-endpoints<br><br>This overrides the `credential.region` field if it is provided.|
|path|string|false|none|This is the path where call artifacts will be stored.<br><br>Usage:<br>- To store call artifacts in a specific folder, set this to the full path. Eg. "/folder-name1/folder-name2".<br>- To store call artifacts in the root of the bucket, leave this blank.<br><br>@default "/"|
|hmacAccessKey|string|false|none|This is the HMAC access key offered by GCP for interoperability with S3 clients. Here is the guide on how to create: https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/authentication/managing-hmackeys#console<br><br>Usage:<br>- If `credential.type` is `gcp`, then this is required.<br>- If `credential.type` is `aws`, then this is not required since credential.awsAccessKeyId is used instead.|
|hmacSecret|string|false|none|This is the secret for the HMAC access key. Here is the guide on how to create: https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/authentication/managing-hmackeys#console<br><br>Usage:<br>- If `credential.type` is `gcp`, then this is required.<br>- If `credential.type` is `aws`, then this is not required since credential.awsSecretAccessKey is used instead.<br><br>Note: This is not returned in the API.|

\| [CreateEmailCredentialDTO](#schemacreateemailcredentialdto) \| [CreateSlackWebhookCredentialDTO](#schemacreateslackwebhookcredentialdto)]|false|none|These are dynamic credentials that will be used for the assistant calls. By default, all the credentials are available for use in the call but you can supplement an additional credentials using this. Dynamic credentials override existing credentials.|
|hooks|[[CallHookCallEnding](#schemacallhookcallending) \| [CallHookAssistantSpeechInterrupted](#schemacallhookassistantspeechinterrupted) \| [CallHookCustomerSpeechInterrupted](#schemacallhookcustomerspeechinterrupted) \| [CallHookCustomerSpeechTimeout](#schemacallhookcustomerspeechtimeout) \| [SessionCreatedHook](#schemasessioncreatedhook)]|false|none|This is a set of actions that will be performed on certain events.|
|name|string|false|none|This is the name of the assistant.<br><br>This is required when you want to transfer between assistants in a call.|
|voicemailMessage|string|false|none|This is the message that the assistant will say if the call is forwarded to voicemail.<br><br>If unspecified, it will hang up.|
|endCallMessage|string|false|none|This is the message that the assistant will say if it ends the call.<br><br>If unspecified, it will hang up without saying anything.|
|endCallPhrases|[string]|false|none|This list contains phrases that, if spoken by the assistant, will trigger the call to be hung up. Case insensitive.|
|compliancePlan|[CompliancePlan](#schemacomplianceplan)|false|none|none|
|metadata|object|false|none|This is for metadata you want to store on the assistant.|
|backgroundSpeechDenoisingPlan|object|false|none|This enables filtering of noise and background speech while the user is talking.<br><br>Features:<br>- Smart denoising using Krisp<br>- Fourier denoising<br><br>Smart denoising can be combined with or used independently of Fourier denoising.<br><br>Order of precedence:<br>- Smart denoising<br>- Fourier denoising|
|analysisPlan|object|false|none|**Deprecated.** This is the plan for analysis of assistant's calls. Stored in `call.analysis`.|
|artifactPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan for artifacts generated during assistant's calls. Stored in `call.artifact`.|
|startSpeakingPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan for when the assistant should start talking.<br><br>You should configure this if you're running into these issues:<br>- The assistant is too slow to start talking after the customer is done speaking.<br>- The assistant is too fast to start talking after the customer is done speaking.<br>- The assistant is so fast that it's actually interrupting the customer.|
|stopSpeakingPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan for when assistant should stop talking on customer interruption.<br><br>You should configure this if you're running into these issues:<br>- The assistant is too slow to recognize customer's interruption.<br>- The assistant is too fast to recognize customer's interruption.<br>- The assistant is getting interrupted by phrases that are just acknowledgments.<br>- The assistant is getting interrupted by background noises.<br>- The assistant is not properly stopping -- it starts talking right after getting interrupted.|
|monitorPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan for real-time monitoring of the assistant's calls.<br><br>Usage:<br>- To enable live listening of the assistant's calls, set `monitorPlan.listenEnabled` to `true`.<br>- To enable live control of the assistant's calls, set `monitorPlan.controlEnabled` to `true`.<br>- To attach monitors to the assistant, set `monitorPlan.monitorIds` to the set of monitor ids.|
|credentialIds|[string]|false|none|These are the credentials that will be used for the assistant calls. By default, all the credentials are available for use in the call but you can provide a subset using this.|
|server|object|false|none|This is where Vapi will send webhooks. You can find all webhooks available along with their shape in ServerMessage schema.<br><br>The order of precedence is:<br><br>1. assistant.server.url<br>2. phoneNumber.serverUrl<br>3. org.serverUrl|
|keypadInputPlan|[KeypadInputPlan](#schemakeypadinputplan)|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_ModelDeprecationNotice">ModelDeprecationNotice</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemamodeldeprecationnotice"></a>
<a id="schema_ModelDeprecationNotice"></a>
<a id="tocSmodeldeprecationnotice"></a>
<a id="tocsmodeldeprecationnotice"></a>

```json
{
  "slot": "model.fallbackModels[1]",
  "provider": "openai",
  "model": "gpt-4-1106-preview",
  "deprecationDate": "2025-09-26",
  "retirementDate": "2026-03-26",
  "replacementStatus": "manual-action-required",
  "replacementModel": "gpt-5"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|slot|string|true|none|Path of the slot that carries the model, relative to the response root,<br>e.g. `model`, `model.fallbackModels[1]`, `transcriber`, `voice`, or<br>`members[2].assistantOverrides.model` on a squad.|
|provider|string|true|none|Provider as stored on the slot.|
|model|string|true|none|Model name as stored on the slot.|
|deprecationDate|string|true|none|Day the model became deprecated, `YYYY-MM-DD` in UTC.|
|retirementDate|string|true|none|Day the model is or was retired, `YYYY-MM-DD` in UTC. On and after this<br>day Vapi no longer runs the model as configured.|
|replacementStatus|string|true|none|Whether a replacement can be recommended for this configuration.|
|replacementModel|string|false|none|Recommended model when replacementStatus is available. Omitted when<br>eligibility cannot be established or no eligible replacement exists.<br>A recommendation reflects the response-time decision; it neither<br>confirms a completed swap nor authorizes a future execution.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|replacementStatus|available|
|replacementStatus|manual-action-required|

|hooks|[[CallHookCallEnding](#schemacallhookcallending) \| [CallHookAssistantSpeechInterrupted](#schemacallhookassistantspeechinterrupted) \| [CallHookCustomerSpeechInterrupted](#schemacallhookcustomerspeechinterrupted) \| [CallHookCustomerSpeechTimeout](#schemacallhookcustomerspeechtimeout) \| [SessionCreatedHook](#schemasessioncreatedhook)]|false|none|This is a set of actions that will be performed on certain events.|
|versionName|string \| null|false|none|Optional human-readable label for this version. Pass `null` to clear.|
|versionDescription|string \| null|false|none|Optional description for this version. Pass `null` to clear.|
|id|string(uuid)|true|none|This is the unique identifier for the version row.|
|orgId|string(uuid)|true|none|This is the unique identifier for the org that owns this version.|
|assistantId|string(uuid)|true|none|This is the unique identifier for the assistant this version was snapshotted from.|
|version|string|true|none|This is the public monotonic version label, e.g. "v1".<br>System-owned and incremented per assistant; never user-supplied.|
|configHash|string|true|none|This is the SHA-256 hex of the snapshotted content used for no-op detection.|
|parentVersion|string \| null|false|none|This is the prior version label (vN-1). Null on v1 or for branch roots.|
|restoredFromVersion|string \| null|false|none|The version this version was restored from. Null when it was not restored.|
|createdBy|string \| null|false|none|This is the actor that wrote this version. Email when created via JWT, null when created via API.|
|deletedAt|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|This is the soft-delete timestamp. Null when active.|
|createdAt|string(date-time)|true|none|This is the ISO 8601 date-time string of when the version was created.|
|modelDeprecations|[[ModelDeprecationNotice](#schemamodeldeprecationnotice)]|false|none|Read-only. Present only when a model this configuration uses is deprecated or retired in Vapi's model deprecation registry, judged on the day of the response. Each entry names the slot (for example `model` or `model.fallbackModels[1]`), provider, stored model, and deprecation and retirement dates as `YYYY-MM-DD` in UTC. `replacementStatus` is `available` with a `replacementModel` when a replacement can be recommended, or `manual-action-required` with no replacement model when eligibility is unknown or no eligible replacement exists. `manual-action-required` can be transient when compliance context is unavailable; re-fetch before acting. HIPAA-required configurations, sparse drafts, and squads with unresolved assistant references currently require manual action. HIPAA requirements include the organization and assistant settings, including HIPAA with data retention. Recommendations reflect the response-time decision; they do not confirm a swap or authorize future execution. Examples: an available recommendation includes `{"replacementStatus":"available","replacementModel":"gpt-5"}`; a blocked recommendation includes `{"replacementStatus":"manual-action-required"}`. Ignored if sent back in a create or update request.|
|name|string|false|none|This is the name of the assistant.<br><br>This is required when you want to transfer between assistants in a call.|
|voicemailMessage|string|false|none|This is the message that the assistant will say if the call is forwarded to voicemail.<br><br>If unspecified, it will hang up.|
|endCallMessage|string|false|none|This is the message that the assistant will say if it ends the call.<br><br>If unspecified, it will hang up without saying anything.|
|endCallPhrases|[string]|false|none|This list contains phrases that, if spoken by the assistant, will trigger the call to be hung up. Case insensitive.|
|compliancePlan|[CompliancePlan](#schemacomplianceplan)|false|none|none|
|metadata|object|false|none|This is for metadata you want to store on the assistant.|
|backgroundSpeechDenoisingPlan|object|false|none|This enables filtering of noise and background speech while the user is talking.<br><br>Features:<br>- Smart denoising using Krisp<br>- Fourier denoising<br><br>Smart denoising can be combined with or used independently of Fourier denoising.<br><br>Order of precedence:<br>- Smart denoising<br>- Fourier denoising|
|analysisPlan|object|false|none|**Deprecated.** This is the plan for analysis of assistant's calls. Stored in `call.analysis`.|
|artifactPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan for artifacts generated during assistant's calls. Stored in `call.artifact`.|
|startSpeakingPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan for when the assistant should start talking.<br><br>You should configure this if you're running into these issues:<br>- The assistant is too slow to start talking after the customer is done speaking.<br>- The assistant is too fast to start talking after the customer is done speaking.<br>- The assistant is so fast that it's actually interrupting the customer.|
|stopSpeakingPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan for when assistant should stop talking on customer interruption.<br><br>You should configure this if you're running into these issues:<br>- The assistant is too slow to recognize customer's interruption.<br>- The assistant is too fast to recognize customer's interruption.<br>- The assistant is getting interrupted by phrases that are just acknowledgments.<br>- The assistant is getting interrupted by background noises.<br>- The assistant is not properly stopping -- it starts talking right after getting interrupted.|
|monitorPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan for real-time monitoring of the assistant's calls.<br><br>Usage:<br>- To enable live listening of the assistant's calls, set `monitorPlan.listenEnabled` to `true`.<br>- To enable live control of the assistant's calls, set `monitorPlan.controlEnabled` to `true`.<br>- To attach monitors to the assistant, set `monitorPlan.monitorIds` to the set of monitor ids.|
|credentialIds|[string]|false|none|These are the credentials that will be used for the assistant calls. By default, all the credentials are available for use in the call but you can provide a subset using this.|
|server|object|false|none|This is where Vapi will send webhooks. You can find all webhooks available along with their shape in ServerMessage schema.<br><br>The order of precedence is:<br><br>1. assistant.server.url<br>2. phoneNumber.serverUrl<br>3. org.serverUrl|
|keypadInputPlan|[KeypadInputPlan](#schemakeypadinputplan)|false|none|none|

|stopSpeakingPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan for when assistant should stop talking on customer interruption.<br><br>You should configure this if you're running into these issues:<br>- The assistant is too slow to recognize customer's interruption.<br>- The assistant is too fast to recognize customer's interruption.<br>- The assistant is getting interrupted by phrases that are just acknowledgments.<br>- The assistant is getting interrupted by background noises.<br>- The assistant is not properly stopping -- it starts talking right after getting interrupted.|

Immutable for the lifetime of the draft.|


### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|latestVersion|string \| null|false|none|This is the latest version label (e.g. `v3`) of the squad in the version<br>history. `null` while the org is not yet onboarded to versioning, or for<br>squads that have not yet been published under it.|
|modelDeprecations|[[ModelDeprecationNotice](#schemamodeldeprecationnotice)]|false|none|Read-only. Present only when a model this configuration uses is deprecated or retired in Vapi's model deprecation registry, judged on the day of the response. Each entry names the slot (for example `model` or `model.fallbackModels[1]`), provider, stored model, and deprecation and retirement dates as `YYYY-MM-DD` in UTC. `replacementStatus` is `available` with a `replacementModel` when a replacement can be recommended, or `manual-action-required` with no replacement model when eligibility is unknown or no eligible replacement exists. `manual-action-required` can be transient when compliance context is unavailable; re-fetch before acting. HIPAA-required configurations, sparse drafts, and squads with unresolved assistant references currently require manual action. HIPAA requirements include the organization and assistant settings, including HIPAA with data retention. Recommendations reflect the response-time decision; they do not confirm a swap or authorize future execution. Examples: an available recommendation includes `{"replacementStatus":"available","replacementModel":"gpt-5"}`; a blocked recommendation includes `{"replacementStatus":"manual-action-required"}`. Ignored if sent back in a create or update request.|
|name|string|false|none|This is the name of the squad.|
|members|[[SquadMemberDTO](#schemasquadmemberdto)]|true|none|This is the list of assistants that make up the squad.<br><br>The call will start with the first assistant in the list.|
|membersOverrides|object|false|none|This can be used to override all the assistants' settings and provide values for their template variables.<br><br>Both `membersOverrides` and `members[n].assistantOverrides` can be used together. First, `members[n].assistantOverrides` is applied. Then, `membersOverrides` is applied as a global override.|
|id|string|true|none|This is the unique identifier for the squad.|
|orgId|string|true|none|This is the unique identifier for the org that this squad belongs to.|
|createdAt|string(date-time)|true|none|This is the ISO 8601 date-time string of when the squad was created.|
|updatedAt|string(date-time)|true|none|This is the ISO 8601 date-time string of when the squad was last updated.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|versionName|string \| null|false|none|Optional human-readable label for this version. Set when the version is published.|
|versionDescription|string \| null|false|none|Optional description for this version. Set when the version is published.|
|id|string(uuid)|true|none|This is the unique identifier for the version row.|
|orgId|string(uuid)|true|none|This is the unique identifier for the org that owns this version.|
|squadId|string(uuid)|true|none|This is the unique identifier for the squad this version was snapshotted from.|
|version|string|true|none|This is the public monotonic version label, e.g. "v1".<br>System-owned and incremented per squad; never user-supplied.|
|configHash|string|true|none|This is the SHA-256 hex of the snapshotted content used for no-op detection.|
|parentVersion|string \| null|false|none|This is the prior version label (vN-1). Null on v1 or for branch roots.|
|restoredFromVersion|string \| null|false|none|The version this version was restored from. Null when it was not restored.|
|createdBy|string \| null|false|none|This is the actor that wrote this version. Email when created via JWT; null<br>when created via API key, and null for a baseline version authored by nobody.|
|deletedAt|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|This is the soft-delete timestamp. Null when active.|
|createdAt|string(date-time)|true|none|This is the ISO 8601 date-time string of when the version was created.|
|name|string|false|none|This is the name of the squad.|
|members|[[SquadMemberDTO](#schemasquadmemberdto)]|true|none|This is the list of assistants that make up the squad.<br><br>The call will start with the first assistant in the list.|
|membersOverrides|object|false|none|This can be used to override all the assistants' settings and provide values for their template variables.<br><br>Both `membersOverrides` and `members[n].assistantOverrides` can be used together. First, `members[n].assistantOverrides` is applied. Then, `membersOverrides` is applied as a global override.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|false|none|This is the name of the squad.|
|members|[[SquadMemberDTO](#schemasquadmemberdto)]|true|none|This is the list of assistants that make up the squad.<br><br>The call will start with the first assistant in the list.|
|membersOverrides|object|false|none|This can be used to override all the assistants' settings and provide values for their template variables.<br><br>Both `membersOverrides` and `members[n].assistantOverrides` can be used together. First, `members[n].assistantOverrides` is applied. Then, `membersOverrides` is applied as a global override.|

|voicemailDetection|string \| [GoogleVoicemailDetectionPlan](#schemagooglevoicemaildetectionplan) \| [OpenAIVoicemailDetectionPlan](#schemaopenaivoicemaildetectionplan) \| [TwilioVoicemailDetectionPlan](#schematwiliovoicemaildetectionplan) \| [VapiVoicemailDetectionPlan](#schemavapivoicemaildetectionplan)|false|none|This is the voicemail detection plan for the workflow.|
|maxDurationSeconds|number|false|none|This is the maximum duration of the call in seconds.<br><br>After this duration, the call will automatically end.<br><br>Default is 1800 (30 minutes), max is 43200 (12 hours), and min is 10 seconds.|
|id|string|true|none|none|
|orgId|string|true|none|none|
|createdAt|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|updatedAt|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|name|string|true|none|none|
|edges|[[Edge](#schemaedge)]|true|none|none|
|globalPrompt|string|false|none|none|
|server|object|false|none|This is where Vapi will send webhooks. You can find all webhooks available along with their shape in ServerMessage schema.<br><br>The order of precedence is:<br><br>1. tool.server<br>2. workflow.server / assistant.server<br>3. phoneNumber.server<br>4. org.server|
|compliancePlan|object|false|none|This is the compliance plan for the workflow. It allows you to configure HIPAA and other compliance settings.|
|analysisPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan for analysis of workflow's calls. Stored in `call.analysis`.|
|artifactPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan for artifacts generated during workflow's calls. Stored in `call.artifact`.|
|startSpeakingPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan for when the workflow nodes should start talking.<br><br>You should configure this if you're running into these issues:<br>- The assistant is too slow to start talking after the customer is done speaking.<br>- The assistant is too fast to start talking after the customer is done speaking.<br>- The assistant is so fast that it's actually interrupting the customer.|
|stopSpeakingPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan for when workflow nodes should stop talking on customer interruption.<br><br>You should configure this if you're running into these issues:<br>- The assistant is too slow to recognize customer's interruption.<br>- The assistant is too fast to recognize customer's interruption.<br>- The assistant is getting interrupted by phrases that are just acknowledgments.<br>- The assistant is getting interrupted by background noises.<br>- The assistant is not properly stopping -- it starts talking right after getting interrupted.|
|monitorPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan for real-time monitoring of the workflow's calls.<br><br>Usage:<br>- To enable live listening of the workflow's calls, set `monitorPlan.listenEnabled` to `true`.<br>- To enable live control of the workflow's calls, set `monitorPlan.controlEnabled` to `true`.|
|backgroundSpeechDenoisingPlan|object|false|none|This enables filtering of noise and background speech while the user is talking.<br><br>Features:<br>- Smart denoising using Krisp<br>- Fourier denoising<br><br>Both can be used together. Order of precedence:<br>- Smart denoising<br>- Fourier denoising|
|credentialIds|[string]|false|none|These are the credentials that will be used for the workflow calls. By default, all the credentials are available for use in the call but you can provide a subset using this.|
|keypadInputPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan for keypad input handling during workflow calls.|
|voicemailMessage|string|false|none|This is the message that the assistant will say if the call is forwarded to voicemail.<br><br>If unspecified, it will hang up.|

|name|string|true|none|none|
|edges|[[Edge](#schemaedge)]|true|none|none|
|globalPrompt|string|false|none|none|
|server|object|false|none|This is where Vapi will send webhooks. You can find all webhooks available along with their shape in ServerMessage schema.<br><br>The order of precedence is:<br><br>1. tool.server<br>2. workflow.server / assistant.server<br>3. phoneNumber.server<br>4. org.server|
|compliancePlan|object|false|none|This is the compliance plan for the workflow. It allows you to configure HIPAA and other compliance settings.|
|analysisPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan for analysis of workflow's calls. Stored in `call.analysis`.|
|artifactPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan for artifacts generated during workflow's calls. Stored in `call.artifact`.|
|startSpeakingPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan for when the workflow nodes should start talking.<br><br>You should configure this if you're running into these issues:<br>- The assistant is too slow to start talking after the customer is done speaking.<br>- The assistant is too fast to start talking after the customer is done speaking.<br>- The assistant is so fast that it's actually interrupting the customer.|
|stopSpeakingPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan for when workflow nodes should stop talking on customer interruption.<br><br>You should configure this if you're running into these issues:<br>- The assistant is too slow to recognize customer's interruption.<br>- The assistant is too fast to recognize customer's interruption.<br>- The assistant is getting interrupted by phrases that are just acknowledgments.<br>- The assistant is getting interrupted by background noises.<br>- The assistant is not properly stopping -- it starts talking right after getting interrupted.|
|monitorPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan for real-time monitoring of the workflow's calls.<br><br>Usage:<br>- To enable live listening of the workflow's calls, set `monitorPlan.listenEnabled` to `true`.<br>- To enable live control of the workflow's calls, set `monitorPlan.controlEnabled` to `true`.|
|backgroundSpeechDenoisingPlan|object|false|none|This enables filtering of noise and background speech while the user is talking.<br><br>Features:<br>- Smart denoising using Krisp<br>- Fourier denoising<br><br>Both can be used together. Order of precedence:<br>- Smart denoising<br>- Fourier denoising|
|credentialIds|[string]|false|none|These are the credentials that will be used for the workflow calls. By default, all the credentials are available for use in the call but you can provide a subset using this.|
|keypadInputPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan for keypad input handling during workflow calls.|
|voicemailMessage|string|false|none|This is the message that the assistant will say if the call is forwarded to voicemail.<br><br>If unspecified, it will hang up.|

<h2 id="tocS_TranscriptWordConfidence">TranscriptWordConfidence</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematranscriptwordconfidence"></a>
<a id="schema_TranscriptWordConfidence"></a>
<a id="tocStranscriptwordconfidence"></a>
<a id="tocstranscriptwordconfidence"></a>

```json
{
  "word": "string",
  "start": 0,
  "end": 0,
  "confidence": 0,
  "punctuated_word": "string",
  "language": "string",
  "speaker": 0
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|word|string|true|none|The word as the transcriber recognised it.|
|start|number|true|none|Offset at which the word begins, measured from the start of the<br>transcriber stream (ElevenLabs, which transcribes each utterance as its<br>own request, measures from the start of that utterance's audio). The unit<br>is transcriber-specific today: seconds for Deepgram, Soniox, Gladia and<br>ElevenLabs realtime (`scribe_v2_realtime`); milliseconds for AssemblyAI,<br>ElevenLabs HTTP Scribe and Google. Transcribers without per-word timing<br>emit a placeholder, typically `0`.|
|end|number|true|none|Offset at which the word ends, with the same origin and unit as `start`.|
|confidence|number|true|none|The transcriber's confidence for this word, in [0, 1]. Transcribers that<br>report no per-word score, or whose stream does not map one (Cartesia,<br>ElevenLabs HTTP Scribe, Google, Talkscriber and custom transcribers), emit<br>`1` for every word; that placeholder is not a measurement. ElevenLabs<br>realtime passes through its token log-probability, which is not a [0, 1]<br>confidence.|
|punctuated_word|string|false|none|The word with punctuation and casing applied, when the transcriber<br>reports a punctuated form. The snake_case name deliberately mirrors the<br>transcriber wire spelling already stored on every existing message;<br>renaming it would break stored data.|
|language|string|false|none|The language the transcriber detected for this word, when it reports one.|
|speaker|number|false|none|The diarized speaker index this word was attributed to, when the<br>transcriber reports one.|

After consecutive<br>transcript fragments are merged into one message the list covers the whole<br>merged message, or is absent when any fragment lacked word scores.|

<!-- backwards compatibility -->
