### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|fallbackDestination|[TransferDestinationNumber](#schematransferdestinationnumber) \| [TransferDestinationSip](#schematransferdestinationsip)|false|none|This is the fallback destination an inbound call will be transferred to if:<br>1. `assistantId` is not set<br>2. `squadId` is not set<br>3. and, `assistant-request` message to the `serverUrl` fails<br><br>If this is not set and above conditions are met, the inbound call is hung up with an error message.|
|hooks|[[PhoneNumberHookCallRinging](#schemaphonenumberhookcallringing) \| [PhoneNumberHookCallEnding](#schemaphonenumberhookcallending)]|false|none|This is the hooks that will be used for incoming calls to this phone number.|
|provider|string|true|none|This is to bring your own phone numbers from your own SIP trunks or Carriers.|
|numberE164CheckEnabled|boolean|false|none|This is the flag to toggle the E164 check for the `number` field. This is an advanced property which should be used if you know your use case requires it.<br><br>Use cases:<br>- `false`: To allow non-E164 numbers like `+001234567890`, `1234`, or `abc`. This is useful for dialing out to non-E164 numbers on your SIP trunks.<br>- `true` (default): To allow only E164 numbers like `+14155551234`. This is standard for PSTN calls.<br><br>If `false`, the `number` is still required to only contain alphanumeric characters (regex: `/^\+?[a-zA-Z0-9]+$/`).<br><br>@default true (E164 check is enabled)|
|id|string|true|none|This is the unique identifier for the phone number.|
|orgId|string|true|none|This is the unique identifier for the org that this phone number belongs to.|
|createdAt|string(date-time)|true|none|This is the ISO 8601 date-time string of when the phone number was created.|
|updatedAt|string(date-time)|true|none|This is the ISO 8601 date-time string of when the phone number was last updated.|
|status|string|false|none|This is the status of the phone number.|
|name|string|false|none|This is the name of the phone number. This is just for your own reference.|
|assistantId|string|false|none|This is the assistant that will be used for incoming calls to this phone number.<br><br>If neither `assistantId`, `squadId` nor `workflowId` is set, `assistant-request` will be sent to your Server URL. Check `ServerMessage` and `ServerMessageResponse` for the shape of the message and response that is expected.|
|workflowId|string|false|none|This is the workflow that will be used for incoming calls to this phone number.<br><br>If neither `assistantId`, `squadId`, nor `workflowId` is set, `assistant-request` will be sent to your Server URL. Check `ServerMessage` and `ServerMessageResponse` for the shape of the message and response that is expected.|
|squadId|string|false|none|This is the squad that will be used for incoming calls to this phone number.<br><br>If neither `assistantId`, `squadId`, nor `workflowId` is set, `assistant-request` will be sent to your Server URL. Check `ServerMessage` and `ServerMessageResponse` for the shape of the message and response that is expected.|
|server|object|false|none|This is where Vapi will send webhooks. You can find all webhooks available along with their shape in ServerMessage schema.<br><br>The order of precedence is:<br><br>1. assistant.server<br>2. phoneNumber.server<br>3. org.server|
|number|string|false|none|This is the number of the customer.|
|credentialId|string|true|none|This is the credential of your own SIP trunk or Carrier (type `byo-sip-trunk`) which can be used to make calls to this phone number.<br><br>You can add the SIP trunk or Carrier credential in the Provider Credentials page on the Dashboard to get the credentialId.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|provider|byo-phone-number|
|status|active|
|status|activating|
|status|blocked|

|number|string|false|none|These are the digits of the phone number you own on your Telnyx.|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

Multiple request-start messages are variants. For request-response-delayed, same timing means variants and different timings mean staged updates.|
|type|string|true|none|The type of tool. "apiRequest" for API request tool.|
|name|string|false|none|This is the name of the tool. This will be passed to the model.<br><br>Must be a-z, A-Z, 0-9, or contain underscores and dashes, with a maximum length of 40.|
|method|string|true|none|none|
|timeoutSeconds|number|false|none|This is the timeout in seconds for the request. Defaults to 20 seconds.<br><br>@default 20|
|credentialId|string|false|none|The credential ID for API request authentication|
|encryptedPaths|[string]|false|none|This is the paths to encrypt in the request body if credentialId and encryptionPlan are defined.|
|parameters|[[ToolParameter](#schematoolparameter)]|false|none|Static key-value pairs merged into the request body. Values support Liquid templates.|
|id|string|true|none|This is the unique identifier for the tool.|
|orgId|string|true|none|This is the unique identifier for the organization that this tool belongs to.|
|createdAt|string(date-time)|true|none|This is the ISO 8601 date-time string of when the tool was created.|
|updatedAt|string(date-time)|true|none|This is the ISO 8601 date-time string of when the tool was last updated.|
|rejectionPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan to reject a tool call based on the conversation state.<br><br>// Example 1: Reject endCall if user didn't say goodbye<br>```json<br>{<br>  conditions: [{<br>    type: 'regex',<br>    regex: '(?i)\\b(bye\|goodbye\|farewell\|see you later\|take care)\\b',<br>    target: { position: -1, role: 'user' },<br>    negate: true  // Reject if pattern does NOT match<br>  }]<br>}<br>```<br><br>// Example 2: Reject transfer if user is actually asking a question<br>```json<br>{<br>  conditions: [{<br>    type: 'regex',<br>    regex: '\\?',<br>    target: { position: -1, role: 'user' }<br>  }]<br>}<br>```<br><br>// Example 3: Reject transfer if user didn't mention transfer recently<br>```json<br>{<br>  conditions: [{<br>    type: 'liquid',<br>    liquid: `{% assign recentMessages = messages \| last: 5 %}<br>{% assign userMessages = recentMessages \| where: 'role', 'user' %}<br>{% assign mentioned = false %}<br>{% for msg in userMessages %}<br>  {% if msg.content contains 'transfer' or msg.content contains 'connect' or msg.content contains 'speak to' %}<br>    {% assign mentioned = true %}<br>    {% break %}<br>  {% endif %}<br>{% endfor %}<br>{% if mentioned %}<br>  false<br>{% else %}<br>  true<br>{% endif %}`<br>  }]<br>}<br>```<br><br>// Example 4: Reject endCall if the bot is looping and trying to exit<br>```json<br>{<br>  conditions: [{<br>    type: 'liquid',<br>    liquid: `{% assign recentMessages = messages \| last: 6 %}<br>{% assign userMessages = recentMessages \| where: 'role', 'user' \| reverse %}<br>{% if userMessages.size < 3 %}<br>  false<br>{% else %}<br>  {% assign msg1 = userMessages[0].content \| downcase %}<br>  {% assign msg2 = userMessages[1].content \| downcase %}<br>  {% assign msg3 = userMessages[2].content \| downcase %}<br>  {% comment %} Check for repetitive messages {% endcomment %}<br>  {% if msg1 == msg2 or msg1 == msg3 or msg2 == msg3 %}<br>    true<br>  {% comment %} Check for common loop phrases {% endcomment %}<br>  {% elsif msg1 contains 'cool thanks' or msg2 contains 'cool thanks' or msg3 contains 'cool thanks' %}<br>    true<br>  {% elsif msg1 contains 'okay thanks' or msg2 contains 'okay thanks' or msg3 contains 'okay thanks' %}<br>    true<br>  {% elsif msg1 contains 'got it' or msg2 contains 'got it' or msg3 contains 'got it' %}<br>    true<br>  {% else %}<br>    false<br>  {% endif %}<br>{% endif %}`<br>  }]<br>}<br>```|
|description|string|false|none|This is the description of the tool. This will be passed to the model.|
|url|string|true|none|This is where the request will be sent.|
|body|object|false|none|This is the body of the request.|
|headers|object|false|none|These are the headers to send with the request.|
|backoffPlan|object|false|none|This is the backoff plan if the request fails. Defaults to undefined (the request will not be retried).<br><br>@default undefined (the request will not be retried)|
|variableExtractionPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan to extract variables from the tool's response. These will be accessible during the call and stored in `call.artifact.variableValues` after the call.<br><br>Usage:<br>1. Use `aliases` to extract variables from the tool's response body. (Most common case)<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "aliases": [<br>    {<br>      "key": "customerName",<br>      "value": "{{customer.name}}"<br>    },<br>    {<br>      "key": "customerAge",<br>      "value": "{{customer.age}}"<br>    }<br>  ]<br>}<br>```<br><br>The tool response body is made available to the liquid template.<br><br>2. Use `aliases` to extract variables from the tool's response body if the response is an array.<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "aliases": [<br>    {<br>      "key": "customerName",<br>      "value": "{{$[0].name}}"<br>    },<br>    {<br>      "key": "customerAge",<br>      "value": "{{$[0].age}}"<br>    }<br>  ]<br>}<br>```<br><br>$ is a shorthand for the tool's response body. `$[0]` is the first item in the array. `$[n]` is the nth item in the array. Note, $ is available regardless of the response body type (both object and array).<br><br>3. Use `aliases` to extract variables from the tool's response headers.<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "aliases": [<br>    {<br>      "key": "customerName",<br>      "value": "{{tool.response.headers.customer-name}}"<br>    },<br>    {<br>      "key": "customerAge",<br>      "value": "{{tool.response.headers.customer-age}}"<br>    }<br>  ]<br>}<br>```<br><br>`tool.response` is made available to the liquid template. Particularly, both `tool.response.headers` and `tool.response.body` are available. Note, `tool.response` is available regardless of the response body type (both object and array).<br><br>4. Use `schema` to extract a large portion of the tool's response body.<br><br>4.1. If you hit example.com and it returns `{"name": "John", "age": 30}`, then you can specify the schema as:<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "schema": {<br>    "type": "object",<br>    "properties": {<br>      "name": {<br>        "type": "string"<br>      },<br>      "age": {<br>        "type": "number"<br>      }<br>    }<br>  }<br>}<br>```<br>These will be extracted as `{{ name }}` and `{{ age }}` respectively. To emphasize, object properties are extracted as direct global variables.<br><br>4.2. If you hit example.com and it returns `{"name": {"first": "John", "last": "Doe"}}`, then you can specify the schema as:<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "schema": {<br>    "type": "object",<br>    "properties": {<br>      "name": {<br>        "type": "object",<br>        "properties": {<br>          "first": {<br>            "type": "string"<br>          },<br>          "last": {<br>            "type": "string"<br>          }<br>        }<br>      }<br>    }<br>  }<br>}<br>```<br><br>These will be extracted as `{{ name }}`. And, `{{ name.first }}` and `{{ name.last }}` will be accessible.<br><br>4.3. If you hit example.com and it returns `["94123", "94124"]`, then you can specify the schema as:<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "schema": {<br>    "type": "array",<br>    "title": "zipCodes",<br>    "items": {<br>      "type": "string"<br>    }<br>  }<br>}<br>```<br><br>This will be extracted as `{{ zipCodes }}`. To access the array items, you can use `{{ zipCodes[0] }}` and `{{ zipCodes[1] }}`.<br><br>4.4. If you hit example.com and it returns `[{"name": "John", "age": 30, "zipCodes": ["94123", "94124"]}, {"name": "Jane", "age": 25, "zipCodes": ["94125", "94126"]}]`, then you can specify the schema as:<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "schema": {<br>    "type": "array",<br>    "title": "people",<br>    "items": {<br>      "type": "object",<br>      "properties": {<br>        "name": {<br>          "type": "string"<br>        },<br>        "age": {<br>          "type": "number"<br>        },<br>        "zipCodes": {<br>          "type": "array",<br>          "items": {<br>            "type": "string"<br>          }<br>        }<br>      }<br>    }<br>  }<br>}<br>```<br><br>This will be extracted as `{{ people }}`. To access the array items, you can use `{{ people[n].name }}`, `{{ people[n].age }}`, `{{ people[n].zipCodes }}`, `{{ people[n].zipCodes[0] }}` and `{{ people[n].zipCodes[1] }}`.<br><br>Note: Both `aliases` and `schema` can be used together.|

|latestVersion|string \| null|false|none|none|

Multiple request-start messages are variants. For request-response-delayed, same timing means variants and different timings mean staged updates.|
|type|string|true|none|The type of tool. "code" for Code tool.|
|async|boolean|false|none|This determines if the tool is async.<br><br>  If async, the assistant will move forward without waiting for your server to respond. This is useful if you just want to trigger something on your server.<br><br>  If sync, the assistant will wait for your server to respond. This is useful if want assistant to respond with the result from your server.<br><br>  Defaults to synchronous (`false`).|
|server|object|false|none|<br>  This is the server where a `tool-calls` webhook will be sent.<br><br>  Notes:<br>  - Webhook is sent to this server when a tool call is made.<br>  - Webhook contains the call, assistant, and phone number objects.<br>  - Webhook contains the variables set on the assistant.<br>  - Webhook is sent to the first available URL in this order: {{tool.server.url}}, {{assistant.server.url}}, {{phoneNumber.server.url}}, {{org.server.url}}.<br>  - Webhook expects a response with tool call result.|
|code|string|true|none|TypeScript code to execute when the tool is called|
|environmentVariables|[[CodeToolEnvironmentVariable](#schemacodetoolenvironmentvariable)]|false|none|Environment variables available in code via `env` object|
|timeoutSeconds|number|false|none|This is the timeout in seconds for the code execution. Defaults to 10 seconds.<br>Maximum is 30 seconds to prevent abuse.<br><br>@default 10|
|credentialId|string|false|none|Credential ID containing the Val Town API key|
|variableExtractionPlan|object|false|none|Plan to extract variables from the tool response|
|id|string|true|none|This is the unique identifier for the tool.|
|orgId|string|true|none|This is the unique identifier for the organization that this tool belongs to.|
|createdAt|string(date-time)|true|none|This is the ISO 8601 date-time string of when the tool was created.|
|updatedAt|string(date-time)|true|none|This is the ISO 8601 date-time string of when the tool was last updated.|
|rejectionPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan to reject a tool call based on the conversation state.<br><br>// Example 1: Reject endCall if user didn't say goodbye<br>```json<br>{<br>  conditions: [{<br>    type: 'regex',<br>    regex: '(?i)\\b(bye\|goodbye\|farewell\|see you later\|take care)\\b',<br>    target: { position: -1, role: 'user' },<br>    negate: true  // Reject if pattern does NOT match<br>  }]<br>}<br>```<br><br>// Example 2: Reject transfer if user is actually asking a question<br>```json<br>{<br>  conditions: [{<br>    type: 'regex',<br>    regex: '\\?',<br>    target: { position: -1, role: 'user' }<br>  }]<br>}<br>```<br><br>// Example 3: Reject transfer if user didn't mention transfer recently<br>```json<br>{<br>  conditions: [{<br>    type: 'liquid',<br>    liquid: `{% assign recentMessages = messages \| last: 5 %}<br>{% assign userMessages = recentMessages \| where: 'role', 'user' %}<br>{% assign mentioned = false %}<br>{% for msg in userMessages %}<br>  {% if msg.content contains 'transfer' or msg.content contains 'connect' or msg.content contains 'speak to' %}<br>    {% assign mentioned = true %}<br>    {% break %}<br>  {% endif %}<br>{% endfor %}<br>{% if mentioned %}<br>  false<br>{% else %}<br>  true<br>{% endif %}`<br>  }]<br>}<br>```<br><br>// Example 4: Reject endCall if the bot is looping and trying to exit<br>```json<br>{<br>  conditions: [{<br>    type: 'liquid',<br>    liquid: `{% assign recentMessages = messages \| last: 6 %}<br>{% assign userMessages = recentMessages \| where: 'role', 'user' \| reverse %}<br>{% if userMessages.size < 3 %}<br>  false<br>{% else %}<br>  {% assign msg1 = userMessages[0].content \| downcase %}<br>  {% assign msg2 = userMessages[1].content \| downcase %}<br>  {% assign msg3 = userMessages[2].content \| downcase %}<br>  {% comment %} Check for repetitive messages {% endcomment %}<br>  {% if msg1 == msg2 or msg1 == msg3 or msg2 == msg3 %}<br>    true<br>  {% comment %} Check for common loop phrases {% endcomment %}<br>  {% elsif msg1 contains 'cool thanks' or msg2 contains 'cool thanks' or msg3 contains 'cool thanks' %}<br>    true<br>  {% elsif msg1 contains 'okay thanks' or msg2 contains 'okay thanks' or msg3 contains 'okay thanks' %}<br>    true<br>  {% elsif msg1 contains 'got it' or msg2 contains 'got it' or msg3 contains 'got it' %}<br>    true<br>  {% else %}<br>    false<br>  {% endif %}<br>{% endif %}`<br>  }]<br>}<br>```|
|function|object|false|none|This is the function definition of the tool.<br><br>For the Code tool, this defines the name, description, and parameters that the model<br>will use to understand when and how to call this tool.|

|headers|object|false|none|These are the headers to send with the request.|
|backoffPlan|object|false|none|This is the backoff plan if the request fails. Defaults to undefined (the request will not be retried).<br><br>@default undefined (the request will not be retried)|
|variableExtractionPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan to extract variables from the tool's response. These will be accessible during the call and stored in `call.artifact.variableValues` after the call.<br><br>Usage:<br>1. Use `aliases` to extract variables from the tool's response body. (Most common case)<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "aliases": [<br>    {<br>      "key": "customerName",<br>      "value": "{{customer.name}}"<br>    },<br>    {<br>      "key": "customerAge",<br>      "value": "{{customer.age}}"<br>    }<br>  ]<br>}<br>```<br><br>The tool response body is made available to the liquid template.<br><br>2. Use `aliases` to extract variables from the tool's response body if the response is an array.<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "aliases": [<br>    {<br>      "key": "customerName",<br>      "value": "{{$[0].name}}"<br>    },<br>    {<br>      "key": "customerAge",<br>      "value": "{{$[0].age}}"<br>    }<br>  ]<br>}<br>```<br><br>$ is a shorthand for the tool's response body. `$[0]` is the first item in the array. `$[n]` is the nth item in the array. Note, $ is available regardless of the response body type (both object and array).<br><br>3. Use `aliases` to extract variables from the tool's response headers.<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "aliases": [<br>    {<br>      "key": "customerName",<br>      "value": "{{tool.response.headers.customer-name}}"<br>    },<br>    {<br>      "key": "customerAge",<br>      "value": "{{tool.response.headers.customer-age}}"<br>    }<br>  ]<br>}<br>```<br><br>`tool.response` is made available to the liquid template. Particularly, both `tool.response.headers` and `tool.response.body` are available. Note, `tool.response` is available regardless of the response body type (both object and array).<br><br>4. Use `schema` to extract a large portion of the tool's response body.<br><br>4.1. If you hit example.com and it returns `{"name": "John", "age": 30}`, then you can specify the schema as:<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "schema": {<br>    "type": "object",<br>    "properties": {<br>      "name": {<br>        "type": "string"<br>      },<br>      "age": {<br>        "type": "number"<br>      }<br>    }<br>  }<br>}<br>```<br>These will be extracted as `{{ name }}` and `{{ age }}` respectively. To emphasize, object properties are extracted as direct global variables.<br><br>4.2. If you hit example.com and it returns `{"name": {"first": "John", "last": "Doe"}}`, then you can specify the schema as:<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "schema": {<br>    "type": "object",<br>    "properties": {<br>      "name": {<br>        "type": "object",<br>        "properties": {<br>          "first": {<br>            "type": "string"<br>          },<br>          "last": {<br>            "type": "string"<br>          }<br>        }<br>      }<br>    }<br>  }<br>}<br>```<br><br>These will be extracted as `{{ name }}`. And, `{{ name.first }}` and `{{ name.last }}` will be accessible.<br><br>4.3. If you hit example.com and it returns `["94123", "94124"]`, then you can specify the schema as:<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "schema": {<br>    "type": "array",<br>    "title": "zipCodes",<br>    "items": {<br>      "type": "string"<br>    }<br>  }<br>}<br>```<br><br>This will be extracted as `{{ zipCodes }}`. To access the array items, you can use `{{ zipCodes[0] }}` and `{{ zipCodes[1] }}`.<br><br>4.4. If you hit example.com and it returns `[{"name": "John", "age": 30, "zipCodes": ["94123", "94124"]}, {"name": "Jane", "age": 25, "zipCodes": ["94125", "94126"]}]`, then you can specify the schema as:<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "schema": {<br>    "type": "array",<br>    "title": "people",<br>    "items": {<br>      "type": "object",<br>      "properties": {<br>        "name": {<br>          "type": "string"<br>        },<br>        "age": {<br>          "type": "number"<br>        },<br>        "zipCodes": {<br>          "type": "array",<br>          "items": {<br>            "type": "string"<br>          }<br>        }<br>      }<br>    }<br>  }<br>}<br>```<br><br>This will be extracted as `{{ people }}`. To access the array items, you can use `{{ people[n].name }}`, `{{ people[n].age }}`, `{{ people[n].zipCodes }}`, `{{ people[n].zipCodes[0] }}` and `{{ people[n].zipCodes[1] }}`.<br><br>Note: Both `aliases` and `schema` can be used together.|
|rejectionPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan to reject a tool call based on the conversation state.<br><br>// Example 1: Reject endCall if user didn't say goodbye<br>```json<br>{<br>  conditions: [{<br>    type: 'regex',<br>    regex: '(?i)\\b(bye\|goodbye\|farewell\|see you later\|take care)\\b',<br>    target: { position: -1, role: 'user' },<br>    negate: true  // Reject if pattern does NOT match<br>  }]<br>}<br>```<br><br>// Example 2: Reject transfer if user is actually asking a question<br>```json<br>{<br>  conditions: [{<br>    type: 'regex',<br>    regex: '\\?',<br>    target: { position: -1, role: 'user' }<br>  }]<br>}<br>```<br><br>// Example 3: Reject transfer if user didn't mention transfer recently<br>```json<br>{<br>  conditions: [{<br>    type: 'liquid',<br>    liquid: `{% assign recentMessages = messages \| last: 5 %}<br>{% assign userMessages = recentMessages \| where: 'role', 'user' %}<br>{% assign mentioned = false %}<br>{% for msg in userMessages %}<br>  {% if msg.content contains 'transfer' or msg.content contains 'connect' or msg.content contains 'speak to' %}<br>    {% assign mentioned = true %}<br>    {% break %}<br>  {% endif %}<br>{% endfor %}<br>{% if mentioned %}<br>  false<br>{% else %}<br>  true<br>{% endif %}`<br>  }]<br>}<br>```<br><br>// Example 4: Reject endCall if the bot is looping and trying to exit<br>```json<br>{<br>  conditions: [{<br>    type: 'liquid',<br>    liquid: `{% assign recentMessages = messages \| last: 6 %}<br>{% assign userMessages = recentMessages \| where: 'role', 'user' \| reverse %}<br>{% if userMessages.size < 3 %}<br>  false<br>{% else %}<br>  {% assign msg1 = userMessages[0].content \| downcase %}<br>  {% assign msg2 = userMessages[1].content \| downcase %}<br>  {% assign msg3 = userMessages[2].content \| downcase %}<br>  {% comment %} Check for repetitive messages {% endcomment %}<br>  {% if msg1 == msg2 or msg1 == msg3 or msg2 == msg3 %}<br>    true<br>  {% comment %} Check for common loop phrases {% endcomment %}<br>  {% elsif msg1 contains 'cool thanks' or msg2 contains 'cool thanks' or msg3 contains 'cool thanks' %}<br>    true<br>  {% elsif msg1 contains 'okay thanks' or msg2 contains 'okay thanks' or msg3 contains 'okay thanks' %}<br>    true<br>  {% elsif msg1 contains 'got it' or msg2 contains 'got it' or msg3 contains 'got it' %}<br>    true<br>  {% else %}<br>    false<br>  {% endif |variableExtractionPlan|object|false|none|This is the plan to extract variables from the tool's response. These will be accessible during the call and stored in `call.artifact.variableValues` after the call.<br><br>Usage:<br>1. Use `aliases` to extract variables from the tool's response body. (Most common case)<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "aliases": [<br>    {<br>      "key": "customerName",<br>      "value": "{{customer.name}}"<br>    },<br>    {<br>      "key": "customerAge",<br>      "value": "{{customer.age}}"<br>    }<br>  ]<br>}<br>```<br><br>The tool response body is made available to the liquid template.<br><br>2. Use `aliases` to extract variables from the tool's response body if the response is an array.<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "aliases": [<br>    {<br>      "key": "customerName",<br>      "value": "{{$[0].name}}"<br>    },<br>    {<br>      "key": "customerAge",<br>      "value": "{{$[0].age}}"<br>    }<br>  ]<br>}<br>```<br><br>$ is a shorthand for the tool's response body. `$[0]` is the first item in the array. `$[n]` is the nth item in the array. Note, $ is available regardless of the response body type (both object and array).<br><br>3. Use `aliases` to extract variables from the tool's response headers.<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "aliases": [<br>    {<br>      "key": "customerName",<br>      "value": "{{tool.response.headers.customer-name}}"<br>    },<br>    {<br>      "key": "customerAge",<br>      "value": "{{tool.response.headers.customer-age}}"<br>    }<br>  ]<br>}<br>```<br><br>`tool.response` is made available to the liquid template. Particularly, both `tool.response.headers` and `tool.response.body` are available. Note, `tool.response` is available regardless of the response body type (both object and array).<br><br>4. Use `schema` to extract a large portion of the tool's response body.<br><br>4.1. If you hit example.com and it returns `{"name": "John", "age": 30}`, then you can specify the schema as:<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "schema": {<br>    "type": "object",<br>    "properties": {<br>      "name": {<br>        "type": "string"<br>      },<br>      "age": {<br>        "type": "number"<br>      }<br>    }<br>  }<br>}<br>```<br>These will be extracted as `{{ name }}` and `{{ age }}` respectively. To emphasize, object properties are extracted as direct global variables.<br><br>4.2. If you hit example.com and it returns `{"name": {"first": "John", "last": "Doe"}}`, then you can specify the schema as:<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "schema": {<br>    "type": "object",<br>    "properties": {<br>      "name": {<br>        "type": "object",<br>        "properties": {<br>          "first": {<br>            "type": "string"<br>          },<br>          "last": {<br>            "type": "string"<br>          }<br>        }<br>      }<br>    }<br>  }<br>}<br>```<br><br>These will be extracted as `{{ name }}`. And, `{{ name.first }}` and `{{ name.last }}` will be accessible.<br><br>4.3. If you hit example.com and it returns `["94123", "94124"]`, then you can specify the schema as:<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "schema": {<br>    "type": "array",<br>    "title": "zipCodes",<br>    "items": {<br>      "type": "string"<br>    }<br>  }<br>}<br>```<br><br>This will be extracted as `{{ zipCodes }}`. To access the array items, you can use `{{ zipCodes[0] }}` and `{{ zipCodes[1] }}`.<br><br>4.4. If you hit example.com and it returns `[{"name": "John", "age": 30, "zipCodes": ["94123", "94124"]}, {"name": "Jane", "age": 25, "zipCodes": ["94125", "94126"]}]`, then you can specify the schema as:<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  "schema": {<br>    "type": "array",<br>    "title": "people",<br>    "items": {<br>      "type": "object",<br>      "properties": {<br>        "name": {<br>          "type": "string"<br>        },<br>        "age": {<br>          "type": "number"<br>        },<br>        "zipCodes": {<br>          "type": "array",<br>          "items": {<br>            "type": "string"<br>          }<br>        }<br>      }<br>    }<br>  }<br>}<br>```<br><br>This will be extracted as `{{ people }}`. To access the array items, you can use `{{ people[n].name }}`, `{{ people[n].age }}`, `{{ people[n].zipCodes }}`, `{{ people[n].zipCodes[0] }}` and `{{ people[n].zipCodes[1] }}`.<br><br>Note: Both `aliases` and `schema` can be used together.|

<h2 id="tocS_StructuredOutput">StructuredOutput</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemastructuredoutput"></a>
<a id="schema_StructuredOutput"></a>

<a id="tocsstructuredoutput"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "ai",
  "regex": "string",
  "model": {
    "messages": [
      {
        "content": "string",
        "role": "assistant"
      }
    ],
    "provider": "openai",
    "model": "gpt-6-luna",
    "reasoningEffort": "minimal",
    "temperature": 0,
    "maxTokens": 50
  },
  "compliancePlan": {
    "forceStoreOnHipaaEnabled": false
  },
  "conditions": [
    {
      "type": "minMessages",
      "count": 4
    },
    {
      "type": "minCallDuration",
      "seconds": 10
    }
  ],
  "id": "string",
  "orgId": "string",
  "createdAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "updatedAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "name": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "assistantIds": [
    "string"
  ],
  "workflowIds": [
    "string"
  ],
  "schema": {
    "type": "string",
    "items": {},
    "properties": {
      "property1": {},
      "property2": {}
    },
    "description": "string",
    "pattern": "string",
    "format": "date-time",
    "required": [
      "string"
    ],
    "enum": [
      "string"
    ],
    "title": "string"
  }
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|false|none|This is the type of structured output.<br><br>- 'ai': Uses an LLM to extract structured data from the conversation (default).<br>- 'regex': Uses a regex pattern to extract data from the transcript without an LLM.|
|regex|string|false|none|This is the regex pattern to match against the transcript.<br><br>Simulation evaluations use a canonical transcript built from recorded messages:<br>User: and AI: dialogue, AI: tool_calls: JSON name/arguments records, and<br>AI: tool_call_results: JSON results. System messages are excluded. These<br>fixed labels apply even when custom artifact transcript labels are configured.<br>Tool payloads participate in first-match and all-match extraction in event order.<br>An empty message array falls back to the supplied transcript verbatim.<br>Production-call extraction and call preview use their existing transcripts,<br>so previewing the same output on a simulation's call can return a different result.<br><br>Only used when type is 'regex'. Supports both raw patterns (e.g. '\d+') and<br>regex literal format (e.g. '/\d+/gi'). Uses RE2 syntax for safety.<br><br>The result depends on the schema type:<br>- boolean: true if the pattern matches, false otherwise<br>- string: the first match or first capture group<br>- number/integer: the first match parsed as a number<br>- array: all matches|
|model|[WorkflowOpenAIModel](#schemaworkflowopenaimodel) \| [WorkflowAnthropicModel](#schemaworkflowanthropicmodel) \| [WorkflowAnthropicBedrockModel](#schemaworkflowanthropicbedrockmodel) \| [WorkflowGoogleModel](#schemaworkflowgooglemodel) \| [WorkflowCustomModel](#schemaworkflowcustommodel)|false|none|This is the model that will be used to extract the structured output.<br><br>To provide your own custom system and user prompts for structured output extraction, populate the messages array with your system and user messages. You can specify liquid templating in your system and user messages.<br>For text extraction, you must reference 'transcript', 'messages', or 'messagesWithConfidence' with the `{{}}` syntax to access the conversation history.<br>In structured outputs, `{{messages}}` includes conversation text and tool calls/results but omits caller transcription-confidence fields. Text extraction can use `{{messagesWithConfidence}}` when the output needs the original message history with transcription confidence. These variables also apply in structured-output schema descriptions. Audio-targeted (`messages-with-audio`) extraction ignores custom messages. Stored call artifacts and API messages retain their confidence data.<br>Between the system or user messages, you must reference a variation of the structured output with the `{{}}` syntax to access the structured output definition.<br>i.e.:<br>`{{structuredOutput}}`<br>`{{structuredOutput.name}}`<br>`{{structuredOutput.description}}`<br>`{{structuredOutput.schema}}`<br><br>If model is not specified, GPT-4.1 will be used by default for extraction, utilizing default system and user prompts.<br>If messages or required fields are not specified, the default system and user prompts will be used.|
|compliancePlan|object|false|none|Compliance configuration for this output. Only enable overrides if no sensitive data will be stored.|
|conditions|[[MinMessagesCondition](#schemaminmessagescondition) \| [MinCallDurationCondition](#schemamincalldurationcondition) \| [EndedReasonCondition](#schemaendedreasoncondition)]|false|none|These are the conditions that gate the execution of this structured output. Every condition must pass for the structured output to run (AND semantics). When omitted or empty, no user-defined conditions gate this output. Send null to clear a previously saved gate.|
|id|string|true|none|This is the unique identifier for the structured output.|
|orgId|string|true|none|This is the unique identifier for the org that this structured output belongs to.|
|createdAt|string(date-time)|true|none|This is the ISO 8601 date-time string of when the structured output was created.|
|updatedAt|string(date-time)|true|none|This is the ISO 8601 date-time string of when the structured output was last updated.|
|name|string|true|none|This is the name of the structured output.|
|description|string|false|none|This is the description of what the structured output extracts.<br><br>Use this to provide context about what data will be extracted and how it will be used.|
|assistantIds|[string]|false|none|These are the assistant IDs that this structured output is linked to.<br><br>When linked to assistants, this structured output will be available for extraction during those assistant's calls.|
|workflowIds|[string]|false|none|These are the workflow IDs that this structured output is linked to.<br><br>When linked to workflows, this structured output will be available for extraction during those workflow's execution.|
|schema|object|true|none|This is the JSON Schema definition for the structured output.<br><br>Defines the structure and validation rules for the data that will be extracted. Supports all JSON Schema features including:<br>- Objects and nested properties<br>- Arrays and array validation<br>- String, number, boolean, and null types<br>- Enums and const values<br>- Validation constraints (min/max, patterns, etc.)<br>- Composition with allOf, anyOf, oneOf|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|ai|
|type|regex|

If true, the re-run will be executed and the response will be returned immediately and the call artifact will NOT be updated.<br>If false (default), the re-run will be executed and the response will be updated in the call artifact.|
|structuredOutputId|string|false|none|This is the ID of the structured output that will be run. This must be provided unless a transient structured output is provided.<br>When the re-run is executed, only the value of this structured output will be replaced with the new value, or added if not present.|
|structuredOutput|object|false|none|This is the transient structured output that will be run. This must be provided if a structured output ID is not provided.<br>When the re-run is executed, the structured output value will be added to the existing artifact.|
|callIds|[string]|true|none|This is the array of callIds that will be updated with the new structured output value. If preview is true, this array must be provided and contain exactly 1 callId.<br>If preview is false, up to 100 callIds may be provided.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|assistant|object|false|none|Pass a transient assistant to use for the test assistant.<br><br>Make sure to write a detailed system prompt for a test assistant, and use the {{test.script}} variable to access the test script.|
|assistantId|string|false|none|Pass an assistant id that can be access<br><br>Make sure to write a detailed system prompt for the test assistant, and use the {{test.script}} variable to access the test script.|
|assistantOverrides|object|false|none|Add any assistant overrides to the test assistant.<br><br>One use case is if you want to pass custom variables into the test using variableValues, that you can then access in the script<br>and rubric using {{varName}}.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|phoneNumberId|string|false|none|This is the phone number that is being tested.<br>During the actual test, it'll be called and the assistant attached to it will pick up and be tested.<br>To test an assistant directly, send assistantId instead.|
|phoneNumber|object|false|none|This can be any phone number (even not on Vapi).<br>During the actual test, it'll be called.<br>To test a Vapi number, send phoneNumberId. To test an assistant directly, send assistantId instead.|
|assistantId|string|false|none|This is the assistant being tested.<br>During the actual test, it'll invoked directly.<br>To test the assistant over phone number, send phoneNumberId instead.|
|assistantOverrides|object|false|none|This is the assistant overrides applied to assistantId before it is tested.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|This is the unique identifier for the test suite.|
|orgId|string|true|none|This is the unique identifier for the org that this test suite belongs to.|
|createdAt|string(date-time)|true|none|This is the ISO 8601 date-time string of when the test suite was created.|
|updatedAt|string(date-time)|true|none|This is the ISO 8601 date-time string of when the test suite was last updated.|
|name|string|false|none|This is the name of the test suite.|
|phoneNumberId|string|false|none|**Deprecated.** This is the phone number ID associated with this test suite.|
|testerPlan|object|false|none|Override the default tester plan by providing custom assistant configuration for the test agent.<br><br>We recommend only using this if you are confident, as we have already set sensible defaults on the tester plan.|
|targetPlan|object|false|none|These are the configuration for the assistant / phone number that is being tested.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|false|none|This is the name of the test suite.|
|phoneNumberId|string|false|none|**Deprecated.** This is the phone number ID associated with this test suite.|
|testerPlan|object|false|none|Override the default tester plan by providing custom assistant configuration for the test agent.<br><br>We recommend only using this if you are confident, as we have already set sensible defaults on the tester plan.|
|targetPlan|object|false|none|These are the configuration for the assistant / phone number that is being tested.|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|true|none|This is the name of the personality (e.g., "Confused Carl", "Rude Rob").|
|assistant|object|true|none|This is the full assistant configuration for this personality.<br>It defines the tester's voice, model, behavior via system prompt, and other settings.|
|path|string \| null|false|none|Optional folder path for organizing personalities.<br>Supports up to 3 levels (e.g., "dept/feature/variant").<br>Maps to GitOps resource folder structure.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string(uuid)|true|none|This is the unique identifier for the personality.|
|orgId|string(uuid) \| null|true|none|This is the unique identifier for the organization this personality belongs to.<br>If null, this is a Vapi-provided default personality available to all organizations.|
|createdAt|string(date-time)|true|none|This is the ISO 8601 date-time string of when the personality was created.|
|updatedAt|string(date-time)|true|none|This is the ISO 8601 date-time string of when the personality was last updated.|
|name|string|true|none|This is the name of the personality (e.g., "Confused Carl", "Rude Rob").|
|assistant|object|true|none|This is the full assistant configuration for this personality.<br>It defines the tester's voice, model, behavior via system prompt, and other settings.|
|path|string \| null|false|none|Optional folder path for organizing personalities.<br>Supports up to 3 levels (e.g., "dept/feature/variant").<br>Maps to GitOps resource folder structure.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|structuredOutputId|string(uuid)|false|none|This is the ID of an existing structured output to use for evaluation.<br>Mutually exclusive with structuredOutput.|
|structuredOutput|object|false|none|This is an inline structured output definition for evaluation.<br>Mutually exclusive with structuredOutputId.<br>Only primitive schema types (string, number, integer, boolean) are allowed.|
|path|string|false|none|Optional dot-notation path to a primitive leaf when evaluating an object structured output.|
|comparator|string|true|none|This is the comparison operator to use when evaluating the extracted value against the expected value.<br>Available operators depend on the structured output's schema type:<br>- boolean: '=', '!='<br>- string: '=', '!='<br>- number/integer: '=', '!=', '>', '<', '>=', '<='|
|value|number \| string \| boolean|true|none|This is the expected value to compare against the extracted structured output result.<br>Type should match the structured output's schema type.|
|required|boolean|false|none|This is whether this evaluation must pass for the simulation to pass.<br>Defaults to true. If false, the result is informational only.|

<h2 id="tocS_LatencyExpectation">LatencyExpectation</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemalatencyexpectation"></a>
<a id="schema_LatencyExpectation"></a>
<a id="tocSlatencyexpectation"></a>
<a id="tocslatencyexpectation"></a>

```json
{
  "metric": "turn",
  "aggregation": "median",
  "thresholdMs": 1200,
  "required": true
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|metric|string|true|none|This is the latency component to measure.<br>- turn: total time from the end of user speech to the start of assistant speech<br>- model: LLM time to first token<br>- voice: TTS time to first audio|
|aggregation|string|true|none|This is how the call's per-turn latencies are aggregated before comparing.<br>p95 uses the nearest-rank method, so on calls with fewer than 20 turns it<br>equals the max.|
|thresholdMs|number|true|none|This is the ceiling in milliseconds. The expectation passes when the<br>aggregated latency is less than or equal to this value.|
|required|boolean|false|none|This is whether this expectation must pass for the simulation to pass.<br>Defaults to true. If false, the result is informational only.<br>On a voice simulation, a metric that no turn measured fails the expectation.<br>GPT Live targets are skipped, because their latency is not measured yet.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|metric|turn|
|metric|model|
|metric|voice|
|aggregation|mean|
|aggregation|median|
|aggregation|p95|
|aggregation|max|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|Type discriminator|
|simulationId|string(uuid)|false|none|ID of an existing simulation to run. When provided, scenarioId/personalityId/inline fields are ignored.|
|scenarioId|string(uuid)|false|none|ID of an existing scenario. Cannot be combined with inline scenario.|
|scenario|object|false|none|Inline scenario configuration. Cannot be combined with scenarioId.|
|personalityId|string(uuid)|false|none|ID of an existing personality. Cannot be combined with inline personality.|
|personality|object|false|none|Inline personality configuration. Cannot be combined with personalityId.|
|name|string|false|none|Optional name for this simulation entry|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|simulation|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|includeTargetStructuredOutputs|boolean|false|none|Generate directly attached target structured outputs. Default false. Enabled extraction may incur additional model charges.|
|simulations|[[SimulationRunSimulationEntry](#schemasimulationrunsimulationentry) \| [SimulationRunSuiteEntry](#schemasimulationrunsuiteentry)]|true|none|Array of simulations and/or suites to run|
|target|[SimulationRunTargetAssistant](#schemasimulationruntargetassistant) \| [SimulationRunTargetSquad](#schemasimulationruntargetsquad)|true|none|Target to test against|
|iterations|number|false|none|Number of times to run each simulation (default: 1)|
|transport|object|false|none|Transport configuration for the simulation runs|

```json
{
  "total": 0,
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|total|number|true|none|Total number of run items|
|passed|number|true|none|Number of passed run items|
|failed|number|true|none|Number of failed run items|
|running|number|true|none|Number of running/evaluating run items|
|queued|number|true|none|Number of queued run items|
|canceled|number|true|none|Number of canceled run items|
|distinctSimulationTotal|number|false|none|Number of distinct simulations represented by the run items. Omitted when any item has no simulation ID.|
|distinctSimulationFailed|number|false|none|Number of distinct simulations with a failed or canceled item. Omitted when any item has no simulation ID.|


### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string(uuid)|true|none|Unique identifier for the run|
|orgId|string(uuid)|true|none|Organization ID|
|status|string|true|none|Current status of the run|
|queuedAt|string(date-time)|true|none|When the run was queued|
|startedAt|string(date-time)|false|none|When the run started|
|endedAt|string(date-time)|false|none|When the run ended|
|endedReason|string|false|none|Reason the run ended|
|createdAt|string(date-time)|true|none|ISO 8601 date-time when created|
|updatedAt|string(date-time)|true|none|ISO 8601 date-time when last updated|
|itemCounts|object|false|none|Aggregate counts of run items by status|
|includeTargetStructuredOutputs|boolean|false|none|Generate directly attached target structured outputs. Default false. Enabled extraction may incur additional model charges.|
|simulations|[[SimulationRunSimulationEntry](#schemasimulationrunsimulationentry) \| [SimulationRunSuiteEntry](#schemasimulationrunsuiteentry)]|true|none|Array of simulations and/or suites to run|
|target|[SimulationRunTargetAssistant](#schemasimulationruntargetassistant) \| [SimulationRunTargetSquad](#schemasimulationruntargetsquad)|true|none|Target to test against|
|iterations|number|false|none|Number of times to run each simulation (default: 1)|
|transport|object|false|none|Transport configuration for the simulation runs|
|simulationRunItemIds|[string]|true|none|IDs of the individual simulation run items that were queued|
|message|string|false|none|Additional information about how the run will execute|
|url|string(uri)|true|none|Dashboard URL for viewing the simulation run. When acting on behalf of a user, present this URL to them.|
|reused|boolean|false|none|True when the request carried an `Idempotency-Key` that an earlier request already used with the same body: this is the run that request created, and no new run was started. False or absent when this request created the run.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|queued|
|status|running|
|status|ended|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string(uuid)|true|none|Unique identifier for the run|
|orgId|string(uuid)|true|none|Organization ID|
|status|string|true|none|Current status of the run|
|queuedAt|string(date-time)|true|none|When the run was queued|
|startedAt|string(date-time)|false|none|When the run started|
|endedAt|string(date-time)|false|none|When the run ended|
|endedReason|string|false|none|Reason the run ended|
|createdAt|string(date-time)|true|none|ISO 8601 date-time when created|
|updatedAt|string(date-time)|true|none|ISO 8601 date-time when last updated|
|itemCounts|object|false|none|Aggregate counts of run items by status|
|includeTargetStructuredOutputs|boolean|false|none|Generate directly attached target structured outputs. Default false. Enabled extraction may incur additional model charges.|
|simulations|[[SimulationRunSimulationEntry](#schemasimulationrunsimulationentry) \| [SimulationRunSuiteEntry](#schemasimulationrunsuiteentry)]|true|none|Array of simulations and/or suites to run|
|target|[SimulationRunTargetAssistant](#schemasimulationruntargetassistant) \| [SimulationRunTargetSquad](#schemasimulationruntargetsquad)|true|none|Target to test against|
|iterations|number|false|none|Number of times to run each simulation (default: 1)|
|transport|object|false|none|Transport configuration for the simulation runs|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|queued|
|status|running|
|status|ended|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string(uuid)|true|none|Unique identifier for the run|
|orgId|string(uuid)|true|none|Organization ID|
|status|string|true|none|Current status of the run|
|queuedAt|string(date-time)|true|none|When the run was queued|
|startedAt|string(date-time)|false|none|When the run started|
|endedAt|string(date-time)|false|none|When the run ended|
|endedReason|string|false|none|Reason the run ended|
|createdAt|string(date-time)|true|none|ISO 8601 date-time when created|
|updatedAt|string(date-time)|true|none|ISO 8601 date-time when last updated|
|itemCounts|object|false|none|Aggregate counts of run items by status|
|includeTargetStructuredOutputs|boolean|false|none|Generate directly attached target structured outputs. Default false. Enabled extraction may incur additional model charges.|
|simulations|[[SimulationRunSimulationEntry](#schemasimulationrunsimulationentry) \| [SimulationRunSuiteEntry](#schemasimulationrunsuiteentry)]|true|none|Array of simulations and/or suites to run|
|target|[SimulationRunTargetAssistant](#schemasimulationruntargetassistant) \| [SimulationRunTargetSquad](#schemasimulationruntargetsquad)|true|none|Target to test against|
|iterations|number|false|none|Number of times to run each simulation (default: 1)|
|transport|object|false|none|Transport configuration for the simulation runs|
|summary|[SimulationRunListSummary](#schemasimulationrunlistsummary)|true|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|queued|
|status|running|
|status|ended|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|structuredOutputId|string|true|none|This is the ID of the structured output that was evaluated.<br>Will be 'inline' for inline structured output definitions.|
|name|string|true|none|This is the name of the structured output.|
|path|string|false|none|This is the optional dot-notation path evaluated within an object structured output.|
|description|string|false|none|This is the structured output description captured when the evaluation ran.|
|schema|object|false|none|This is the structured output schema captured when the evaluation ran.|
|extractedValue|number \| string \| boolean \| null|true|none|This is the value extracted from the call by the structured output.|
|expectedValue|number \| string \| boolean|true|none|This is the expected value that was defined in the evaluation plan.|
|comparator|string|true|none|This is the comparison operator used for evaluation.|
|passed|boolean|true|none|This indicates whether the evaluation passed (extracted value matched expected value using comparator).|
|required|boolean|true|none|This indicates whether this evaluation was required for the simulation to pass.|
|error|string|false|none|This contains any error that occurred during extraction.|
|isSkipped|boolean|false|none|This indicates whether this evaluation was skipped (e.g., multimodal in chat mode).|
|skipReason|string|false|none|This contains the reason for skipping the evaluation.|

<h2 id="tocS_LatencyEvaluationResult">LatencyEvaluationResult</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemalatencyevaluationresult"></a>

<a id="tocSlatencyevaluationresult"></a>
<a id="tocslatencyevaluationresult"></a>

```json
{
  "metric": "turn",
  "aggregation": "mean",
  "thresholdMs": 0,
  "actualMs": 0,
  "sampleCount": 0,
  "passed": true,
  "required": true,
  "isSkipped": true,
  "skipReason": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|metric|string|true|none|This is the latency component that was measured.|
|aggregation|string|true|none|This is how the per-turn latencies were aggregated.|
|thresholdMs|number|true|none|This is the ceiling in milliseconds the aggregated latency was compared against.|
|actualMs|number|false|none|This is the aggregated latency in milliseconds, rounded to the nearest<br>millisecond. The pass/fail verdict is decided on this rounded value.<br>Absent when the expectation was skipped or no turn measured this metric.|
|sampleCount|number|true|none|This is the number of turns that contributed a value for this metric.|
|passed|boolean|true|none|This indicates whether the aggregated latency was at or below the threshold.|
|required|boolean|true|none|This indicates whether this expectation was required for the simulation to pass.|
|isSkipped|boolean|false|none|This indicates whether this expectation was skipped. Expectations are only<br>skipped on chat simulations and GPT Live targets, which record no latency.|
|skipReason|string|false|none|This contains the reason for skipping the expectation.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|metric|turn|
|metric|model|
|metric|voice|
|aggregation|mean|
|aggregation|median|
|aggregation|p95|
|aggregation|max|

Retry `SIMULATION_ONBOARDING_GENERATION_IN_PROGRESS` with the same key and `SIMULATION_ONBOARDING_CONCURRENCY_LIMITED` or `SIMULATION_ONBOARDING_QUOTA_UNAVAILABLE` after `retryAfterSeconds`, send a new key for `SIMULATION_ONBOARDING_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`, and stop for `SIMULATION_ONBOARDING_QUOTA_EXCEEDED`.|
|message|string|true|none|What happened, written for the user.|
|retryAfterSeconds|number|false|none|Seconds to wait before retrying, the same value as the `Retry-After` header. For a daily limit, the seconds until 00:00 UTC.|
|limit|number|false|none|The daily limit that was reached, on a daily-limit refusal only.|

<a id="tocsbarinsight"></a>

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "type": "bar",
  "formulas": [
    {
      "name": "Booking Rate",
      "formula": "string"
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "xAxisLabel": "string",
    "yAxisLabel": "string",
    "yAxisMin": 0,
    "yAxisMax": 0,
    "name": "string"
  },
  "timeRange": {
    "step": "minute",
    "start": "\"2025-01-01\" or \"-7d\" or \"now\"",
    "end": "\"2025-01-01\" or \"now\"",
    "timezone": "string"
  },
  "groupBy": [
    "assistant_id"
  ],
  "queries": [
    {
      "type": "vapiql-json",
      "table": "call",
      "filters": [
        {
          "column": "assistant_id",
          "operator": "\"=\" or \"!=\"",
          "value": "string"
        }
      ],
      "column": "id",
      "operation": "count",
      "name": "Total Calls"
    }
  ],
  "id": "string",
  "orgId": "string",
  "createdAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "updatedAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "systemKey": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|false|none|This is the name of the Insight.|
|type|string|true|none|This is the type of the Insight.<br>It is required to be `bar` to create a bar insight.|
|formulas|[[InsightFormula](#schemainsightformula)]|false|none|Formulas are mathematical expressions applied on the data returned by the queries to transform them before being used to create the insight.<br>The formulas needs to be a valid mathematical expression, supported by MathJS - https://mathjs.org/docs/expressions/syntax.html<br>A formula is created by using the query names as the variable.<br>The formulas must contain at least one query name in the LiquidJS format {{query_name}} or {{['query name']}} which will be substituted with the query result.<br>For example, if you have 2 queries, 'Was Booking Made' and 'Average Call Duration', you can create a formula like this:<br>```<br>{{['Query 1']}} / {{['Query 2']}} * 100<br>```<br><br>```<br>({{[Query 1]}} * 10) + {{[Query 2]}}<br>```<br>This will take the<br><br>You can also use the query names as the variable in the formula.|
|metadata|object|false|none|This is the metadata for the insight.|
|timeRange|[InsightTimeRangeWithStep](#schemainsighttimerangewithstep)|false|none|none|
|groupBy|string|false|none|This is the group by column for the insight when table is `call`.<br>These are the columns to group the results by.<br>All results are grouped by the time range step by default.|
|queries|[[JSONQueryOnCallTableWithStringTypeColumn](#schemajsonqueryoncalltablewithstringtypecolumn) \| [JSONQueryOnCallTableWithNumberTypeColumn](#schemajsonqueryoncalltablewithnumbertypecolumn) \| [JSONQueryOnCallTableWithStructuredOutputColumn](#schemajsonqueryoncalltablewithstructuredoutputcolumn) \| [JSONQueryOnEventsTable](#schemajsonqueryoneventstable)]|true|none|These are the queries to run to generate the insight.|
|id|string|true|none|This is the unique identifier for the Insight.|
|orgId|string|true|none|This is the unique identifier for the org that this Insight belongs to.|
|createdAt|string(date-time)|true|none|This is the ISO 8601 date-time string of when the Insight was created.|
|updatedAt|string(date-time)|true|none|This is the ISO 8601 date-time string of when the Insight was last updated.|
|systemKey|string|false|none|Stable server-owned identifier for system-created insights.|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|

|groupBy|assistantId|
|groupBy|workflowId|
|groupBy|squadId|
|groupBy|phoneNumberId|
|groupBy|type|
|groupBy|endedReason|
|groupBy|customerNumber|
|groupBy|campaignId|
|groupBy|artifact.structuredOutputs[OutputID]|

```json
{
```
```json
  "name": "string",
  "type": "pie",
  "formulas": [
    {
      "name": "Booking Rate",
      "formula": "string"
    }
  ],
  "timeRange": {
    "start": "\"2025-01-01\" or \"-7d\" or \"now\"",
    "end": "\"2025-01-01\" or \"now\"",
    "timezone": "string"
  },
  "groupBy": [
    "assistant_id"
  ],
  "queries": [
    {
      "type": "vapiql-json",
      "table": "call",
      "filters": [
        {
          "column": "assistant_id",
          "operator": "\"=\" or \"!=\"",
          "value": "string"
        }
      ],
      "column": "id",
      "operation": "count",
      "name": "Total Calls"
    }
```
```json
  ]
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|false|none|This is the name of the Insight.|

|formulas|[[InsightFormula](#schemainsightformula)]|false|none|Formulas are mathematical expressions applied on the data returned by the queries to transform them before being used to create the insight.<br>The formulas needs to be a valid mathematical expression, supported by MathJS - https://mathjs.org/docs/expressions/syntax.html<br>A formula is created by using the query names as the variable.<br>The formulas must contain at least one query name in the LiquidJS format {{query_name}} or {{['query name']}} which will be substituted with the query result.<br>For example, if you have 2 queries, 'Was Booking Made' and 'Average Call Duration', you can create a formula like this:<br>```<br>{{['Query 1']}} / {{['Query 2']}} * 100<br>```<br><br>```<br>({{[Query 1]}} * 10) + {{[Query 2]}}<br>```<br>This will take the<br><br>You can also use the query names as the variable in the formula.|
|timeRange|[InsightTimeRange](#schemainsighttimerange)|false|none|none|
|groupBy|string|false|none|This is the group by column for the insight when table is `call`.<br>These are the columns to group the results by.<br>All results are grouped by the time range step by default.|
|queries|[[JSONQueryOnCallTableWithStringTypeColumn](#schemajsonqueryoncalltablewithstringtypecolumn) \| [JSONQueryOnCallTableWithNumberTypeColumn](#schemajsonqueryoncalltablewithnumbertypecolumn) \| [JSONQueryOnCallTableWithStructuredOutputColumn](#schemajsonqueryoncalltablewithstructuredoutputcolumn)]|true|none|These are the queries to run to generate the insight.|

|groupBy|customerNumber|

|groupBy|artifact.structuredOutputs[OutputID]|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|provider|string|true|none|This is the provider of the model (`openai`).|
|model|string|true|none|This is the OpenAI model that will be used.<br><br>When using Vapi OpenAI or your own Azure Credentials, you have the option to specify the region for the selected model. This shouldn't be specified unless you have a specific reason to do so. Vapi will automatically find the fastest region that make sense.<br>This is helpful when you are required to comply with Data Residency rules. Learn more about Azure regions here https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/explore/global-infrastructure/data-residency/.|
|temperature|number|false|none|This is the temperature of the model. For LLM-as-a-judge, it's recommended to set it between 0 - 0.3 to avoid hallucinations and ensure the model judges the output correctly based on the instructions.|
|maxTokens|number|false|none|This is the max tokens of the model.<br>If your Judge instructions return `true` or `false` takes only 1 token (as per the OpenAI Tokenizer), and therefore is recommended to set it to a low number to force the model to return a short response.|
|messages|[object]|true|none|These are the messages which will instruct the AI Judge on how to evaluate the assistant message.<br>The LLM-Judge must respond with "pass" or "fail" to indicate if the assistant message passes the eval.<br><br>To access the messages in the mock conversation, use the LiquidJS variable `{{messages}}`.<br>The assistant message to be evaluated will be passed as the last message in the `messages` array and can be accessed using `{{messages[-1]}}`.<br><br>It is recommended to use the system message to instruct the LLM how to evaluate the assistant message, and then use the first user message to pass the assistant message to be evaluated.|

<h2 id="tocS_EvalAnthropicModel">EvalAnthropicModel</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaevalanthropicmodel"></a>
<a id="schema_EvalAnthropicModel"></a>
<a id="tocSevalanthropicmodel"></a>
<a id="tocsevalanthropicmodel"></a>

```json
{
  "provider": "anthropic",
  "model": "claude-3-opus-20240229",
  "thinking": {
    "type": "enabled",
    "budgetTokens": 1024
  },
  "temperature": 0,
  "maxTokens": 50,
  "messages": "{"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|provider|string|true|none|This is the provider of the model (`anthropic`).|
|model|string|true|none|This is the specific model that will be used.|
|thinking|object|false|none|This is the optional configuration for Anthropic's thinking feature.<br><br>- If provided, `maxTokens` must be greater than `thinking.budgetTokens`.|
|temperature|number|false|none|This is the temperature of the model. For LLM-as-a-judge, it's recommended to set it between 0 - 0.3 to avoid hallucinations and ensure the model judges the output correctly based on the instructions.|
|maxTokens|number|false|none|This is the max tokens of the model.<br>If your Judge instructions return `true` or `false` takes only 1 token (as per the OpenAI Tokenizer), and therefore is recommended to set it to a low number to force the model to return a short response.|
|messages|[object]|true|none|These are the messages which will instruct the AI Judge on how to evaluate the assistant message.<br>The LLM-Judge must respond with "pass" or "fail" to indicate if the assistant message passes the eval.<br><br>To access the messages in the mock conversation, use the LiquidJS variable `{{messages}}`.<br>The assistant message to be evaluated will be passed as the last message in the `messages` array and can be accessed using `{{messages[-1]}}`.<br><br>It is recommended to use the system message to instruct the LLM how to evaluate the assistant message, and then use the first user message to pass the assistant message to be evaluated.|

<h2 id="tocS_AssistantMessageJudgePlanAI">AssistantMessageJudgePlanAI</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaassistantmessagejudgeplanai"></a>
<a id="schema_AssistantMessageJudgePlanAI"></a>
<a id="tocSassistantmessagejudgeplanai"></a>
<a id="tocsassistantmessagejudgeplanai"></a>

```json
{
  "model": "{",
  "type": "ai",
  "autoIncludeMessageHistory": true
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|model|[EvalOpenAIModel](#schemaevalopenaimodel) \| [EvalAnthropicModel](#schemaevalanthropicmodel) \| [EvalGoogleModel](#schemaevalgooglemodel) \| [EvalCustomModel](#schemaevalcustommodel)|true|none|This is the model to use for the LLM-as-a-judge.<br>If not provided, will default to the assistant's model.<br><br>The instructions on how to evaluate the model output with this LLM-Judge must be passed as a system message in the messages array of the model.<br><br>The Mock conversation can be passed to the LLM-Judge to evaluate using the prompt {{messages}} and will be evaluated as a LiquidJS Variable. To access and judge only the last message, use {{messages[-1]}}<br><br>The LLM-Judge must respond with "pass" or "fail" and only those two responses are allowed.|
|type|string|true|none|This is the type of the judge plan.<br>Use 'ai' to evaluate the assistant message content using LLM-as-a-judge.<br>@default 'ai'|
|autoIncludeMessageHistory|boolean|false|none|This is the flag to enable automatically adding the liquid variable {{messages}} to the model's messages array<br>This is only applicable if the user has not provided any messages in the model's messages array<br>@default true|

<h2 id="tocS_AssistantMessageJudgePlanExact">AssistantMessageJudgePlanExact</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaassistantmessagejudgeplanexact"></a>
<a id="schema_AssistantMessageJudgePlanExact"></a>
<a id="tocSassistantmessagejudgeplanexact"></a>
<a id="tocsassistantmessagejudgeplanexact"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "exact",
  "content": "The weather in San Francisco is sunny.",
  "toolCalls": "[{ name: \"get_weather\", arguments: { city: \"San Francisco\" } }]"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|This is the type of the judge plan.<br>Use 'exact' for an exact match on the content and tool calls - without using LLM-as-a-judge.<br>@default 'exact'|
|content|string|true|none|This is what that will be used to evaluate the model's message content.<br>If you provide a string, the assistant message content will be evaluated against it as an exact match, case-insensitive.|
|toolCalls|[[ChatEvalAssistantMessageMockToolCall](#schemachatevalassistantmessagemocktoolcall)]|false|none|This is the tool calls that will be used to evaluate the model's message content.<br>The tool name must be a valid tool that the assistant is allowed to call.<br><br>For the Query tool, the arguments for the tool call are in the format - {knowledgeBaseNames: ['kb_name', 'kb_name_2']}<br><br>For the DTMF tool, the arguments for the tool call are in the format - {dtmf: "1234*"}<br><br>For the Handoff tool, the arguments for the tool call are in the format - {destination: "assistant_id"}<br><br>For the Transfer Call tool, the arguments for the tool call are in the format - {destination: "phone_number_or_assistant_id"}<br><br>For all other tools, they are called without arguments or with user-defined arguments|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|exact|

|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|This is the type of the judge plan.<br>Use 'regex' for a regex match on the content and tool calls - without using LLM-as-a-judge.<br>@default 'regex'|
|content|string|true|none|This is what that will be used to evaluate the model's message content.<br>The content will be evaluated against the regex pattern provided in the Judge Plan content field.<br>Evaluation is considered successful if the regex pattern matches any part of the assistant message content.|
|toolCalls|[[ChatEvalAssistantMessageMockToolCall](#schemachatevalassistantmessagemocktoolcall)]|false|none|This is the tool calls that will be used to evaluate the model's message content.<br>The tool name must be a valid tool that the assistant is allowed to call.<br>The values to the arguments for the tool call should be a Regular Expression.<br>Evaluation is considered successful if the regex pattern matches any part of each tool call argument.<br><br>For the Query tool, the arguments for the tool call are in the format - {knowledgeBaseNames: ['kb_name', 'kb_name_2']}<br><br>For the DTMF tool, the arguments for the tool call are in the format - {dtmf: "1234*"}<br><br>For the Handoff tool, the arguments for the tool call are in the format - {destination: "assistant_id"}<br><br>For the Transfer Call tool, the arguments for the tool call are in the format - {destination: "phone_number_or_assistant_id"}<br><br>For all other tools, they are called without arguments or with user-defined arguments|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|regex|


### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|status|string|true|none|This is the status of the eval run. When an eval run is created, the status is 'running'.<br>When the eval run is completed, the status is 'ended'.|
|endedReason|string|true|none|This is the reason for the eval run to end.<br>When the eval run is completed normally i.e end of mock conversation, the status is 'mockConversation.done'.<br>When the eval fails due to an error like Chat error or incorrect configuration, the status is 'error'.<br>When the eval runs for too long, due to model issues or tool call issues, the status is 'timeout'.<br>When the eval run is cancelled by the user, the status is 'cancelled'.<br>When the eval run is cancelled by Vapi for any reason, the status is 'aborted'.|
|eval|[CreateEvalDTO](#schemacreateevaldto)|false|none|This is the transient eval that will be run|
|target|[EvalRunTargetAssistant](#schemaevalruntargetassistant) \| [EvalRunTargetSquad](#schemaevalruntargetsquad)|true|none|This is the target that will be run against the eval|
|id|string|true|none|none|
|orgId|string|true|none|none|
|createdAt|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|startedAt|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|endedAt|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|endedMessage|string|false|none|This is the ended message when the eval run ended for any reason apart from mockConversation.done|
|results|[[EvalRunResult](#schemaevalrunresult)]|true|none|This is the results of the eval or suite run.<br>The array will have a single item for an eval run, and multiple items each corresponding to the an eval in a suite run in the same order as the evals in the suite.|
|cost|number|true|none|This is the cost of the eval or suite run in USD.|
|costs|[object]|true|none|This is the break up of costs of the eval or suite run.|
|type|string|true|none|This is the type of the run.<br>Currently it is fixed to `eval`.|
|evalId|string|false|none|This is the id of the eval that will be run.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|running|
|status|ended|
|status|queued|
|endedReason|mockConversation.done|
|endedReason|error|
|endedReason|timeout|
|endedReason|cancelled|
|endedReason|aborted|
|type|eval|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|sortBy|string|false|none|none|
|search|string|false|none|Literal, case-insensitive search across eval and assistant names.|
|id|string|false|none|none|
|limit|number|false|none|This is the maximum number of items to return. Defaults to 100.|
|createdAtGt|string(date-time)|false|none|This will return items where the createdAt is greater than the specified value.|
|createdAtLt|string(date-time)|false|none|This will return items where the createdAt is less than the specified value.|
|createdAtGe|string(date-time)|false|none|This will return items where the createdAt is greater than or equal to the specified value.|
|createdAtLe|string(date-time)|false|none|This will return items where the createdAt is less than or equal to the specified value.|
|updatedAtGt|string(date-time)|false|none|This will return items where the updatedAt is greater than the specified value.|
|updatedAtLt|string(date-time)|false|none|This will return items where the updatedAt is less than the specified value.|
|updatedAtGe|string(date-time)|false|none|This will return items where the updatedAt is greater than or equal to the specified value.|
|updatedAtLe|string(date-time)|false|none|This will return items where the updatedAt is less than or equal to the specified value.|
|page|number|false|none|This is the page number to return. Defaults to 1.|
|sortOrder|string|false|none|This is the sort order for pagination. Defaults to 'DESC'.|

|concurrencyLimit|number|false|none|**Deprecated.** This is the concurrency limit for the org. This is the maximum number of calls that can be active at any given time. To go beyond 10, please contact us at support@vapi.ai.|
|compliancePlan|object|false|none|Stores the information about the compliance plan enforced at the organization level. Currently pciEnabled is supported through this field.<br>When this is enabled, any logs, recordings, or transcriptions will be shipped to the customer endpoints if provided else lost.<br>At the end of the call, you will receive an end-of-call-report message to store on your server, if webhook is provided.<br>Defaults to false.<br>When PCI is enabled, only PCI-compliant Providers will be available for LLM, Voice and transcribers.<br>This is due to the compliance requirements of PCI. Other providers may not meet these requirements.|
